proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge on the pendant within 500 ms, collect Calendar/Mail and Mac state in 2–5 s, wait up to 8 s for the browser bridge; if it is offline, explicitly mark that source unavailable and finish rather than blocking. Write the packet and enqueue audio within 10 s.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.04 per invocation depending on browser text and synthesis; the dominant costs are background model input from extracted snippets and TTS/audio bytes, not the realtime acknowledgement.
proposals.security_concerns: Keep browser content local to the Mac bridge where possible; send only redacted excerpts and hashes to relay. Never submit or mutate browser forms. Include source URL/title, timestamps, and confidence for every claim. Store the packet with a short TTL and provide a pendant double-press or dashboard delete action. Require explicit confirmation before sharing it externally; creating the local artifact and audio is reversible/deletable.
missing: Implementation behind the newly granted mac_read_sources tool (currently schema-only)

Implementation behind mac_readonly_inspect (currently schema-only); accessibility and Screen Recording are still unavailable, so workspace inspection must use permitted AppleScript/app metadata until the owner grants TCC
A relay orchestration endpoint that fans out bounded Mac reads plus authenticated browser extraction and returns a redacted, cited packet
Browser bridge reconnect/timeout semantics (currently browser online=false with 5 pending commands)
A durable, expiring audio-queue write path and packet deletion/receipt linkage

proposals.user_asks: "Is anything inconsistent?" Have the system continuously reconcile my current Calendar, unread Mail, already-open authenticated browser tabs, and the Mac files or notes relevant to my active project. Tell me only when two sources disagree or a deadline/status has silently changed, explain the evidence side by side, and prepare a local correction plan without changing or sending anything.
proposals.why_useful: Today each surface can report its own facts, but none can notice that they conflict: a rescheduled meeting still has the old video link in Mail, a browser portal shows a different deadline than a local project note, or a task is marked done in one place and overdue in another. The owner gets an actionable discrepancy rather than a flood of unchanged updates. This requires the pendant/relay for low-friction alerts, the browser's private session, Mac source access, and a shared evidence engine; no single node can perform it privately and continuously.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model or deterministic field comparison for polling, entity resolution, and change detection; use the realtime model only to announce a confirmed high-value discrepancy and answer follow-up questions. Escalate ambiguous identity matches to a slower judgement pass rather than spending realtime tokens.
proposals.latency_budget: Evaluate on a configurable cadence (for example every 15 minutes during an attention window), acknowledge an alert in under 1 second after detection, and produce cited side-by-side evidence within 5 seconds. Quiet hours and a per-project cooldown are mandatory.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.005–$0.03 per scan depending on extracted browser text; most scans should be deterministic and use no model. Cost is dominated by background entity resolution for genuinely changed records and optional TTS, not continuous realtime conversation.
proposals.security_concerns: Keep raw Mail, browser pages, and local notes on the Mac whenever possible; send the relay only normalized fields, redacted snippets, hashes, and provenance. Treat webpage text as untrusted data, never follow instructions embedded in it, and never auto-correct or submit. The owner must choose sources/projects, retention TTL, quiet hours, and whether audio may mention sensitive titles. Every alert needs citations, confidence, observedAt, and a dismiss/snooze/delete control.
missing: A durable cross-source observation store with canonical entities, field-level provenance, freshness, and suppression/cooldown state
A browser read-only extraction/watch adapter that can reattach to selected authenticated tabs and report semantic field changes
Bounded Mac adapters for Calendar, Mail, Notes/files, and project scope with redaction before relay upload
A discrepancy classifier that distinguishes true contradictions from expected formatting/version differences and resists prompt injection
A relay scheduler and pendant notification queue supporting quiet hours, deduplication, offline delivery, and explicit partial-source status
A review UI that shows side-by-side evidence and generates a reversible local correction plan without executing it

proposals.user_asks: Pause what you’re doing on my Mac and continue it later—even if I close the laptop; when I say resume, tell me what changed and pick up without repeating work.
proposals.why_useful: Today an asynchronous Mac job can report a receipt, but there is no durable, cross-surface pause/resume contract that captures the desktop/browser state, detects stale context, and prevents duplicate mutations. This lets the pendant act as a reliable control surface for interrupted work rather than merely starting or checking jobs.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to interpret the short pause/resume utterance and speak the result; use a cheaper background model to serialize the task capsule, compare state on resume, and summarize diffs. No model should infer success without a Mac receipt.
proposals.latency_budget: A pause acknowledgement under 2 seconds; capsule write under 5 seconds. Resume should return a stale-state check and spoken summary within 10 seconds, then execute only the remaining bounded actions.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually 1 short realtime turn plus 1–2 cheap background comparisons; roughly $0.01–$0.05 per pause/resume depending on browser extraction and context size. The dominant cost is re-reading changed private pages, not the capsule itself.
proposals.security_concerns: Capsules must contain references and hashes by default, not page bodies or email contents; encrypt at rest, apply per-item TTL, and redact secrets. Resuming a high-impact or irreversible action must preserve the owner’s existing maximum-access policy but still emit an explicit before/after receipt. If browser extension is offline, do not claim a resume; queue it and report pending.
missing: A durable task-capsule schema with step IDs, idempotency keys, precondition snapshots, expiry, and remaining actions
Mac read-only inspection implementation (the granted mac_readonly_inspect schema currently has no implementation) for foreground app, running apps, browser tabs, and directory state
Relay persistence and a resume endpoint that reconciles Mac job receipts with the capsule
Browser bridge support for reattaching the original tab/session and returning typed state diffs
A dashboard view for paused, stale, blocked, and completed capsules

proposals.user_asks: Save this moment for me: keep the page I’m on, the relevant draft or selection, and why I cared, then let me reopen the same private workspace from the pendant later; erase it automatically after I’m done.
proposals.why_useful: The owner can start jobs and create notes, but cannot make a bounded, expiring bookmark of the exact cross-surface moment they are in. This would preserve the working set—not just a URL—across a logged-in browser tab, the Mac’s current document/draft, and a spoken intent, while avoiding a permanent personal-data archive.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime handles only the short capture/restore utterance. A cheaper background model extracts a one-sentence intent and ranks relevant fields; deterministic adapters collect URLs, tab IDs, app/document identifiers, selection hashes, and draft metadata. Never send full page or document bodies to the model unless explicitly requested.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge capture in under 2 seconds and finish the local/browser snapshot within 8 seconds. Restore should show a compact preview within 5 seconds, then open only after the owner says restore/open.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.03 per capture/restore for a small intent extraction and optional diff summary; storage and browser IPC dominate, not inference.
proposals.security_concerns: This may contain private URLs, drafts, clipboard selections, and account context. Store an encrypted capsule with field-level redaction, device-bound keys, explicit per-capsule TTL, and a visible list of captured fields. Do not capture passwords, tokens, full clipboard contents, or page bodies by default. Restoration must not submit, send, or mutate anything; if the original tab/session is gone, report that precisely and offer only the safe artifacts.
missing: A new expiring workspace-capsule primitive, distinct from a job: field manifest, encrypted payload, provenance, TTL, and one-time restore semantics
A foreground/document/selection adapter on Mac that works without relying on arbitrary shell and reports unavailable fields honestly
Browser bridge support for exporting and reattaching a specific private tab’s safe state (URL, tab ID, semantic anchors, and redacted draft metadata)
Pendant-side capture and restore affordances (button/voice confirmation and a short spoken capsule name)
A dashboard showing exactly which fields were captured, remaining TTL, and a destructive erase control

proposals.user_asks: Before you use my private Mac or logged-in browser, tell me exactly what information would leave the device, let me remove any fields by voice, and then do the task with the redacted version.
proposals.why_useful: The owner has maximum-access automation but no usable, per-request data-egress preview. This gives them a practical privacy control that is narrower than blocking automation: they can inspect and edit the context packet before the relay/model/browser receives it, including fields the system would otherwise silently infer from tabs, mail, calendar, or documents.
proposals.model_tier: A deterministic local classifier builds the candidate field manifest; a cheap background model labels fields and explains them. Realtime is used only for the owner’s brief spoken edits and confirmation of the final manifest. Sensitive values remain local unless included in the final approved packet.
proposals.latency_budget: Generate the manifest in 2–5 seconds for a normal task, speak a 10-second summary, and apply voice redactions immediately. The actual task starts only after the edited manifest is available; no extra model turn is needed for unchanged fields.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.002–$0.02 per request; most work is local field extraction and serialization. Cost rises only when the owner asks for a natural-language explanation of many fields.
proposals.security_concerns: The preview itself is sensitive and must be rendered locally when possible; store only a hash and policy decision, not the unredacted manifest. Default to URLs/titles/selected snippets rather than bodies, mask credentials and tokens unconditionally, and record exactly which fields were permitted. This is an informational control, not a promise that a third-party page cannot observe its own browser interaction.
missing: A context-egress manifest protocol with field IDs, source, sensitivity, byte count, destination, TTL, and redaction state
Local extraction hooks for Mac documents, Calendar/Mail reads, and authenticated browser tabs
A relay ingress that accepts only the approved manifest and rejects undeclared fields
Pendant UI/voice grammar for 'remove the email body', 'allow this tab title', and 'show me the rest'
Dashboard audit view linking approved fields to job and browser receipts

proposals.user_asks: Keep my pendant conversation clear when the LTE-M connection gets crowded, and return to full-quality 24 kHz audio automatically when it recovers.
proposals.why_useful: Today the measured duplex link drops about 7.8 seconds of uplink while the agent speaks. This would preserve the owner's words first, degrade gracefully instead of going silent, and recover superwideband without making them manage audio settings.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime model only interprets the QoS profile when needed; deterministic firmware/relay rules handle adaptation. Use a cheaper background model for post-call quality summaries, never for the live control loop.
proposals.latency_budget: QoS telemetry every 2 seconds; profile changes applied within one 60 ms frame plus one relay scheduling interval (<300 ms target). No extra conversational model turn.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible inference cost during calls; roughly a few hundred bytes of telemetry per minute. Optional post-call summary costs a small background-model invocation and is not required.
proposals.security_concerns: Telemetry contains timing and quality counters, not microphone content or transcripts. Keep raw audio unchanged in the existing encrypted WebSocket; dashboard should redact session identifiers. Never store audio merely to diagnose loss.
missing: Implement the requested pendant duplex_audio_congestion_guard skill
Relay-side adaptive profile scheduler that reserves uplink capacity and changes downlink Opus bitrate/frame profile
A negotiated Opus profile contract covering 24 kHz/60 ms and a low-bandwidth fallback with hysteresis
Dashboard quality timeline and a completion receipt proving when quality changed and recovered
End-to-end test using the measured half-duplex contention case
built_from: GET /health and live relay capabilities for durable audio
POST /pipeline/audio for the existing audio pipeline
POST /execute and the Mac bridge receipt/job system for a spoken completion receipt
Existing firmware nRF9160 Opus path and cloud-relay/opusTranscode.js

proposals.user_asks: When I interrupt you or the connection drops during a spoken answer, preserve the unfinished turn and let me resume it later from the pendant or Mac without repeating myself.
proposals.why_useful: Today an interruption can leave the owner with a clipped answer and no reliable way to recover the missing context. This would make conversation resilient: the system remembers the exact assistant sequence and the owner's interruption point, then offers a concise continuation rather than replaying or guessing.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic sequence tracking and a cheaper background model for reconstruction. Use the realtime model only when the owner explicitly asks for a natural-language continuation or clarification.
proposals.latency_budget: Detect interruption within one audio frame (<60 ms), persist a resumable turn within 1 second, and make a resume available immediately after reconnect. Reconstruction can take up to 2 seconds outside the live turn.
proposals.cost_estimate: Minimal storage and telemetry per interrupted turn. One small background-model call only when audio is genuinely missing and a textual reconstruction is needed; do not retranscribe or regenerate intact audio.
proposals.security_concerns: Persist only encrypted transcript fragments, sequence ranges, and redacted metadata with a short retention period. Never resume a turn aloud automatically if the pendant has been idle in a public setting; require a button press or explicit phrase. Mac receipts must identify whether content was original or reconstructed.
missing: A cross-surface resumable-turn protocol with globally unique turn and audio sequence IDs
Pendant local marker for button/voice interruption and last-heard playback sequence
Relay durable checkpointing that stores encrypted turn metadata and bounded missing ranges
Mac planner endpoint that renders a continuation receipt and lets the owner choose resume, summarize, or discard
A deterministic reconciliation test for duplicate packets, reconnects, and partial TTS delivery
built_from: Existing pendant WebSocket audio stream and Opus sequence handling
Existing durable audio capability in the relay
Existing Mac job/receipt system and POST /execute handoff
Existing pipeline event and audio routes

proposals.user_asks: When I start talking over the pendant's reply, stop or duck it immediately, understand my interruption as a correction or new request, and continue with the right response without making me repeat myself.
proposals.why_useful: Today duplex speech can make the owner talk over playback, lose words, or wait through a response that is no longer relevant. This would make the pendant feel conversational rather than like a walkie-talkie: the owner's intent wins within one speech turn, while the interrupted reply remains available for recovery if needed.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for the live barge-in decision and turn boundary; a cheaper background model may summarize abandoned replies for diagnostics, but must not sit in the hot path.
proposals.latency_budget: Local playback duck/pause within 100 ms of a reliable voice-onset signal; relay turn arbitration within 300 ms; resumed answer should begin within 1.5 s after the owner's utterance ends.
proposals.cost_estimate: Small incremental realtime cost because interruption detection and turn arbitration reuse the active call; roughly one extra short event and possibly a truncated response per interruption. The dominant cost remains audio streaming, not a new model invocation.
proposals.security_concerns: The pendant must detect voice onset locally and send only control markers until the owner continues speaking; do not open a microphone on the Mac. An interrupted response may contain private content, so retain it only in the existing call receipt policy and expose a local delete control. Never interpret playback leakage as owner speech without confidence and hysteresis.
missing: A local pendant voice-activity/onset detector with echo-awareness against its own speaker output
A duplex turn-control protocol carrying interrupt, duck, resume, and abandon events with sequence numbers
Relay support for cancelling or checkpointing an in-flight realtime response and preventing stale audio packets from playing
Mac TTS/playback cancellation that can stop an audio render without affecting microphone state
A per-call interruption receipt and recovery state machine, including a fallback when onset confidence is low
built_from: The pendant's existing Opus uplink/downlink path
The relay's existing realtime audio session and Mac bridge handoff

proposals.user_asks: “Do this when I’m free”: stage the browser/Mac work now, wait for a real interruption-safe gap, then carry it out and tell me on the pendant exactly what happened; let me cancel it with one button press.
proposals.why_useful: Long tasks would stop competing with meetings and active work. The pendant supplies the owner’s intent and cancellation; relay keeps the request alive; Calendar/Mail and Mac foreground state identify a safe gap; the browser bridge performs logged-in steps; receipts return to the pendant. This is more useful than either an immediate automation or a generic overnight job.
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheap background planner to decompose and poll the queued task; use realtime only for the initial voice exchange, spoken status, and cancellation. Use a stronger planner only when the browser task is ambiguous.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge and stage within 2 seconds. Gap evaluation every 2–5 minutes (or on Calendar/foreground events); start within 30 seconds of a qualifying gap. Pendant cancellation should take under 1 second. No microphone needs to remain open.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.002–$0.02 per request depending on decomposition; polling and gap checks should be deterministic or use a cheap model. Browser extraction and receipts dominate compute, not voice.
proposals.security_concerns: Private calendar/mail snippets and authenticated page data leave the Mac only as compact task context and cited results. Store the queued plan encrypted with a TTL and bind browser work to a named tab/session. Do not submit irreversible browser actions unless the owner explicitly included submission; always retain before/after receipts. A physical pendant cancel must win over queued execution.
missing: A durable deferred-job state machine with a next-eligible-time and cancellation token, distinct from the existing immediate jobs queue

A Mac context event/periodic sampler that reports Calendar busy/free, foreground app, idle/active state, and a freshness timestamp without Accessibility (AppleScript can cover Calendar/foreground where possible)
Browser bridge online/reconnect and a queue consumer that can resume a named authenticated tab after a dropped link
Pendant firmware/server protocol for one-button cancel and concise queued/running/completed/error tones
A dashboard view for staged jobs, eligibility reason, TTL, and receipts

proposals.user_asks: “I’m leaving the Mac—package this exactly so I can resume it from the pendant later.” Preserve the current Mac app/document state, authenticated browser tabs, unsent drafts, evidence, and next safe step; let me ask the pendant what is waiting and resume or abandon it when I return.
proposals.why_useful: Today a task is split across a browser session, Mac files/apps, and conversation history; walking away loses the working set or forces the owner to reconstruct it. A resumable handoff would make the pendant a true continuation of the Mac rather than a separate voice endpoint. It is specifically a state-preservation and restoration capability, not a generic background job or page watch.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to summarize and validate the handoff capsule. Use realtime only when the owner asks the pendant for status or gives resume/abandon commands. Use a stronger model only to resolve conflicting state during restoration.
proposals.latency_budget: Create a capsule in under 5 seconds after the owner says to leave. Pendant status should answer in under 2 seconds. Restore should begin within 10 seconds of returning the Mac, with a clear partial-restore report.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.003–$0.02 per handoff, dominated by optional document/browser summarization. Deterministic file manifests, app identifiers, tab metadata, and action receipts should avoid model calls.
proposals.security_concerns: Capsules may contain private file paths, authenticated tab identifiers, drafts, and snippets. Encrypt them, keep the default retention short, bind browser data to the original session, exclude passwords/tokens and full page bodies unless explicitly requested, and provide a physical pendant abandon/delete command. Restoration must never silently send, submit, or delete anything.
missing: A cross-surface handoff-capsule schema with typed state, provenance, sensitivity labels, expiry, and a resumable step pointer
Mac snapshot/restore adapters for open documents, app context, unsaved draft locations, and the active project without requiring Accessibility for the basic tier
Browser extension export/import of tab/session identity and staged form state without exporting credentials
Relay storage and synchronization for encrypted capsules plus pendant-sized status summaries
A restoration reconciler that detects changed files/tabs and presents conflicts instead of replaying stale actions
A user-facing dashboard and pendant commands for list, resume, fork, abandon, and securely erase

proposals.user_asks: “Before you use my Mac or logged-in browser, show me exactly what private data will leave each device, what will stay local, and let me say ‘redact that’ or ‘local only.’ Then proceed with the least-data version and give me a receipt afterward.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently has maximum-control automation but no intelligible, per-task data boundary. This would let them use powerful cross-device actions without needing to understand prompts, tokens, browser sessions, or relay internals. It is a live privacy contract spanning the pendant, Mac, browser, and relay—not merely an execution confirmation.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic typed accounting for paths, snippets, tab origins, and payload sizes. Use a cheap model to phrase the summary for speech; realtime is only needed for the owner’s short redact/local-only replies.
proposals.latency_budget: Generate the data-flow preview in under 2 seconds for ordinary tasks. Apply redaction before any network submission. Final receipt should be available within 3 seconds of task completion.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually below $0.005 per task because accounting is deterministic; model cost is only the short spoken explanation. Storage cost is small for hashed receipts and policy decisions.
proposals.security_concerns: The preview itself must not reveal the sensitive data it is describing. Use category labels, hashes, lengths, and destination names by default, with optional local-only reveal. Enforce the selected policy at every handoff, not just at planning time; fail closed if a new field appears. Keep the policy decision and receipt tamper-evident but avoid retaining raw content.
missing: A typed end-to-end data-flow ledger attached to every plan, browser command, Mac action, and relay message
A preflight transformation layer that can remove fields, replace values with local summaries, or force a computation to remain on the Mac
A small pendant interaction protocol for redact, local-only, allow-once, and revoke-current-task
Browser and Mac adapters that report actual outbound fields rather than only intended actions
Tamper-evident receipts showing destinations, categories, byte counts, and policy decisions
A dashboard view that lets the owner inspect and revoke standing data policies

proposals.user_asks: “If that multi-step task partly failed, figure out exactly what changed, what did not, and repair only the missing pieces—without repeating anything that already happened.”
proposals.why_useful: Cross-surface work can succeed in one place and fail in another: a file may be created while a browser update times out, or a draft may be staged while its evidence fetch fails. Today the owner must manually inspect every surface and risks duplicate actions. A bounded reconciliation mode would make failures recoverable rather than opaque.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic receipt/state comparison first; use a cheap background model to classify discrepancies and generate a repair plan. Realtime is only for announcing the failure and accepting “repair,” “leave it,” or “discard.”
proposals.latency_budget: Report partial failure within 3 seconds of detection. Produce a repair plan within 10 seconds for ordinary jobs; execute only the missing idempotent steps after the owner’s command.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low: receipts and hashes dominate, with roughly $0.002–$0.01 for discrepancy classification. Avoid re-running expensive browser extraction when prior evidence remains valid.
proposals.security_concerns: Never infer success from a timeout. Preserve before/after evidence, use idempotency keys, and treat unknown outcomes as requiring reconciliation. Repair plans must exclude irreversible steps unless explicitly reissued. Keep sensitive evidence local or hashed in relay receipts.
missing: A cross-surface transaction journal with per-step preconditions, postconditions, idempotency keys, and unknown-outcome status
State probes for Mac files/apps and browser pages that can verify postconditions without replaying actions
A reconciliation planner that computes the minimal missing-step set and detects conflicting external changes
A durable repair lease and retry budget shared by Mac and browser workers
Pendant and dashboard controls for inspect, repair, abandon, and export the failure receipt

proposals.user_asks: When I say “save this for later” while I’m looking at a page, capture the page and my spoken note as a sourced, searchable research card; later I can ask the pendant what I saved and have the Mac reopen the exact source.
proposals.why_useful: This turns an ephemeral browser tab plus a two-second pendant utterance into durable memory with provenance. It works across the surfaces: the browser has the authenticated page, the pendant supplies intent while away from the keyboard, the relay keeps the request alive, and the Mac creates/reopens a human-readable artifact. It is materially safer than an unsourced memory because every claim points back to URL, tab, timestamp, and excerpt.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime tier only parses the short capture command and acknowledges it. A cheaper background model normalizes the note, extracts a short title/topics, deduplicates against existing cards, and generates a citation-preserving summary. Retrieval is semantic plus exact-topic matching; no model call if the user asks for a title/URL lookup.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge the pendant within 500 ms, enqueue capture in under 2 s, and finish the card in 5–15 s. Retrieval should return the top cards in under 2 s and open the chosen source on the Mac in another 1–3 s.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.01 per capture depending on page length and summarization; retrieval usually under $0.001. Dominant costs are extracting long authenticated pages and background summarization, so cap captured text and hash unchanged excerpts.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated page content and the spoken note leave the browser/Mac only to the owner's relay and memory store; redact secrets and form fields before persistence. Store URL, title, excerpt hash, and source timestamp by default, with full text opt-in. Never submit forms or alter the page. Reopening a private URL must preserve its browser session and should fail closed if the session is gone. The pendant acknowledgement should not read the captured page aloud in public.
missing: A browser-extension command that returns the active tab's selected/semantic content with URL, tab ID, and stable excerpt locators
A durable research-card schema joining capture key, browser provenance, normalized text, and context-graph entities
A background indexing/deduplication worker and retention controls for private captures
An implementation of the granted Mac read-only inspection/sources tools so retrieval can verify the target tab and calendar context
A relay-to-Mac resumable enqueue/receipt path for captures made while the Mac is temporarily offline

proposals.user_asks: Tell me before my important logged-in browser sessions expire or get signed out, and when I’m back at the Mac, open only the affected sign-in pages so I can restore them without exposing page contents.
proposals.why_useful: Silent session expiry is a recurring failure mode for every authenticated workflow: a morning brief can look empty, a form can be half-filled, or a watch can stop silently. This gives the owner an actionable warning from the pendant while keeping private page contents out of the alert, then uses the Mac only for the narrowly scoped recovery step.
proposals.model_tier: No expensive model for detection: a deterministic browser heartbeat/session-state classifier runs on the relay or extension. Use the realtime tier only to understand a spoken request such as “which account needs attention?” and a cheap background model to rank urgency from session age and scheduled watches.
proposals.latency_budget: Heartbeat every 5–15 minutes with <1 s relay processing; alert within one heartbeat of an auth transition. On request, enumerate affected sessions in <2 s; Mac opens the recovery pages in 1–3 s.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost; roughly a few thousand lightweight heartbeat events per month. The dominant cost is relay/browser storage and any optional notification audio, not inference.
proposals.security_concerns: Transmit only state (session ID, origin, auth-needed/healthy, last-seen), never cookies, tokens, DOM text, screenshots, or typed credentials. Keep an allowlist of origins and let the owner pause monitoring from the pendant. Never auto-enter credentials or submit MFA; opening a sign-in page is the maximum automatic action. Expiry records should have short retention and be deletable.
missing: A browser-extension heartbeat payload that can distinguish healthy, expired, MFA-required, and network-failed without exposing page content
Durable per-origin watch policy with quiet hours and a last-alert fingerprint to prevent repeated alerts
A relay alert queue that can reach the pendant and retain the event while the Mac is offline
A Mac action that opens only the affected origin's re-auth URL and returns a receipt
A small dashboard showing session state and allowing per-origin pause/delete

proposals.user_asks: When a meeting, deadline, or reservation changes in one place, tell me what other commitments it breaks and prepare the coordinated cleanup across my Mac, browser, and pendant—updated calendar details, draft notifications, and the exact tabs/files to close or reopen.
proposals.why_useful: Today the surfaces are isolated: a changed calendar event does not reconcile the email thread, authenticated booking page, open documents, reminders, or the owner's spoken plan. This would maintain a live dependency map of commitments and prepare one coherent recovery packet instead of making the owner discover each consequence manually.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model for entity resolution and dependency/risk ranking; use realtime only when the owner asks for the impact or wants the prepared cleanup read aloud. Deterministic connectors should detect source changes and produce diffs before any model call.
proposals.latency_budget: Detect changes within 2–5 minutes for watched sources, generate an impact packet within 30 seconds, and speak a concise alert on the next available pendant connection. Preparing Mac/browser drafts should take under 10 seconds after the owner requests it.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.005–$0.03 per meaningful change, dominated by resolving related messages/pages and generating a short impact summary; unchanged polling should be deterministic and nearly free.
proposals.security_concerns: The dependency graph contains sensitive relationships between calendar, mail, private browser pages, and local files. Keep raw content on the Mac where possible; send the relay only normalized event IDs, titles, times, and redacted impact facts. Never send or delete anything automatically. Any calendar edit, email send, booking change, or file deletion remains a separately previewed action under the owner's maximum-access policy.
missing: A cross-source commitment/dependency graph with provenance, confidence, and expiry rather than isolated per-surface records
Change feeds or reliable polling adapters for Calendar/Mail and authenticated browser watches, with normalized before/after diffs
A planner that maps one changed commitment to affected drafts, reminders, files, tabs, and pending jobs
A single review packet format that the relay can summarize on the pendant and the Mac can render with source links and prepared actions
Idempotent reconciliation actions and receipts so a partially completed cleanup can resume without duplicating drafts or edits

proposals.user_asks: “I lost connection—resume the task I was doing and tell me exactly what is left.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a disconnected browser job can sit behind six pending commands while the Mac job receipt merely says failed; the owner has no single, trustworthy answer about what actually happened, what was already changed, or what is safe to retry. This creates a cross-device recovery conversation: the pendant identifies the interrupted intent, the relay reconciles Mac receipts with browser command/result history, the Mac writes a local recovery capsule, and the browser resumes only idempotent steps after its heartbeat returns. The owner gets one concise spoken status and one concrete next step rather than duplicate submissions or guesswork.
proposals.model_tier: background for receipt reconciliation and capsule generation; realtime only to answer the pendant follow-up and read the final short status
proposals.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds for an initial spoken 'paused/resumed/blocked' status; reconciliation under 10 seconds; browser reconnect may take as long as the extension heartbeat, with no 45-second blind navigate timeout
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.002–$0.01 per recovery (small background text pass; realtime cost only if the owner asks follow-up). Storage is a small local JSON/Markdown capsule plus D1 job metadata.
proposals.security_concerns: Never infer that an unacknowledged browser mutation succeeded. Reconcile by request/idempotency key and typed receipt, quarantine ambiguous writes, and expose URL/tab, timestamps, and before/after evidence locally. Authenticated page content stays on the Mac/extension unless the owner’s existing relay privacy setting permits excerpts. Resume should be limited to the exact original plan and expire after a short lease; no new submission or destructive action is invented.
missing: A cross-surface causal recovery record linking relay intent, Mac jobId/action receipts, browser commandId/result, and the originating pendant utterance
A reconciliation endpoint that distinguishes completed, failed, not-delivered, and ambiguous browser mutations and emits one safe next step
A local recovery-capsule writer plus a reconnect trigger on browser heartbeat; current browser is offline and six commands are pending
A fail-fast browser enqueue/resume path that does not wait 45 seconds when the extension is offline

proposals.user_asks: “Switch me to work mode” (or “personal mode”) and keep every action, tab, file, and spoken briefing in the right context.
proposals.why_useful: The owner cannot safely use one assistant across work and personal life today: a pendant request can reach the Mac, relay memory, Mail/Calendar, and authenticated browser without a durable context boundary. A physical mode switch would make the hive respect the owner's current context—work requests use the work browser session and project, personal requests use the personal session and files—and refuse to silently mix evidence or carry private content into a work briefing.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic routing and redaction by default; background model only to classify an ambiguous request. Realtime is used only to acknowledge the mode change and explain a blocked cross-context action.
proposals.latency_budget: Mode acknowledgment under 300 ms; routing decision under 1 second. Switching must take effect before the next Mac or browser action, and any in-flight action must be paused or explicitly marked with its prior context.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero per switch; small local/relay metadata records. Occasional background classification costs under $0.005, with no page bodies sent to the model unless explicitly allowed.
proposals.security_concerns: Context must be a hard data boundary, not a prompt hint. Store only an opaque context ID in relay telemetry; keep source content local where possible. Tag every job, browser tab/session, file operation, receipt, memory write, and audio item with context and reject mismatches. The pendant should provide a long-press physical override to emergency-neutral mode; switching must not delete or move data.
missing: A persistent context/profile identity on the pendant with an offline-safe toggle and current-mode announcement
Relay and Mac job schemas that carry a non-forgeable context ID through planning, execution, receipts, memory, and audio
Browser session/container affinity and a way to label existing tabs as work or personal without scraping their contents
A context-aware memory projection and redaction layer that prevents cross-context retrieval and cross-context summaries
Dashboard views and recovery tooling that show the active context and flag any in-flight work from the previous context

proposals.user_asks: If I say “pause that” or press the pendant button while a Mac/browser task is running, stop safely, save exactly where it got to, and let me say “resume it” later—even after the browser reconnects or the Mac was asleep.
proposals.why_useful: Today a long job can outlive the browser connection, leave pending commands, or require the owner to remember what was already done. A cross-surface task lease gives the owner a dependable pause/resume control and prevents duplicate clicks, submissions, or stale browser actions.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only for the short spoken pause/resume interaction. Use a cheaper background worker for checkpoint compaction, stale-step validation, and retry planning; use the Mac local planner only to expand the next concrete step.
proposals.latency_budget: A pause acknowledgement should be under 1 second when the relay is reachable; checkpoint persistence under 2 seconds. Resume may take 2–5 seconds to validate Mac/browser availability before acting. If browser is offline, acknowledge and defer without issuing another command.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.01 per pause/resume interaction depending on realtime audio duration; background checkpointing is negligible. The dominant cost is only the spoken interaction, not the persisted state.
proposals.security_concerns: Checkpoint data can contain URLs, page snippets, file paths, and draft text, so encrypt or redact sensitive fields and retain only the minimum needed to resume. Never replay an irreversible browser step from a checkpoint without an explicit fresh confirmation; invalidate leases on tab/session changes and mark unknown outcomes for review.
missing: A durable task-lease/checkpoint schema shared by relay, Mac job runner, and browser bridge
A pendant button/event route that targets the active job rather than starting a new command
Browser command cancellation and idempotent step keys, including an offline queue TTL and supersession rule
Mac-side checkpoint hooks around each action and a resume endpoint that reports the last verified receipt
A dashboard/voice status view showing paused, stale, unknown-outcome, and resumable states

proposals.user_asks: After you do something important for me—send a message, change a record, submit a form, or create an appointment—prove that it actually took effect and tell me if the result is confirmed, contradicted, or unknown.
proposals.why_useful: Today an action receipt mostly reports what the executor attempted. The owner still cannot reliably distinguish “the click ran” from “the remote service accepted and persisted the change,” especially when a browser disconnects or a Mac action times out. A postcondition verifier would prevent false completion claims and surface ambiguous outcomes immediately.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to acknowledge the result briefly. Use a cheaper background verifier for re-reading the target state and comparing it with the intended mutation; use a stronger model only when the returned evidence is structurally inconsistent or ambiguous.
proposals.latency_budget: For local Mac changes, verify within 1 second. For browser-backed mutations, verify within 3–10 seconds, with a bounded retry after navigation or session recovery. Speak immediately when the state is unknown rather than waiting indefinitely.
proposals.cost_estimate: Typically $0.001–$0.02 per verification, dominated by browser/page retrieval and occasional model-based comparison; local structured checks should require no model call.
proposals.security_concerns: Verification may re-read private mail, account pages, files, or calendar records. Limit it to the exact target and fields involved, redact evidence in spoken output, encrypt retained before/after hashes, and never treat a failed verification as permission to retry an irreversible action automatically. Sending, deletion, purchases, and submissions still require the owner's existing confirmation policy.
missing: A postcondition contract attached to every mutating action: target, expected state, verification method, deadline, and safe-failure behavior
Independent read-after-write adapters for Mac files/Notes/Calendar/Mail and authenticated browser pages
A durable evidence record linking intent, action receipt, verification read, and normalized before/after values
A reconciliation policy for timeouts and duplicate-risk outcomes that marks the job unknown instead of replaying it
Pendant and dashboard result states for confirmed, contradicted, and unknown, with a concise evidence link

proposals.user_asks: “If I start a multi-step task and then close my laptop or lose the browser, keep the work safe, resume it when the right device returns, and tell me exactly what was completed, skipped, or still needs me.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the relay, Mac, and browser can each be online while a job still has seven queued browser commands, no usable tab identity, and no durable user-facing explanation of where execution stopped. This would turn an interrupted workflow into a recoverable one: the owner gets a concise pendant update and a Mac evidence folder instead of a silent timeout or duplicate submission. It is deliberately review-only for browser mutations; it can resume reads and drafts, but never silently sends or submits.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model for checkpoint reconciliation, stale-step classification, and summarization; reserve realtime only for the pendant's live explanation or a direct follow-up question.
proposals.latency_budget: A start acknowledgement in under 2 seconds; resume automatically within 30 seconds of a device heartbeat; final evidence brief within 1 minute after the last step. No repeated model call while waiting for a device.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per interrupted job, dominated by one small reconciliation/summarization call; storage and heartbeats are negligible. Avoid replaying page contents or resending full context at every retry.
proposals.security_concerns: Persist only step metadata, redacted result snippets, source URL/tab/session IDs, hashes, and receipts; keep authenticated page bodies local to the browser/Mac evidence folder unless explicitly requested. Use idempotency keys and step leases so reconnects cannot duplicate a form fill or submission. Require explicit owner confirmation for any irreversible browser action, even though the Mac owner policy allows maximum local access.
missing: A durable cross-surface checkpoint record with step state (pending/running/completed/expired/needs-owner), lease expiry, idempotency key, and dependency graph
A heartbeat and stale-step reaper that distinguishes browser offline, Mac offline, and an actually failed step; queued browser commands need dead-letter visibility instead of indefinite pending state
Resume semantics that reattach a browser session/tab when available and correlate Mac /execute job IDs with action receipts and the final evidence bundle
A small pendant notification/ack path for resumed, blocked, and completed states, plus a dashboard timeline showing before/after evidence and skipped steps

proposals.user_asks: “I’m leaving my desk—freeze this work exactly where it is, and when I come back, restore the useful parts and remind me what I was doing.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner loses working context whenever they close the laptop, move between locations, or return after an interruption. Today the system can act on individual Mac or browser jobs, but it cannot preserve the human’s live workspace as a resumable handoff: which documents and tabs mattered, what was unsaved, what the next intended action was, and what must not be reopened. This would create a private, time-bounded work capsule rather than another task queue.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to label the captured workspace and produce a short resume note; use the realtime model only if the owner asks follow-up questions through the pendant.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge the freeze in under 2 seconds, capture a bounded manifest within 10 seconds, and restore or explain unavailable items within 20 seconds after the Mac returns.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually below $0.02 per capsule; the dominant cost is one small summarization call. Keep document contents local and summarize only metadata and explicitly selected snippets.
proposals.security_concerns: The capsule may expose sensitive filenames, URLs, and unsaved text. Encrypt it, give it an expiry, allow an immediate pendant delete gesture, redact secret-like fields, and never silently reopen a private page or send a draft. Restoration should show a manifest first and require confirmation for reopening sensitive tabs or unsaved files.
missing: A Mac workspace-capture adapter that records bounded app/document/browser manifests and unsaved-state warnings without requiring Screen Recording
An encrypted, expiring capsule format shared by relay and Mac, with a local-only option
Browser APIs for exporting and restoring a selected tab set with session affinity, without copying page bodies to the relay
A resume planner that distinguishes safe reopening from potentially destructive restoration and produces a cited next-step note
A pendant trigger and return-to-desk signal, such as an explicit button phrase plus Mac heartbeat reappearance

proposals.user_asks: “When you finish something for me, tell me at the first moment I can actually absorb it—not while I’m presenting or driving—and escalate only if it is genuinely time-critical.”
proposals.why_useful: A completed job is not useful if its result arrives during a meeting, focused writing, or an audio conversation and is then forgotten. Today results can be produced and queued, but there is no shared interruptibility decision across the relay, pendant, calendar, and Mac state. This would make completion delivery part of the task: urgent items break through with a concise alert, while everything else waits for a safe attention window and arrives as one grouped, sourced update.
proposals.model_tier: Use a small background model for urgency classification and grouping; use realtime only for a live spoken alert when the owner is already interacting with the pendant.
proposals.latency_budget: Classify on job completion in under 1 second; defer nonurgent results until the next detected safe window, with a configurable maximum delay such as 30 minutes. Urgent alerts should reach the pendant within 3 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: A few cents per day at most; classification can use a compact model and calendar/app metadata, with no need to resend the original task context.
proposals.security_concerns: Calendar titles, foreground-app names, and job contents are sensitive. Keep raw metadata local where possible, send only a redacted interruptibility signal to relay, expose why an alert was escalated, and provide a physical pause gesture. Never infer that a meeting is safe to interrupt merely because the calendar is empty.
missing: A shared interruptibility state with calendar quiet periods, active pendant conversation, foreground app, and explicit owner pause/resume
A result mailbox that groups completed receipts by urgency and prevents duplicate audio or desktop notifications
A pendant delivery primitive supporting concise alert, deferred digest, and acknowledgement/snooze
A policy evaluator that can explain urgency and distinguish deadline risk from ordinary completion
A local Mac notification/Calendar adapter that works without Accessibility or Screen Recording

proposals.user_asks: “Keep an eye on my important things, but only interrupt me when it’s genuinely urgent and I’m at a safe stopping point.”
proposals.why_useful: This would combine the pendant’s always-available intent and haptic channel, the relay’s persistent scheduling, the Mac’s current foreground app and calendar context, and authenticated browser sessions into one interruption policy. Instead of either spamming notifications or missing changes, it queues evidence-backed items and delivers a one-sentence alert only when urgency and interruptibility both pass; otherwise it leaves a cited review queue for later.
proposals.model_tier: Background/scheduled triage uses a cheaper slow model; realtime is used only for the owner’s button-press follow-up or spoken delivery.
proposals.latency_budget: Source polling can be minutes to hours depending on watch cadence. A button press should acknowledge state in under 1 second; a delivered summary should begin within 2 seconds once a safe window is detected.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low-to-moderate: mostly scheduled extraction and small ranking calls; roughly $0.01–$0.05 per daily source sweep, with realtime cost only for an actual spoken interaction. Storage/egress is dominated by retained browser snippets and generated audio.
proposals.security_concerns: Only named authenticated browser sessions and redacted Calendar/Mail snippets enter triage. Never include secrets or full mail bodies by default. A page change can be adversarial or misleading, so alerts must include source URL/time and confidence, and actions remain draft-only. The owner’s physical quiet/urgent control should override model judgment locally.
missing: A shared attention-envelope schema (urgency, interruptibility, quiet hours, source provenance, expiry, delivery channel) understood by relay, Mac, browser, and pendant
A durable scheduler/queue that deduplicates page changes and survives browser or Mac offline periods
A Mac read-only context implementation for foreground app, running apps, and calendar/mail; the granted tools are currently schemas without implementations
Browser watch execution with TTL and stale-session parking/revalidation; Safari is currently offline and has stale queued commands
Pendant firmware support for a persistent quiet/urgent mode and a small haptic/audio delivery queue

proposals.user_asks: “If my Mac loses Wi‑Fi, keep only my essential work connected through the pendant until normal internet returns.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the pendant can speak over LTE-M, but it cannot serve as a controlled backup link for the Mac. A cellular failover mode would preserve calendar/mail sync, relay control, and a narrow set of approved browser or collaboration endpoints during a router outage or travel—without pretending LTE-M is a fast general-purpose hotspot.
proposals.model_tier: No expensive model is needed for failover. Firmware and Mac networking handle routing; a cheap background policy service maintains the allowlist and reports health. Realtime is used only if the owner asks what is happening.
proposals.latency_budget: Failover detection and route activation within 5–15 seconds; status should be visible locally within 1 second. Throughput is deliberately best-effort and bounded by LTE-M, with large downloads blocked or deferred.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low model cost (health checks and policy are deterministic). Cellular data and hardware certification dominate; expect a small monthly data charge and roughly $5–$15 incremental modem/power-management hardware if the product board needs a proper USB/network interface.
proposals.security_concerns: The Mac must not expose the pendant’s cellular link as unrestricted routing. Use an owner-visible allowlist, device-bound keys, DNS/IP filtering, per-app quotas, and an emergency disable gesture. Relay sees connection metadata and approved traffic, not decrypted HTTPS contents. Never silently upload private browser data merely because failover is active.
missing: Pendant firmware USB networking or a secure tether protocol; the current prototype exposes no implemented network-interface mode
A Mac network-extension/helper that detects Wi‑Fi loss, installs a metered route, and removes it cleanly on recovery
Relay-side authenticated tunnel termination and traffic accounting
A policy UI for essential apps/domains, quotas, and an explicit failover indicator
A browser harness mode that pauses nonessential polling and stale commands while the link is metered

proposals.user_asks: “If you lose connection while working on something, keep the work safe and resume it exactly once when my Mac or browser comes back—then tell me what was completed, skipped, or still needs me.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a pendant request can leave a stale browser command or an ambiguous Mac job after a disconnect. A single intent would survive relay, Mac, and browser outages, resume only idempotent steps, and provide one truthful completion report instead of duplicate submissions or guesswork.
proposals.model_tier: background for checkpoint reconciliation and receipt summarization; deterministic workers for lease/step replay; realtime only for the short spoken status when the owner asks
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgement under 1 second; reconnect reconciliation within 5 seconds; spoken summary under 2 seconds after receipts arrive
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per recovery using deterministic replay and a small background summary; planner escalation only for ambiguous or non-idempotent steps. Storage/queue operations dominate, not model calls.
proposals.security_concerns: Private URLs, file paths, and action receipts remain on the relay/Mac account scope; browser session tokens never enter the pendant. Non-idempotent sends, purchases, deletes, or submissions are marked blocked-after-disconnect and require an explicit new owner command. Dashboard must show device, lease, and before/after evidence.
missing: A cross-surface intent ledger with durable step IDs, idempotency keys, leases, and a reconciliation state machine shared by Mac and browser workers
A device liveness/epoch protocol so an offline browser extension cannot claim commands after its lease expires
A unified receipt endpoint joining Mac action receipts and browser typed results under one intent ID
A pendant-friendly resume/status event and dashboard view for orphaned, replayed, and blocked steps

proposals.user_asks: “Tell me when my Mac, browser, and pendant disagree about whether something happened, and help me reconcile it without repeating the action.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a timeout, sleep, or reconnect can leave conflicting evidence: the browser may show a changed page while the Mac has no receipt, or the Mac may report completion while the authenticated page still shows the old state. The owner needs an evidence-based contradiction alert, not a guessed success or an unsafe retry.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic evidence matching and state-machine logic first; background model only to summarize the contradiction in plain language. Realtime is used only when the owner asks for the short spoken explanation.
proposals.latency_budget: Detect contradictions within 2 seconds of receiving a new receipt or page observation; spoken alert under 2 seconds when requested. Reconciliation can take up to 30 seconds because it may require a fresh browser read.
proposals.cost_estimate: Under $0.01 per contradiction in the common case; most work is receipt comparison and one read-only verification. Planner escalation is reserved for genuinely ambiguous evidence.
proposals.security_concerns: Evidence must remain account-scoped and redact private page contents in pendant audio. Never retry an uncertain mutation automatically. Show URLs, timestamps, action IDs, and before/after snippets only in the protected Mac/dashboard view; require a fresh owner instruction for any corrective mutation.
missing: A typed shared state vocabulary for Mac actions, browser observations, and pendant acknowledgements, including unknown and contradicted states
A causal evidence graph that links receipts, page observations, device epochs, and timestamps rather than treating each surface's success flag as authoritative
A read-only verification workflow for authenticated browser pages and Mac state after a contradiction
A dashboard and pendant event format that explains the conflict and offers safe choices: verify again, mark resolved, or prepare (but not execute) a correction

proposals.user_asks: “Start this multi-step task and keep it safe if the browser, Mac, or connection drops—resume where you left off and tell me exactly what completed, what did not, and what needs me.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a task can leave partial Mac mutations, stale browser commands, and a relay job with no single truth. A cross-surface transaction would make long tasks trustworthy: the relay coordinates checkpoints, the Mac records durable receipts, the browser contributes tab-scoped evidence, and the pendant gives a compact status/resume control even after disconnection.
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheaper background model for checkpoint reconciliation and retry planning; reserve realtime for the owner's spoken request and a short exception/resume conversation.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 2 seconds; checkpoint updates within 5 seconds of each action; retries can run in the background. Never block the owner waiting for a whole workflow.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly 1–3 background model calls per failed or resumed task; normal successful steps use typed receipts and no model call. Dominant cost is only reconciliation of ambiguous outcomes.
proposals.security_concerns: The coordinator must never replay a non-idempotent browser submit or Mac mutation merely because a receipt is missing. Persist a step idempotency key, precondition/evidence hash, and outcome (completed/unknown/skipped); quarantine unknown steps for review. Private URLs, snippets, and action receipts leave the Mac only when needed for the relay's task record; redact by default. Pendant resume/status should reveal only task labels, not page contents. Existing maximum-access policy means this is observability and safe replay—not a new approval gate.
missing: A durable cross-surface saga/job schema with step IDs, idempotency keys, preconditions, evidence hashes, and explicit unknown outcomes
A relay coordinator that leases work to Mac/browser and reconciles receipts after reconnect
A pendant status/resume command and offline-safe cancellation marker
Browser stale-command quarantine and a Mac-to-relay receipt acknowledgement protocol

proposals.user_asks: “Prepare this for me, but make the approval expire if anything important changes—tell me exactly what changed instead of letting stale work go through.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can get drafts and prepared actions, but today a prepared artifact can become stale while it sits in a browser tab, Mac job queue, or relay overnight. This capability turns preparation into time-bounded escrow: the relay records the relevant facts, the browser and Mac re-check them immediately before the final action, and the pendant reports a concise change alert. A stale approval cannot silently authorize a different price, recipient, appointment, or document.
proposals.model_tier: Use a low-cost background model to identify which fields are approval-critical and compare before/after evidence; use realtime only to tell the owner what changed and ask whether to regenerate the preparation.
proposals.latency_budget: Preparation can be asynchronous. The final freshness check should complete within 3–5 seconds; if it fails, stop and notify rather than retrying blindly.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually no model call for typed field comparisons; approximately one inexpensive background call only when page structure or semantics changed. Storage is a small snapshot of redacted critical fields and hashes per escrow.
proposals.security_concerns: Never retain full private pages or message bodies when hashes and selected fields suffice. Scope each escrow to a specific account, tab/session, file, recipient, and expiry. A changed critical field invalidates the escrow; a harmless volatile field should not. Final mutation remains impossible from an expired token, even if an old browser command or Mac job is replayed.
missing: A cross-surface escrow record with expiry, critical-field allowlist, source identity, and approval nonce
Browser and Mac preflight endpoints that return typed before/after evidence against the escrow
Relay enforcement that rejects expired or invalidated non-idempotent actions
Pendant notification/control for approve, regenerate, or abandon

proposals.user_asks: Keep my private browser work reliable: if the browser bridge drops or has stuck commands, recover what can be recovered, tell me what was not run, and never silently replay a risky step.
proposals.why_useful: Today seven commands are pending while the bridge is offline, and failed browser jobs can sit indistinguishable from work that merely needs retry. A cross-surface watchdog would make the pendant a trustworthy status channel: it can drain safe reads after reconnection, quarantine stale or mutating steps, and give the owner an exact interruption report rather than losing work or duplicating a submission.
proposals.model_tier: Background/scheduled triage should use a cheaper model; realtime is used only for the short pendant alert and follow-up. Deterministic queue-state checks and idempotency comparisons should run without an LLM.
proposals.latency_budget: Heartbeat detection under 30 seconds; reconnect reconciliation under 2 minutes after the extension returns; pendant alert under 3 seconds once the decision is made. No polling or browser action while the extension is offline.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero for heartbeats, queue reconciliation, hashes, and receipts; roughly one inexpensive text-model call per incident (typically <$0.01), with realtime cost only if the owner asks a spoken follow-up.
proposals.security_concerns: Private URLs, snippets, and session identifiers stay on the Mac/relay and are not sent to the public browser backend. Read-only steps may auto-retry only with an idempotency key and unchanged tab/session binding. Click/type/submit/delete steps are quarantined and require an explicit owner command after showing the last known URL, action, and evidence. On reconnect, cancel commands whose TTL expired rather than replay them.
missing: A durable browser job runner with persisted step states, TTLs, idempotency keys, and retry policy (the router exists but the runner does not).
A bridge watchdog that can distinguish offline, stale polling, and Safari-dialog failure, then reconcile or cancel pending commands.
A typed browser receipt/evidence record exposed to the pendant and planner, plus a safe-read versus mutation classifier.
An extension wake/reconnect hook or a clear owner-facing instruction when Safari must be opened manually.

proposals.user_asks: When I walk away from my Mac, pause browser work safely, and when I come back, give me a one-line spoken handoff before anything continues.
proposals.why_useful: A browser session can outlive the person who started it. Presence-bound leases prevent a queued private-page task from continuing unattended, while the pendant gives a useful handoff instead of forcing the owner to inspect logs or guess whether a form was submitted.
proposals.model_tier: Presence detection, lease expiry, and safe pause are deterministic. Use a cheap background model to summarize the receipt; use realtime only to speak the short handoff when the pendant reconnects.
proposals.latency_budget: Pause within one heartbeat (target 10–30 seconds) after the pendant/Mac presence signal disappears. On return, produce the handoff within 5 seconds, and do not resume mutating steps until the owner explicitly says resume.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible for lease and heartbeat state; <$0.01 per return summary when there is substantive work. No browser-model call is needed for simple receipts.
proposals.security_concerns: Presence is sensitive metadata, so retain only coarse active/away state and short history. Private URLs remain local. A lost presence signal must fail closed for mutating browser actions, while read-only actions may be cancelled or retained—not silently run. The pendant’s explicit resume phrase should be bound to the same job/session and a displayed action hash.
missing: A relay-to-Mac presence/lease channel with signed session and pendant identity.
Browser commands carrying a lease ID and action class, enforced by the executor rather than only by the planner.
A compact receipt-to-speech handoff formatter and a resume endpoint that requires the matching job/action hash.

proposals.user_asks: Use my private accounts to answer a question, but never send the private page or raw personal data off my Mac—give me only the minimum derived result and show me exactly what was disclosed.
proposals.why_useful: The owner could get genuinely useful cross-site answers today only by exposing whole private pages to a general model or by doing the comparison manually. A local privacy boundary would let the pendant ask questions over logged-in data while keeping credentials, page contents, and unnecessary personal fields on the Mac.
proposals.model_tier: Use a small local Mac model or deterministic extraction for filtering and aggregation; use the cheaper background model for synthesis over the redacted derived dataset. Realtime is reserved for the final short spoken answer.
proposals.latency_budget: Local extraction and redaction under 10 seconds for a handful of pages; synthesis under 15 seconds. If the query requires broad browsing or an uncertain field mapping, pause and ask rather than widening disclosure.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.02 per request, dominated by one background synthesis call; local filtering and hashing are effectively free. No cloud token cost for raw page content because it never leaves the Mac.
proposals.security_concerns: The Mac must treat authenticated browser DOM and credentials as private. A non-bypassable data diode should allow only typed aggregates, boolean predicates, ranges, and owner-approved snippets to cross into the relay. Every outbound field needs a reason, sensitivity label, provenance, and hash; the pendant should announce the disclosure summary. No automatic submission, message send, or account mutation. Encrypt the local intermediate and expire it after the answer.
missing: A Mac-local privacy broker that can query authenticated tabs, transform raw DOM into a typed derived dataset, and enforce an allowlisted outbound schema.
A browser extraction protocol with field-level provenance and sensitivity labels rather than whole-page text results.
Relay/model routing that rejects payloads containing raw private fields and accepts only the signed derived-result envelope.
A pendant disclosure receipt and a way for the owner to approve expanding one field when the derived answer is insufficient.

proposals.user_asks: When I ask you to check or do something in my browser, keep it queued if the browser bridge is asleep, wake the right browser when possible, and tell me on the pendant when it is ready or why it cannot proceed—then continue automatically without me repeating myself.
proposals.why_useful: Today a voice request can silently become a failed browser job because the extension is offline or blocked. This turns the wearable, always-on relay, Mac executor, and browser session into one durable handoff: the owner gets a clear status and does not need to remember or reissue work.
proposals.model_tier: Cheap background/state-machine logic for health checks, queueing, retries, and notifications; realtime model only for the initial spoken request and concise exception explanation.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge on pendant in under 1 second; retry on browser heartbeat for up to 10 minutes with exponential backoff; once online, begin within 2 seconds. Never busy-loop or hold the realtime model open.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for normal operation; a few short TTS/status messages per failure or recovery dominate, plus negligible D1/local queue storage.
proposals.security_concerns: Browser commands may touch authenticated sessions, so preserve existing per-session affinity and evidence capsules; never auto-submit forms or send messages as part of recovery. Opening a browser is low impact, but navigation and mutations must retain existing receipts and owner policy. Status should disclose only site/task labels, not page contents, until execution succeeds.
missing: A durable browser-intent queue with idempotency keys and retry policy shared by relay and Mac agent
A Mac-side health action that can launch the configured browser and surface an actionable notification when the extension is not polling (extension enablement itself may still require the owner)
A relay-to-pendant completion/failure event contract tied to the original voice request
A watchdog that distinguishes offline extension, blocked dialog, expired session, and owner-required permission rather than reporting one timeout

proposals.user_asks: Replay the last failed thing I asked for in a safe sandbox, compare it with the original pendant, relay, Mac, and browser trace, and tell me exactly which device or step diverged.
proposals.why_useful: Today a failed voice request leaves separate job receipts, pipeline records, and browser errors, but the owner must manually correlate them and try again. This would turn an intermittent multi-device failure into a reproducible diagnosis rather than another blind retry.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic trace correlation, request-id matching, and sandbox replay first; use a cheap background model only to render the final three-sentence explanation. Realtime is unnecessary.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate spoken acknowledgement; collect the original trace in under 2 seconds and produce a diagnosis within 30 seconds. If replay needs an unavailable browser, report the exact blocked boundary rather than waiting indefinitely.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually near-zero model cost; bounded trace storage and one optional short summary call. Replay may consume ordinary Mac/browser execution time but should not invoke paid external actions.
proposals.security_concerns: Sandbox replay must prevent sends, purchases, deletes, form submissions, and other irreversible effects; authenticated pages should be inspected only in the original paired session and with redacted evidence. Store hashes and bounded excerpts by default, not raw page bodies or audio.
missing: A durable cross-surface correlation ID propagated from pendant audio/pipeline events through relay intent, Mac job, browser command, and every receipt
A replay mode that clones or stubs high-impact actions and marks the boundary where execution was intentionally suppressed
A trace joiner that orders events by monotonic timestamp across device clocks and distinguishes timeout, permission, offline, and application errors
A compact pendant/dashboard result schema carrying first-divergence step, evidence references, and a resumable next action

proposals.user_asks: If something I asked you to do in a logged-in browser fails because the bridge is offline, tell me what failed, keep the safe read-only part, and resume it automatically when the browser reconnects—without replaying a stale form submission or click.
proposals.why_useful: The live Mac agent has seven pending browser commands while the bridge is offline, and prior navigations have timed out. Today the owner gets opaque failures and cannot know whether retrying could duplicate a mutation. This makes the wearable, relay, Mac, and authenticated browser behave as one recoverable system: the pendant can report the interruption, the relay can retain the work, the Mac can reattach, and the browser can revalidate before continuing.
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheap background model for queue classification, URL/title revalidation, and compact failure summaries; reserve realtime only for the spoken interruption/recovery sentence. No model is needed for idempotency, tab affinity, or mutation quarantine.
proposals.latency_budget: Detect disconnect within one heartbeat (about 5–10 seconds), speak a short status on the next available relay turn, and resume read-only extraction within 10 seconds of a healthy browser heartbeat. Never auto-resume a write step; stage it for the owner.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per interrupted job; most work is deterministic state and browser polling. Realtime/TTS cost occurs only for the brief spoken alert, and background summarization dominates when a long page must be re-explained.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated page text must remain local to the Mac/relay policy and be redacted before any spoken alert. Persist tab/session IDs, URL, title, step hashes, and before/after evidence—not passwords or full page bodies. A reconnect must prove the same tab/session and a fresh URL/title/DOM fingerprint; otherwise quarantine and ask. Never replay submit/send/delete/purchase or arbitrary click steps automatically, even though the owner permits broad Mac access.
missing: A durable per-step browser work capsule with read/write classification, idempotency key, precondition fingerprint, retry count, and quarantine state
A browser heartbeat/reconnect handshake that returns tab identity and a fresh page fingerprint before releasing queued commands
Relay-to-pendant delivery of a compact interruption and resume receipt, with a deduplicated alert ID
A deterministic rule that permits automatic retries only for reads/navigation and converts mutations into a reviewable plan with evidence
A dashboard view for quarantined steps and an explicit resume/discard action

proposals.user_asks: Keep a draft I asked you to prepare synchronized across my Mac editor and logged-in browser: if I edit it while you work, detect the conflict, preserve both versions, and tell me the smallest decision needed so I can continue without losing either one.
proposals.why_useful: Today a server plan, a Mac file, and a browser form are separate copies. If the owner edits one while the agent is preparing another, the system can overwrite work, submit stale text, or force them to reconstruct the difference. This would give them a genuinely collaborative handoff: the pendant identifies the conflict, the relay retains the draft state, the Mac computes a local diff, and the browser supplies the current authenticated target.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic hashes, file/editor version tracking, and structured field diffs first. Use a cheaper background model only to summarize non-sensitive conflicts; use realtime only to speak the one decision required. Never ask the expensive realtime model to regenerate an entire draft merely because versions diverged.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture a version before each agent write, detect divergence within 2 seconds of a local edit or browser result, and present a compact conflict card within 5 seconds. Applying the owner's selected resolution should complete in under 3 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually below $0.01 per conflict; local diffing and browser metadata dominate. Model spend is limited to ambiguous prose conflict summaries, and spoken output is one short TTS response.
proposals.security_concerns: Drafts may contain private email, work, or account data. Keep full versions on the Mac or the authenticated browser session, send only redacted field names and hashes to the relay by default, and require explicit selection before any version is copied into a form or sent. Preserve the owner's original and never silently overwrite or submit.
missing: A cross-surface draft identity and version manifest binding a local file/editor buffer to a browser form or message
Mac file/editor change notifications and a bounded three-way diff service that can work without Accessibility for supported editors
