changes.effort: Small to medium: identity-aware permission probe, action-result propagation, dashboard status card, and launch/recheck flow; add tests for stale grants after app replacement and for read-only operation with UI disabled.
changes.risk: A false negative could temporarily disable UI automation after an update; recover with explicit recheck and a visible manual retry. Never auto-grant or weaken macOS permissions.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible runtime/API cost; one local probe at startup and after permission changes.
changes.latency_impact: Milliseconds at startup; avoids wasted 25-step computer-use loops and false receipts.
changes.security_impact: Positive: prevents untrusted or misidentified binaries from being treated as authorized, without expanding permissions.
depends_on: Owner must grant Accessibility to the exact AI Pendant Agent app currently running, or the app must preserve its signed identity across updates

changes.change: Create a cross-surface outbound-preflight protocol. The Mac and browser facets independently produce a canonical payload manifest (destination identity, account, attachments, fields, redacted content labels, and hashes); the relay reconciles them with the owner's sensitivity policy and returns a signed report hash. The executor must require that exact hash at send/upload time and invalidate it whenever the payload or destination changes.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets a meaningful final safety check instead of a generic confirmation: “this exact file, to this exact account, containing these flagged fields.” A stale approval cannot accidentally authorize a changed draft or tab.
changes.effort: Medium to high: define the manifest schema, add Mail/app and browser interception adapters, implement policy evaluation and hash binding, and provide a compact dashboard/pendant explanation.
changes.risk: Overly aggressive rules could create confirmation fatigue; begin with high-confidence secrets, external recipients, and account mismatches, with per-rule muting. If one surface cannot produce a trustworthy manifest, fail closed for sending/uploading but preserve editing and draft creation.
changes.cost_impact: Low recurring cost; mostly local hashing and deterministic policy evaluation, with occasional small background-model calls for ambiguous classification.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 1–3 seconds before an irreversible send/upload; no impact on ordinary editing or browsing.
changes.security_impact: Strongly positive: minimizes raw-data movement, binds approval to immutable payload evidence, and prevents confused-deputy actions across stale browser tabs or changed files.
depends_on: Local draft/attachment manifest extraction
Browser destination identity contract
Owner sensitivity-policy storage
Send/upload interception points
Pendant approval bound to a report hash

changes.change: Add a MeetingContextCapsule service spanning relay, Mac, and browser: at a scheduled boundary it creates a versioned, content-addressed snapshot containing the selected event ID, redacted mail/tab citations, open-window/tab identifiers, and focused document metadata; it exposes prepare, handoff, restore, and expire operations with idempotency keys. Restore must verify postconditions (expected app/tab/document present) and return a partial-success receipt rather than silently claiming success.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can leave for a meeting and come back to the same work with a trustworthy, short handoff. If the Mac reconnects late or a tab disappeared, they see exactly what was restored and what needs attention instead of losing their place or receiving a fabricated 'done'.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and durable store, Mac window/tab snapshot adapter, browser tab identity adapter, scheduler integration, and tests for disconnects, duplicate triggers, and partial restore.
changes.risk: Window restoration can disrupt an active workflow or reopen sensitive tabs. Default to restoring only the captured app/tab set and never closing unrelated work; expire capsules after a short retention period. If restore fails, preserve the capsule and present a manual recovery list.
changes.cost_impact: Small storage and one background summarization call per prepared meeting; no additional realtime calls unless the owner asks to hear it. Implementation cost is primarily integration and reliability testing.
changes.latency_impact: Snapshot capture should be under 2 seconds; preparation is bounded by source reads and should complete within 20 seconds; restore is parallelized and should complete within 10 seconds.
changes.security_impact: Keep raw content on the Mac where possible; relay receives only redacted excerpts and opaque citations. Encrypt capsules at rest, scope them to the owner's account, and provide immediate delete/pause controls. Never include passwords, cookies, or full page dumps.
depends_on: Implement mac_read_sources and mac_readonly_inspect rather than schema-only stubs
Stable browser tab/session IDs with bounded authenticated page reads
Durable scheduler and idempotent job execution
Postcondition/evidence receipt contract across Mac and relay

changes.change: Add a live cross-surface readiness panel and preflight API for any planned desktop routine. It should show relay, Mac, browser, Calendar/Mail, Accessibility, and Screen Recording states; classify a plan as ready, degraded, or blocked; list exactly which steps will be skipped; and automatically requeue only the missing browser/read-source steps when their heartbeat returns. Do not fabricate completion from a partial run.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Before asking the pendant to prepare a meeting or act on a portal, the owner can see whether it can actually reach the required context. A disconnected browser or missing permission becomes an honest, actionable warning instead of a long failed action and a misleading summary.
changes.effort: Medium: health aggregation, plan dependency declarations, UI status card, and reconnect-aware retry tests.
changes.risk: Health checks may expose app names, URLs, or account scopes on the dashboard. Redact URLs/titles by default and show details only on demand; cap retries to prevent repeated actions when a bridge reconnects.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible runtime cost; one small health poll on dashboard open and no model call.
changes.latency_impact: Preflight under 500 ms locally; retries begin on heartbeat rather than polling aggressively.
changes.security_impact: Readiness metadata must be scoped to the owner and must not include cookies or page content. Treat permission state as sensitive local telemetry.
depends_on: Implementations for mac_read_sources and mac_readonly_inspect
Browser heartbeat with pending-command reconciliation
Plan dependency metadata and idempotent retry keys

changes.change: Create a crash-safe, privacy-preserving Recovery Capsule protocol: Mac and browser producers write encrypted local checkpoints using a common manifest (producer, timestamp, app/tab identity, content class, redaction status, checksum, expiry); the relay stores only opaque capsule IDs and redacted indexes. A two-phase restore API must first return a dry-run conflict report, then apply only the requested capsule and emit per-artifact postconditions.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A dropped connection or accidental close would stop being a permanent loss. The owner could recover a specific unfinished task from the pendant without handing the service passwords or silently overwriting newer work.
changes.effort: High: OS/app event adapters, browser draft checkpointing, encrypted local storage, relay index/TTL handling, conflict detection, and recovery tests across crashes and reconnects.
changes.risk: A faulty checkpoint could preserve stale or sensitive content, and a restore could overwrite newer work. Use immutable capsules, short retention, checksums, explicit conflict reports, and never overwrite by default; if a producer cannot prove its snapshot is complete, mark it incomplete rather than restoring it.
changes.cost_impact: Low ongoing API cost; storage is local-first. Engineering cost is substantial because each app/browser form has different save semantics.
changes.latency_impact: Checkpoint writes must be asynchronous and non-blocking; restore adds one local verification pass and should remain under 10 seconds for a bounded capsule.
changes.security_impact: This is a new sensitive-data surface. Encrypt at rest with a device-bound key, keep raw payloads off the relay, redact before indexing, support immediate purge, and log access without logging payloads.
depends_on: Mac app/window and document lifecycle events
Browser extension draft checkpoint API with explicit site allowlists
Durable encrypted local storage and relay opaque-index endpoints
Typed restore executor with dry-run conflict reporting

changes.change: Add a signed, low-bandwidth handoff envelope shared by pendant, relay, Mac bridge, and browser bridge. The envelope contains taskId, compact intent, allowed operation classes, last confirmed step, evidence hashes, expiry, cancellation nonce, and a monotonic sequence. Each surface acknowledges the sequence; the Mac and browser persist step receipts and can safely replay only idempotent steps after reconnect.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A dropped call or moving away from the Mac no longer loses the work already described. The owner can press the pendant once to continue, later hear 'ready for review,' and inspect exactly where the task stopped instead of repeating themselves.
changes.effort: 3–5 engineering days across firmware protocol, relay D1 schema/worker logic, local-agent bridge, and browser session restoration; add fault-injection tests for duplicate delivery, stale tabs, and mid-step disconnects.
changes.risk: Replay could duplicate a mutation or a stale browser tab could act on the wrong page. Mitigate with sequence numbers, idempotency keys, tab URL/session binding, before/after evidence, expiry, and mandatory pause at irreversible actions. Cancel and expire envelopes server-side.
changes.cost_impact: A few hundred bytes per checkpoint and a few KB of D1 receipts; roughly $0.01 or less per handoff, mostly background summarization. Firmware RAM impact under 4 KB with a single queued envelope.
changes.latency_impact: One LTE control packet and relay acknowledgement under 1 s when connected; reconnect polling adds 1–2 s on the Mac. No added latency to normal live audio.
changes.security_impact: Use device-bound signing/MAC and short-lived opaque IDs; never place page text or secrets in the pendant envelope. Relay stores encrypted checkpoint metadata with 7-day TTL; dashboard exposes revoke/delete.
depends_on: Durable relay job state and cancellation
Mac/browser typed receipts and session affinity
Pendant event/retry queue and completion notification

changes.change: Add a failure-aware reconciliation loop that joins relay pipeline events, Mac /jobs state, /journal action receipts, and browser heartbeat/session state by requestId. It should classify each unfinished job as progressing, completed-with-missing-receipt, failed-retryable, failed-permanent, or unreachable; issue at most one idempotent retry for retryable read/open steps; and publish a concise owner-facing outcome with the exact last successful step and next recovery option. Do not add blocking approval gates.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner asks the hive to do something and walks away, they get a trustworthy answer instead of a vague 'processing' or silent failure. If the browser disappears or the Mac bridge loses permission, the system can say precisely what happened and recover harmless steps automatically.
changes.effort: Medium: correlation schema, watchdog worker, retry classification, and dashboard/pendant status rendering; action adapters must emit requestId and step receipts consistently.
changes.risk: A bad retry classifier could repeat a mutation. Restrict automatic retries to explicitly read-only or idempotent open/inspect steps, and mark all other steps unresolved for the owner. Recover by stopping reconciliation and preserving raw receipts.
changes.cost_impact: Low background compute and storage; roughly <$0.01 per watched job. No realtime model call unless a final spoken explanation is requested.
changes.latency_impact: Adds a 5–15 second stale-job detection interval; no impact on the first action response.
changes.security_impact: Correlating browser URLs, filenames, and action history increases metadata sensitivity. Store only IDs/status/source hashes in the relay, keep detailed snippets local where possible, and enforce owner-scoped access.
depends_on: Consistent requestId/stepId propagation across /pipeline, /jobs, browser heartbeat, and Mac action receipts
A durable background scheduler/worker (not a realtime turn)
Typed action result metadata identifying read-only/idempotent steps

changes.change: Implement a cross-surface saga coordinator between the existing job, browser, and Mac bridges. A workflow record should map one owner request to ordered typed steps and external IDs (browser commandId, Mac jobId, pipelineId), persist compact input/output hashes and source provenance, lease each step with heartbeat/expiry, and expose resume/reconcile endpoints. On reconnect or worker restart, retry only explicitly idempotent steps; otherwise mark the step blocked and deliver a recovery receipt rather than duplicating a mutation. Add a single workflow status stream that merges browser heartbeat/results, Mac job receipts, and pendant pipeline events.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A request that spans a logged-in tab and the Mac will stop disappearing halfway through or running the same action twice after Wi‑Fi, browser, or laptop sleep. The owner gets one truthful status—completed, waiting on a named step, or safely abandoned—with a one-tap/voice resume path.
changes.effort: Medium-high: a durable state machine and storage schema, adapters for browser and Mac IDs, lease/retry worker, reconnect delivery, and failure-injection tests for sleeps, duplicate results, and late callbacks.
changes.risk: Incorrect reconciliation could replay a form submission or file deletion. Default unknown steps to blocked, require explicit idempotency keys for mutations, retain before/after hashes, and use existing job cancel/undo where available. If the coordinator is unavailable, current direct /execute and browser paths continue unchanged.
changes.cost_impact: Small persistent metadata and event-log cost per workflow; background reconciliation uses a cheap model only when semantic recovery is needed. No meaningful pendant hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: Initial acknowledgment unchanged; each step adds a sub-second durable checkpoint. Reconnect recovery becomes seconds rather than a lost 45-second blocking wait.
changes.security_impact: Workflow state can contain private URLs, snippets, and paths. Encrypt payloads, store hashes instead of raw content where possible, enforce per-session access, and expire sensitive checkpoints. Never expose secrets in spoken receipts.
depends_on: Existing browser request IDs/idempotency and tab affinity need a non-blocking progress/resume API (chg-14accc01 is still open specifically because browserBridge waits 45 seconds).
A stable typed Mac job receipt schema from /jobs/:jobId/receipts and /journal/:jobId.
A relay-to-pendant reconnect queue for completion and blocked-step notifications.

changes.change: Make browser execution offline-aware: before dispatch, consult the bridge heartbeat and return a typed unavailable state immediately when offline; move queued commands into a durable pending state with TTL and owner-visible count instead of holding an HTTP request for 45 seconds. When the extension heartbeats again, reconcile commands by idempotency key, emit progress, and expire stale reads safely. Keep mutations blocked from automatic replay and surface them as needing review.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner would hear “Safari is offline; I saved this task and will resume when it reconnects” in seconds instead of waiting 45 seconds for a failed request, and would never face five invisible pending commands or accidental duplicate browser actions.
changes.effort: Medium: bridge heartbeat gate, durable queue state transitions, non-blocking polling/SSE, idempotent result reconciliation, TTL cleanup, and tests for late/duplicate extension results.
changes.risk: A false offline report could delay a read; fail-open is unnecessary for reads because they can be resumed. A stale heartbeat could cause a mutation to be incorrectly replayed, so mutations must remain non-replayable unless explicitly proven idempotent. Preserve the existing direct path as fallback.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage/event overhead; no model calls required for the fast path.
changes.latency_impact: Offline failure goes from ~45 seconds to under 1 second; online commands retain current latency, with progress available during long operations.
changes.security_impact: Pending commands may contain private URLs or form data; encrypt or redact queue payloads, bind them to the browser session, and expire them. Do not speak sensitive page contents in the offline notice.
depends_on: Existing POST /browser/heartbeat, GET /browser/poll, POST /browser/result/:commandId, and GET /browser/status.
The resumable progress portion of chg-14accc01; its current 45-second blocking wait is directly observed live.
A durable command queue with per-command idempotency and session affinity.

changes.change: Add a device-local evidence gateway and enforce a redacted-envelope mode end to end. Browser and Mac adapters must extract source facts locally, classify sensitivity, redact or hash disallowed fields, and send the relay only a signed envelope of claims plus provenance. The relay/model router rejects raw page/file payloads when this mode is requested, and the dashboard exposes an export ledger of every field released.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They could ask questions about private work accounts and local documents without having to choose between usefulness and exporting their raw personal data. They would see exactly what crossed the device boundary and have a durable way to detect accidental over-sharing.
changes.effort: High: shared policy schema, local DOM/file extractors, signed envelope verification, router enforcement, redaction tests against secrets and re-identification, and dashboard UX.
changes.risk: Over-redaction can make answers incomplete; return an explicit missing-evidence explanation rather than silently guessing. A compromised local adapter could mislabel data, so the relay must verify envelope signatures and reject untyped payloads. Keep an owner-controlled unrestricted mode separate and visibly labeled.
changes.cost_impact: Lower model/API cost for large private sources because only compact evidence leaves the device; moderate engineering and local CPU cost for extraction/redaction; no hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 1–10 seconds of local extraction/redaction, but avoids repeated large-context uploads and can stream an initial evidence summary sooner.
changes.security_impact: Substantially reduces raw private-data exposure, but provenance and hashes can still leak correlation information; salt hashes per task, minimize metadata, encrypt local audit logs, and expire envelopes.
depends_on: A typed evidence-envelope format with provenance, sensitivity, confidence, expiry, and task purpose.
Local browser/Mac extraction and redaction libraries.
Relay-side schema enforcement and a visible export ledger; these do not exist in the current stack.

changes.change: Add a resumable action ledger shared by relay, Mac executor, and Safari browser bridge. Before dispatch, assign a durable workflowId and deterministic actionId per semantic step; persist step intent, backend, precondition fingerprint, attempt, status, and receipt. Commit the completion record atomically with the receipt. On link loss, restart, or extension sleep, the relay asks for the ledger and resumes at the first incomplete step; completed actionIds are skipped only when their postcondition/evidence still matches, otherwise the step is marked needs-reconciliation. For non-idempotent mutations, add an operation key passed to the bridge/Mac side and retain it until the workflow is terminal. Expose pause/resume/reconcile and a pendant-friendly progress event, not a blind whole-plan retry.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: If the Mac sleeps, Safari disconnects, or the pendant link drops halfway through 'collect these details, fill the form, save the file, and draft the reply,' the owner gets a truthful continuation instead of duplicate clicks, duplicate drafts, or uncertainty about what happened. They can leave a long task running and hear exactly which step completed and which needs attention.
changes.effort: Medium-high: a D1/R2 ledger and state machine in the relay, Mac job-store integration, browser bridge acknowledgement/postcondition protocol, recovery tests for crashes between side effect and receipt, and progress fan-out to pendant/dashboard.
changes.risk: The hard failure window is a side effect occurring before its completion record is committed; recovery must classify that step as unknown and inspect evidence rather than replay it. Stale fingerprints could incorrectly skip a step, so unknown or changed postconditions stop at reconciliation. Existing one-shot jobs remain compatible and can be imported as non-resumable terminal runs.
changes.cost_impact: Small persistent storage and a few relay writes per step; negligible model cost because recovery is deterministic. Additional browser polling/heartbeat traffic is minor.
changes.latency_impact: One ledger write and acknowledgement per step adds roughly tens of milliseconds locally and one network round trip for remote browser steps; retries become much faster and safer than restarting a long plan.
changes.security_impact: Ledger contains URLs, touched paths, and action metadata, so encrypt sensitive fields, minimize retention, and bind records to the owner/session. Never persist form secrets or page bodies; operation keys should be opaque.
depends_on: chg-5fc73ce3 receipt infrastructure (implemented but currently lacks checkpoints/preconditions)
chg-16bc5dee durable browser job runner (router exists; runner and result stream remain missing)
chg-14accc01 browser request IDs/idempotency and tab affinity (partially implemented)

changes.change: Implement the already-granted mac_readonly_inspect contract as a real local-agent state-witness endpoint/tool. Support running_apps, foreground_app, browser_tabs, accessibility_enabled, ui_snapshot (only when Screen Recording is granted), and bounded list_directory. Return timestamped, redacted, typed snapshots with a monotonic witnessId and explicit unavailable reasons; never infer current state from stale browser sessions or the jobs log. Add a pre/post witness attachment to every mac_run_actions receipt so the relay can reconcile whether a step actually changed the desktop.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner says 'continue that' or asks what is on screen, the pendant can tell the truth about the Mac and resume without stealing focus or replaying a stale browser command. Failed/offline browser work becomes an actionable 'extension offline / 5 commands pending' report instead of a misleading success.
changes.effort: Medium: local read-only inspectors plus receipt schema and tests; ui_snapshot needs the owner to enable Accessibility and Screen Recording, while the other inspectors can work with existing automation grants.
changes.risk: Snapshots may expose app names, URLs, window titles, or file names; default to redaction and bounded allowlisted paths, and attach only hashes/summaries to relay memory. If an inspector fails, mark witness unavailable and do not block ordinary actions. Recovery is retrying the witness and preserving the action receipt.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; local CPU only. Small storage increase for bounded witness summaries (roughly <10 KB per action).
changes.latency_impact: ~50-300 ms for app/foreground/browser inspection; ui_snapshot may add 0.5-2 s. Do not invoke vision unless explicitly needed.
changes.security_impact: Read-only local access; browser URLs and UI text are sensitive, so redact by default and require explicit scope for raw snapshots. No new arbitrary shell capability.
depends_on: Implement the granted mac_readonly_inspect tool (currently schema exists but returns 'no implementation yet')
Keep browser session IDs and extension heartbeat as freshness checks
Optional: owner enables Accessibility and Screen Recording for UI snapshots

changes.change: Add an Accessibility identity-integrity watchdog to the Mac agent. At startup and before any ui_* action, compare the bundle identity actually posting events (com.aipendant.agent), the authorized Accessibility identity, and the executable path; run a harmless zero-delta probe, persist the result as an input-reachability witness, and make receipts say 'not executed' when the probe fails. If mismatched, open the exact System Settings Privacy & Security > Accessibility pane and show the owner the one binary that must be enabled; after the owner changes it, re-probe and publish a new witness to the relay. Send only status/path hashes to the relay, never screen contents. This is observability and truthful execution, not an approval gate: FULL_CONTROL_MODE remains unchanged.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Right now ui_click/type_text can report success while doing nothing: live observation says Accessibility is untrusted because permission belongs to a different binary, and screen recording is also off. The owner would stop getting false claims that work was completed and could repair the Mac in one guided step.
changes.effort: Small-to-medium: local-agent permission module and receipt fields, a System Settings deep link, startup/periodic probe, and relay/dashboard status card; about 1–2 engineering days plus a few manual permission tests.
changes.risk: The probe must be side-effect-free and must not steal focus. A bad identity comparison could unnecessarily report unavailable; recover by retaining raw diagnostics locally and allowing a manual re-probe. Opening Settings is reversible and does not change permissions automatically.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a few local probes per hour and small status events. No hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 50–200 ms before UI actions when a cached healthy witness exists; a failed probe is reported immediately instead of wasting a 45-second UI action timeout.
changes.security_impact: Improves security posture by preventing untrusted UI receipts and exposing only bundle identifiers/path hashes upstream. It does not add a confirmation gate or reduce the owner's existing maximum-control policy.
depends_on: mac_readonly_inspect implementation or an equivalent local permission inspection path
A stable receipt schema for inputReachability witness IDs
Owner granting Accessibility to the exact AI Pendant Agent binary when they want UI automation

changes.change: Create a privacy-preserving cross-surface handoff capsule protocol. The Mac agent locally watches only foreground-app transitions, accessibility reachability, active browser session IDs, and action receipts—not continuous screen or microphone content. On an explicit pendant 'pause here' command, it snapshots a typed checkpoint: intent label, unfinished step, safe next action, provenance, sensitivity, expiry, and a cryptographic hash of the local encrypted payload. The relay routes the opaque capsule to the pendant and dashboard; on 'resume', Mac and browser must each issue fresh reachability/session witnesses before restoring context. Capsules become immutable after capture, support owner edits as a new version, and expire automatically.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can leave a task at the desk and pick it up from the pendant without losing the exact place or exposing an always-on recording of their screen. Today receipts show what happened, not what the owner meant to continue, so the next action has to be reconstructed manually.
changes.effort: Medium: define the capsule schema and versioning, add local encrypted storage and TTL cleanup, add relay routing and pendant/dashboard list/summarize/resume messages, and connect fresh Mac/browser witnesses to resume. Roughly 3–5 engineering days.
changes.risk: Foreground-app metadata can still be sensitive, and an incorrect inferred next step could cause confusion. Make explicit pause the default trigger, show the capsule summary before restore, keep the next step advisory unless explicitly resumed, and recover by deleting or reverting to an earlier capsule version.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible infrastructure cost; compact encrypted local records and small opaque relay records. One inexpensive summarization call only when the owner requests a spoken summary.
changes.latency_impact: Explicit capture under 3 seconds; list/metadata under 1 second; full summary 2–3 seconds. No continuous model or network inference loop.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy by excluding screen capture, microphone audio, cookies, and page bodies from the relay. Encrypt the local payload with the Mac keychain, use opaque IDs upstream, redact draft text by default, and enforce expiry/deletion.
depends_on: A durable local encrypted capsule store and schema
Pendant message intents for pause/list/summarize/resume/delete
Fresh witness fields from Mac input reachability and browser session heartbeat
A dashboard review surface

changes.change: Implement a reconnect-safe cross-surface execution lease and stale-command quarantine. When a plan originates from the pendant/relay, bind its job to a plan hash, browser tab/session (if any), Mac bridge instance, and short-lived nonce. The Mac bridge and browser extension may prepare/read and return evidence, but on reconnect they must first revalidate the lease and current tab URL/title/fingerprint; commands older than the lease or whose tab/session changed move to quarantined (not executed) with an explicit reason. Reconciliation should be idempotent by request ID, preserve receipts, and let the pendant ask to resume or discard. This is observability/reliability, not an approval gate, and must work with FULL_CONTROL_MODE owner policy.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: If the laptop sleeps, Chrome restarts, or Wi‑Fi drops while you say “handle this,” the system will not silently apply an old command to a different page or duplicate a submission. When you come back, you get a clear “paused because the page changed” result and can resume from the pendant or Mac instead of reconstructing the task.
changes.effort: Medium: shared lease schema in relay D1, bridge reconnect handshake, browser extension reattachment/fingerprint check, quarantine state and dashboard/pendant status messages, plus crash/replay tests.
changes.risk: A legitimate long-running job may pause after expiry; recovery is explicit resume against fresh evidence. Network partitions can leave a job pending, but idempotency prevents duplicate execution. No mutation is blocked permanently; it is only held when identity/evidence is stale.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a few D1 reads/writes and small status payloads per reconnect. Engineering cost is primarily protocol and replay testing.
changes.latency_impact: No added latency to ordinary connected reads; reconnect adds one handshake and evidence refresh, typically sub-second before resuming.
changes.security_impact: Reduces confused-deputy and replay risk by binding actions to device/session/tab identity and freshness. Lease metadata should avoid storing page content beyond existing receipts and use nonce hashes rather than raw secrets.
depends_on: Browser command queue with request IDs/idempotency/tab affinity (chg-14accc01)
Mac action receipts/undo records (chg-5fc73ce3)
Relay durable jobs and /jobs status routes
Browser extension reconnect status currently reported by /browser/status and /browser/sessions

changes.change: Implement the granted mac_readonly_inspect tool as a real read-only adapter over the existing /observe and narrowly scoped inspection routes. Support running_apps, foreground_app, accessibility_enabled, browser_tabs, and list_directory with bounded limits, and return an explicit implementationUnavailable error only for unsupported operations. Add a startup self-test that compares tool output with GET /observe without exposing bearer tokens or page bodies.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The system currently grants inspection in the interface but every call fails because there is no implementation. The owner and all agents therefore cannot reliably answer basic questions like what app is foreground, whether input can reach the screen, or whether the browser is connected. This is especially harmful because UI actions can report success while doing nothing.
changes.effort: Small-to-medium: implement the adapter, route mapping, bounds/redaction, and tests for the five operations; no new Mac permissions required for the non-UI observations already exposed by /observe.
changes.risk: A faulty adapter could over-report state or leak directory names. Keep it read-only, cap result sizes, use the existing /observe redaction policy, and return timestamps plus source route. Recovery is simply disabling the tool; existing execution paths are unaffected.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost and disk use; one local HTTP request per inspection.
changes.latency_impact: Typically under 200 ms locally; directory listings may take longer but remain bounded.
changes.security_impact: No additional authority. Do not implement this by shelling out arbitrary commands; use the existing authenticated agent routes and approved path validation.
depends_on: The tool schema already granted for mac_readonly_inspect
GET /observe is live and read-only
A small server-side mapping from operation names to observation fields

changes.change: Make execution authorization and pipeline status come from one shared policy/result object. A read-only research command currently reaches /pipeline as “Waiting for your approval” even though the live Mac agent reports FULL_CONTROL_MODE=true and the configured owner policy says no approval gate; add explicit action classes (read-only, reversible, destructive) for observability, execute according to the active policy, and emit the same class, decision, and reason in /jobs receipts, /pipeline events, and spoken status. Never claim “waiting for approval” when the action was actually uploaded and accepted.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner should not have to guess whether a request ran, is paused, or merely has a stale dashboard label. This fixes the concrete news-job failure and makes every future pendant-to-Mac action trustworthy without reducing access.
changes.effort: Medium: centralize the decision/result serializer used by POST /execute, job receipts, and pipeline event emission; add replay tests for read-only shell, reversible file action, and destructive mail/delete cases.
changes.risk: A policy mismatch could accidentally run or block an action. Recover with a compatibility flag, retain raw event history, and fail closed only on contradictory state while clearly reporting the contradiction.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible runtime/API cost; fewer unnecessary planner retries and approval round trips.
changes.latency_impact: Slightly lower latency for read-only work by removing the false approval wait; no added model call.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability and preserves the owner’s existing maximum-access policy; classification is telemetry, not an unrequested gate. Destructive actions remain labeled so the owner can inspect receipts.
depends_on: A single authoritative execution-policy configuration shared by local-agent and relay
Receipt schema that stores action class, decision, and evidence
Regression tests covering /execute and /pipeline together

changes.change: Replace the single nRF9160 development-kit audio/transport bottleneck in the wearable design with a two-processor audio architecture: a low-power audio MCU with DMA, larger RAM, and a timestamped 2–4 second bidirectional ring buffer handles 24 kHz playback/15.625 kHz capture, while the cellular/application processor handles LTE/TLS and relay protocol. Add a small hardware clock/timestamp boundary so queued PCM/Opus frames can be resumed and de-duplicated after modem stalls.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They would be able to speak naturally while the pendant is talking without the current LTE contention dropping roughly eight seconds of speech, and a brief coverage dip would sound like a short delay instead of losing the middle of the conversation.
changes.effort: High: select a production wearable audio MCU/codec and memory, redesign the board and power tree, define an inter-processor transport, then validate RF coexistence, thermal behavior, and end-to-end latency with real LTE-M traces.
changes.risk: More parts, firmware, and power domains create new failure modes; recover with watchdogs, a bypass mode that routes audio directly through the application processor, and a factory diagnostic that verifies clock/queue health before enabling the split path.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly $8–$20 added BOM at low volume plus board redesign; approximately 10–30 mW average for the audio subsystem depending on codec/DSP choice, potentially offset by letting the cellular processor sleep during playback.
changes.latency_impact: Adds about 1–5 ms of local buffering, but removes multi-second stalls and packet loss under simultaneous uplink/downlink; target conversational round-trip remains under 300 ms when coverage is good.
changes.security_impact: The audio MCU must not retain raw speech beyond the bounded ring buffer; secure-boot both processors, authenticate their firmware, and erase buffers on call end or pairing change.
depends_on: A production audio/transport protocol with frame sequence numbers and resume semantics
Measured LTE-M contention and battery targets for the intended enclosure
End-to-end 24 kHz relay/Opus acceptance tests on the replacement hardware

changes.change: Add an automatic observation sandwich around every ui_* action: capture /observe immediately before dispatch and again afterward, then enrich the existing action receipt with accessibilityTrusted, foregroundAppBefore/After, inputReachability, and verificationStatus (verified, unverified, or contradicted). Never block or require approval; if synthesized input is rejected, report the action as unverified instead of successful. For browser actions, attach the active session/tab identity and any evidence capsule ids to the same receipt.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner will stop hearing “done” when a click or keystroke actually did nothing. They get a truthful, concise result and can choose a retry or another route such as AppleScript, even while using the Mac themselves.
changes.effort: Medium: wrap computerControl dispatch and actionReceipt creation, persist two small observe snapshots per action, add dashboard/journal rendering and tests for Accessibility false, app focus changes, and browser-offline cases.
changes.risk: Extra observation could slightly increase action latency and may expose foreground-app names in logs; redact sensitive window titles and retain only bounded metadata. A post-action snapshot can still miss a fast transient, so label it verification rather than proof. Recovery is to fall back to the current receipt path if observation fails.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; two local probes per UI action. Small JSON growth in the job journal, bounded by retention.
changes.latency_impact: Approximately 50–200 ms per UI action locally; no model call.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without adding authority or gates. It should avoid storing screenshots or keystroke contents in the observation record.
depends_on: GET /observe is already live
Existing action receipts from chg-5fc73ce3
Owner’s accepted FULL_CONTROL_MODE/no-confirmation policy
A small receipt schema extension shared with the relay and dashboard

changes.change: Implement the granted mac_readonly_inspect and mac_read_sources tools in the local agent as bounded, redacted adapters. Use AppleScript/JXA through the already-granted per-app automation permissions for foreground/running apps, Safari/Chrome tab metadata, Calendar, and Mail; return typed records with timestamps and source app. Add a capability/status field so callers can distinguish implemented, unavailable, and permission-denied instead of receiving a generic tool error.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask for a truthful work brief or resume a task without the agent guessing from stale machine-context data. It also lets the pendant hear what is actually open while the owner is away, without screen recording or Accessibility.
changes.effort: Medium: local-agent route handlers, allowlisted scripts, redaction tests, timeout handling, and contract tests for empty/denied accounts. No model work required.
changes.risk: AppleScript can expose sensitive subject lines or URLs; default to metadata/snippets and redact bodies. A hung app can block collection, so enforce per-source timeouts and return partial results. Recovery is retrying one source; never mutate apps in these handlers.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; local CPU only. A few hundred bytes to a few KB per query, depending on tab/mail counts.
changes.latency_impact: Roughly 0.2–2 s for app/tab metadata and 1–4 s for Calendar/Mail, with parallel collection and hard timeouts.
changes.security_impact: Read-only allowlists, account_scope validation, body exclusion by default, URL/query redaction, and audit receipts. No Accessibility or Screen Recording grant is needed for the initial implementation.
depends_on: The local agent's existing AppleScript automation grant cache
A documented response schema for mac_readonly_inspect/mac_read_sources
Browser lease/epoch fencing before authenticated tab data is trusted

changes.change: Add reconnect fencing for the browser bridge: every heartbeat issues a device epoch and lease token; poll claims must include that epoch; commands claimed by an offline or expired extension are quarantined, never replayed automatically, and require explicit reattachment to the same session/tab before retry. Expose pending, quarantined, expired, and replayed counts in /browser/status and dashboard.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner will not accidentally navigate or submit an old command when Chrome reconnects after sleep, a crash, or extension replacement. Today the bridge is offline while five commands remain pending and one has been repeatedly claimed, so reconnect behavior is unsafe and opaque.
changes.effort: Medium: schema fields and atomic claim/update logic in browser queue, heartbeat/poll/result validation, migration for existing pending records, and dashboard state labels.
changes.risk: A legitimate command may be quarantined and need retry. Provide a one-click or spoken 'reattach this browser session' operation, preserve the command and reason, and never delete it silently.
changes.cost_impact: Tiny D1 read/write increase per heartbeat and command claim; no model calls.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one token/epoch validation per poll/result, normally sub-10 ms; reconnect may take one heartbeat before work resumes.
changes.security_impact: Improves session binding and prevents cross-device replay. Store only hashes of lease tokens in D1; invalidate all leases on extension identity change or prolonged offline interval.
depends_on: Existing GET /browser/status
GET /browser/heartbeat
GET /browser/poll
POST /browser/result/:commandId
POST /browser/sessions
The command queue and browser session records already identified by chg-14accc01

changes.change: Add a durable Meeting Continuity Orchestrator keyed by Calendar event ID. It schedules a preflight job, fans out bounded reads from Calendar/Mail/local workspace and the authenticated browser, stores source-cited packet sections and a redacted digest, emits a short audio item, then transitions on event end or a pendant “done” signal into a follow-up draft job. Persist idempotent checkpoints and receipts so a Mac sleep, relay restart, or duplicate trigger cannot create duplicate drafts. Keep outbound mutations as explicit draft-only outputs.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets one dependable “ready me / wrap this up” experience instead of separate calendar, browser, notes, and audio features that each work only when manually invoked.
changes.effort: Medium-high: a server-side state machine and scheduler, Mac read adapter implementation, browser job persistence/reattachment, and a small pendant event protocol; most extraction and speech primitives already exist.
changes.risk: Wrong event matching or stale browser content could produce an irrelevant packet; mitigate with event-ID binding, freshness timestamps, source links, confidence labels, and a “no packet” fallback. Duplicate triggers are handled by idempotency keys. Outbound actions remain drafts and require explicit confirmation.
changes.cost_impact: About $0.01–$0.05 per meeting for background summarization/browser extraction; storage is small redacted JSON plus short audio with TTL. No continuous realtime model spend.
changes.latency_impact: Preflight runs asynchronously and should be ready 10 minutes before the event; post-meeting draft target is under 2 minutes. No impact on normal pendant conversation.
changes.security_impact: Private calendar/mail/browser evidence is minimized and redacted before relay persistence; authenticated pages are read only. No email/calendar/browser submission without owner confirmation; packet/audio retention should default to 24 hours.
depends_on: Implementation (not just schemas) for mac_read_sources and mac_readonly_inspect
Durable browser job runner and result stream (chg-16bc5dee remaining gap)
A pendant offline-safe meeting-ended/follow-up capture event
Relay audio queue with retry and expiry

changes.change: Create a cross-surface Attention Ledger and delivery arbiter. Normalize every candidate interruption (mail, calendar changes, browser watches, Mac jobs, relay jobs) into an event with source evidence, urgency, deadline, confidence, duplicate keys, expiry, and delivery history. Join it with current activity/meeting state and owner-set quiet windows, then choose one channel (pendant audio, Mac notification, queued digest) or defer. Add a pendant-local override: urgent-only, mute, and deliver-now, with local state replayed when connectivity returns.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can stay focused without manually silencing several agents, while time-critical changes still reach them through the one device they are wearing. Deferred information arrives once, grouped and explained, rather than as repeated alerts.
changes.effort: High integration effort: event schema and durable ledger, adapters from existing job/browser/briefing systems, deterministic policy plus lightweight ranking, relay scheduler, and a small offline pendant state machine.
changes.risk: Bad urgency ranking could suppress something important or interrupt unnecessarily. Mitigate with conservative deadlines/sender rules, visible rationale, expiry, an urgent override, replayable receipts, and a daily audit showing what was deferred. Recovery is ledger replay after restart or link loss.
changes.cost_impact: Low ongoing storage (small event records with short TTL); roughly $0.005–$0.03 per batch for ranking, with deterministic rules handling the common case. No continuous realtime inference.
changes.latency_impact: Urgent candidates classified within 30 seconds; delivery under 2 seconds after classification. Digest generation is asynchronous and does not delay normal conversation.
changes.security_impact: Ledger stores redacted metadata and hashes rather than full message/page bodies by default. Source content stays on the Mac/browser session unless the owner asks for detail. No outbound mutation is permitted by the arbiter.
depends_on: An implemented read-only Mac activity/calendar adapter rather than the currently schema-only grants
A common event-ingestion API for browser watches, Mac job receipts, Mail/Calendar reads, and relay jobs
Pendant-local mute/defer/urgent override with reconnect replay
Relay audio queue with deduplication, expiry, and retry

changes.change: Add a cross-surface action lease and reconciliation protocol shared by relay, Mac planner, and browser bridge. Every requested mutation gets one durable intent ID and semantic idempotency key before dispatch; relay owns the lease, Mac/browser claim it with a heartbeat, and receipts include precondition hash, effect summary, and terminal state. If the pendant retries after a dropped connection, the relay returns the existing receipt instead of dispatching a second action. If a worker disappears mid-step, mark the intent uncertain and run a read-only reconciliation probe before allowing continuation.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A spoken “send it,” “move that file,” or “book this” will happen once—not twice—when Wi‑Fi, the browser extension, or the Mac bridge drops at the worst moment. The owner gets a clear spoken result such as completed, not started, or needs review instead of guessing whether to retry.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared intent schema and D1/local persistence, lease heartbeats, adapters for Mac job receipts and browser command IDs, plus reconciliation handlers for common actions.
changes.risk: A false precondition or incomplete receipt could incorrectly report an action as complete, while an overly cautious uncertain state may delay a legitimate action. Keep uncertain terminal states explicit, never auto-repeat high-impact mutations, and provide an inspectable receipt timeline and manual retry.
changes.cost_impact: Low relay storage and a few metadata writes per action; negligible model cost. Reconciliation may add one local read or browser query, not a model call in the normal path.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly one metadata round trip (tens to low hundreds of ms); retries become faster because they resolve from the receipt. Reconciliation is only on failures.
changes.security_impact: Intent records contain sensitive targets and URLs; encrypt or minimize payloads, retain hashes rather than full contents, scope records to the paired owner, and do not expose browser credentials or message bodies to the relay.
depends_on: Existing Mac job receipts/undo records and browser request IDs/session affinity
A relay-side durable intent table and event stream
Typed result schemas from the Mac and browser adapters

changes.change: Create a Mac-resident privacy boundary between browser/file readers and every server-side planner. It should accept extraction requests, perform source reads locally, classify each field (safe derived fact, sensitive, secret), redact or aggregate locally, hash the original evidence, and emit a signed outbound manifest containing only the permitted facts and provenance. Relay and dashboard should render the manifest and hashes as a privacy receipt; raw evidence stays on the Mac and is deleted according to a short TTL unless the owner explicitly asks to retain it.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can safely ask one mind to combine authenticated browser information with local documents without having to trust an invisible upload. They can hear exactly what was used and what crossed the Mac/server boundary, while still getting the benefit of unified reasoning.
changes.effort: High: local broker API and policy engine, browser/Mac adapter hooks, signed manifest schema, relay verification, receipt UI/audio, and deletion tests.
changes.risk: Misclassification could leak sensitive content or make an answer incomplete. Default-deny unknown fields, expose unavailable/redacted states, preserve local evidence hashes for audit, and allow a retry with a narrower or explicitly authorized scope.
changes.cost_impact: Small local CPU/storage overhead and one compact relay receipt per task; raw-content model calls become less frequent and therefore cheaper.
changes.latency_impact: Adds local classification and hashing, usually under 300 ms; parallel extraction keeps normal tasks interactive. Explicit raw-content escalation is slower and clearly marked.
changes.security_impact: Reduces data leaving the Mac, provides tamper-evident provenance, and avoids copying credentials or full authenticated pages to the relay. Requires secure local key storage and careful receipt minimization.
depends_on: A shared typed extraction result format for Mac and browser
Local implementations of the granted read-only source and inspection adapters
Relay verification and dashboard rendering for signed privacy manifests

changes.change: Implement a signed, versioned Resume Capsule coordinator. On pause or any long-running job checkpoint, write a compact manifest containing goal/constraints, last completed action, pending action class, Mac jobId plus receipt, app/file references, browser session+tab IDs with evidence hashes, relay job state, and pendant audio/message offsets. Store immutable checkpoints with a short TTL and append-only transitions. On continue, fan out read-only probes first, compare current state to the manifest, present a concise drift report, and only then replay idempotent open/read/fill-preparation steps; mark every restored step with the capsule ID.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can stop mid-task, close the lid, or lose the browser connection and later pick up without guessing what was already done or accidentally repeating a mutation. Drift warnings prevent acting on stale prices, forms, meetings, or files.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and relay persistence, Mac job/checkpoint hooks, browser session rebinding, pendant command/state handling, and a small drift/diff service. Start with JSON manifests and receipts before adding richer UI.
changes.risk: Stale or duplicated actions are the main risk. Mitigate with idempotency keys, read-only revalidation, explicit distinction between prepared and committed mutations, expiry, and recovery to a review-only state if any surface changed. If relay is unavailable, retain the last capsule locally and sync later.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage; roughly $0.005–$0.03 for background drift summarization per resume, with browser extraction the dominant cost. No new per-action realtime call.
changes.latency_impact: Adds 1–3 seconds for checkpoint writes and 2–8 seconds for parallel revalidation; avoids much longer manual recovery.
changes.security_impact: Capsules are sensitive cross-surface metadata. Encrypt and minimize snippets, redact mail bodies by default, scope browser tokens to existing sessions, bind manifests to device identity, and audit reads/restores. Never encode secrets such as captured owner credentials.
depends_on: Durable browser job runner and result stream (chg-16bc5dee remains incomplete)
A relay durable capsule endpoint and Mac/browser idempotency-key propagation
Implementation of the newly granted read-only Mac inspection/source tools (currently schema-only)
Browser extension recovery/rebinding when Safari bridge is offline
A pendant offline pause/continue queue or equivalent local intent persistence

changes.change: Replace the prototype nRF9160 DK's single LED/button feedback with a product pendant that includes a small tri-color status LED or sunlight-readable e-ink privacy indicator, a vibration motor, and a secure-element-backed link-status counter. The pendant should show distinct hardware-confirmed states—mic/audio active, relay connected, Mac/browser command lease active, and privacy-paused—using tactile/visual patterns that remain meaningful when the phone or Mac display is unavailable. The secure element signs state transitions so the relay and Mac can distinguish a real pendant gesture from a replayed network event.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can know immediately, without opening a screen or trusting a spoken claim, whether the wearable is listening, connected, or still able to trigger private Mac/browser work. This is especially valuable while walking away from an authenticated Mac: a physical indicator gives a trustworthy answer even when Chrome is offline or the relay is unreachable.
changes.effort: New pendant PCB/enclosure revision, secure-element provisioning, low-power LED/e-ink and haptic drivers, firmware state machine, and relay/Mac verification of signed monotonic counters. Requires a product hardware prototype and testing across LTE dropouts, reboot, and low battery.
changes.risk: Added parts increase enclosure complexity and power draw; an ambiguous indicator could create false confidence. Fail closed: unknown, stale, or unverifiable state must display an unmistakable warning pattern rather than 'private.' Recover with a hardware reset and re-pairing flow that preserves no page or audio content.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly $3–$10 BOM increase for secure element, haptic motor, driver, and indicator (more for e-ink); approximately 1–8 mA while indicating/vibrating, with deep-sleep nearly unchanged. No per-invocation API cost.
changes.latency_impact: Gesture acknowledgement can be local in under 300 ms; signed state propagation adds roughly one network round trip when connected. E-ink updates are slower but need only change on state transitions.
changes.security_impact: Improves authenticity and observability of privacy state through hardware-rooted signatures and monotonic anti-replay counters. It does not itself prevent a compromised Mac from misbehaving, so the indicator must distinguish 'Mac acknowledged' from merely 'relay requested.'
depends_on: A defined cross-surface privacy-state protocol with explicit per-surface acknowledgements
Product pendant redesign beyond the current nRF9160 development kit
Firmware support for signed state events and low-power feedback
Relay and Mac bridge verification of the pendant's counter and state signature

changes.change: Make the wearable’s audio path genuinely 24 kHz end to end: use a microphone/ADC and I2S clocking mode that captures 24 kHz (48 kHz wire clock with 24-bit slots), move Opus uplink to 24 kHz rather than the current 15.625 kHz capture/16 kHz stream, keep 24 kHz decode, and teach the ESP32 bridge and relay to pass 24 kHz frames without a hidden downsample. Add a small hardware DSP/codec offload or select a production MCU with enough DSP headroom; the current nRF9160 prototype spends roughly 87% of a core when encode and decode overlap.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets natural, consistent wideband speech in both directions instead of high-quality playback fed by a narrowband uplink. This directly fulfills the stated 24 kHz superwideband goal and makes queued briefings and live conversation sound like one system.
changes.effort: High: choose and validate a 24 kHz-capable digital microphone/codec, retune I2S clocks and DMA, update fixed-point Opus frame/rate settings, relay transcoding, bridge framing, jitter buffering, and run RF-loss/long-call tests. Keep a negotiated 16 kHz fallback for the current prototype.
changes.risk: The nRF9160’s CPU and RAM budget may cause underruns, modem contention, or battery drain; a bad clock configuration can create drift or aliasing. Recover with explicit capability negotiation, watchdog-triggered fallback to 16 kHz, frame-loss concealment, and telemetry for encode/decode occupancy. Do not silently label 16 kHz audio as 24 kHz.
changes.cost_impact: Prototype firmware/relay work is modest API cost (under $0.05 per test call); production hardware likely adds roughly $3–$12 per unit for a codec/DSP or upgraded MCU plus $1–$4 for a suitable microphone/clocking solution. Power rises during active audio, likely tens of milliwatts depending on the chosen offload.
changes.latency_impact: A 24 kHz Opus path can retain 40–60 ms frames; expect no material conversational latency increase if offloaded. On the current MCU, software-only operation risks 20–50 ms additional buffering and underruns, so it should not ship without measured headroom.
changes.security_impact: No new content leaves the device beyond the existing encrypted audio stream, but audio diagnostics must report only rates, packet loss, and CPU occupancy—not raw audio. Capability negotiation should be authenticated so a peer cannot force an unsupported mode or exhaust battery.
depends_on: A production audio hardware decision based on measured nRF9160 headroom
End-to-end relay and ESP32 bridge sample-rate negotiation
A/B audio quality and battery test harness under LTE contention
Offline queued-audio format/versioning so 24 kHz clips remain playable and can downgrade safely

changes.change: Add a live 'audio contract' panel and pendant status event that reports negotiated uplink/downlink sample rates, codec mode, packet-loss concealment, jitter-buffer depth, and whether the call is in true 24 kHz mode or the 16 kHz fallback. Show a one-line spoken/LED indication only on transitions (for example, 'wideband restored' or 'fallback audio') and attach the same metrics to each audio receipt.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can trust what they are hearing and immediately know whether a weak LTE link or prototype limitation degraded a call. It prevents the current failure mode where 24 kHz playback makes a narrowband uplink sound as if the whole conversation were wideband.
changes.effort: Medium: define a signed negotiated-mode event, relay metrics aggregation, a small dashboard card, and two pendant transition states; no raw audio needs to be stored.
changes.risk: Too many status announcements would be distracting, and stale metrics could mislead. Announce only mode changes, mark telemetry freshness, and make the dashboard explicit when values are estimates or unavailable.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible model/API cost; a few bytes per call event and minimal dashboard storage. No meaningful hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: No added conversational latency; mode-change status can be emitted asynchronously.
changes.security_impact: Telemetry must exclude content and identifiers beyond a short call/job ID. Authenticate mode events so a relay or browser intermediary cannot falsely claim wideband quality.
depends_on: End-to-end sample-rate negotiation and 24 kHz implementation
A signed audio receipt schema shared by pendant, bridge, relay, and Mac dashboard

changes.change: Ship a cross-surface Task Capsule service between relay, Mac planner, and browser bridge. On every long-running or interrupted job, persist a compact capsule keyed by a user-visible thread ID: current goal, last successful step, pending steps, Mac app/window references, browser session/tab IDs, file paths, evidence hashes, timestamps, and expiry. Add POST /capsules, GET /capsules/:id, POST /capsules/:id/resume, and DELETE /capsules/:id. Resume must validate that apps/tabs/files still exist, produce a dry-run plan, then invoke the existing /execute path and append receipts to the existing job journal. Implement the already-granted mac_readonly_inspect/mac_read_sources bridges so capsule capture can observe state without using the mutating executor.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: After walking away, losing LTE, or saying “not now,” the owner can return to the exact unfinished work instead of explaining it again or risking duplicate actions. They see what is stale and what will reopen before anything is sent or submitted.
changes.effort: Medium-high: relay schema and retention, Mac read-only adapters, browser evidence normalization, resume planner, and tests for stale tabs/files and duplicate execution.
changes.risk: A capsule could expose private browser or file metadata, or resume against a changed page. Mitigate with metadata-first storage, redaction, encryption, short TTL, stale-reference checks, idempotency keys, and never auto-submit external mutations. Recovery is DELETE capsule plus existing job cancel/undo where supported; failed steps remain in the journal.
changes.cost_impact: Small persistent storage and hashing cost; roughly $0.01–$0.05 per model-assisted capture/resume, with metadata-only refreshes usually below that. No pendant hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: Capture is near-instant for hashes/metadata; model summarization runs asynchronously. Resume confirmation target is under 3 seconds, with reopening and verification continuing via receipts.
changes.security_impact: Adds a sensitive artifact class. Encrypt at rest, bind to owner/session, redact bodies by default, log every read/resume, enforce TTL, and support explicit “forget this thread.” Browser cookies/tokens never enter the capsule.
depends_on: Actual implementations for mac_readonly_inspect and mac_read_sources (currently schema-only despite being granted)
Stable browser tab/session identity and extraction receipts
A relay-to-pendant thread-reference protocol
Idempotent job execution and durable journal linkage

changes.change: Add a tiny priority control plane on the pendant WebSocket: task/capsule references, acknowledgements, cancellation, and resume tokens use a separate sequenced queue from audio frames. Under LTE-M contention, downlink control packets pre-empt optional speech playback, are retried idempotently from RAM, and are persisted to the existing microSD failure buffer only when the link is down. Include a monotonic device sequence and expiry so a delayed “resume” cannot execute twice.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A dropped or overlapped voice connection will not lose the one short instruction that ties the owner to unfinished Mac/browser work. They can walk away and later say “resume” without creating duplicate jobs or repeating sensitive actions.
changes.effort: Medium firmware and relay protocol change: frame type, bounded queue, reconnect replay, sequence tests, and relay deduplication. It must fit the current prototype rather than assume a new SoC.
changes.risk: Queue corruption or replay could produce a stale command. Bound the queue, authenticate every envelope, expire tokens, require the relay to acknowledge a job ID, and treat unknown/expired references as no-ops with a spoken failure. SD wear is controlled by only writing undelivered control envelopes.
changes.cost_impact: No per-call model cost and negligible additional LTE bytes. Uses a few KB of the existing 211,608 B application RAM; no hardware BOM change.
changes.latency_impact: Control acknowledgements should arrive in under a second when LTE is available; speech may be interrupted or delayed slightly because control is prioritized.
changes.security_impact: Control envelopes must be TLS-protected and nonces/sequence numbers checked. Do not put page text, credentials, or file contents on the pendant—only opaque capsule IDs and short status codes.
depends_on: A relay capsule/job reference API
Existing WebSocket reconnect and SD fallback path
Relay-side idempotency and receipt linkage
A durable pendant-to-thread reference mechanism

changes.change: Introduce a signed, short-lived global execution lease with an epoch counter. Every Mac and browser action must carry the current epoch and check it before each step; a pendant emergency gesture increments the epoch, cancels queued jobs, invalidates browser command leases, and causes workers to stop at the next safe boundary. Persist a per-action terminal receipt (prevented, interrupted, completed, or unknown) and require an explicit re-enable operation to issue a new epoch.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets a real emergency brake across all automation surfaces, including work already handed off to a background worker. They can stop the system from the pendant and later know exactly what did and did not happen, instead of guessing whether a command is still running.
changes.effort: High distributed-systems work: relay lease authority, worker checks, pendant envelope/reconnect handling, cancellation adapters, race-condition tests, and dashboard incident history.
changes.risk: A network partition may prevent immediate cancellation on an offline Mac, and stopping mid-step may leave a partial local mutation. Use bounded check intervals, local deny-new-work state, idempotency keys, explicit unknown outcomes, and never claim rollback of an external action. Recovery is a new epoch plus deliberate re-enable.
changes.cost_impact: No meaningful model cost; small durable relay state and one tiny control message per job step. No hardware cost if the existing button/LED is used, though a production pendant should add haptic confirmation.
changes.latency_impact: Adds a sub-100 ms local lease check per action and typically under 1 second over the live link; offline surfaces can only enforce stop when reachable.
changes.security_impact: This becomes a high-value control channel: authenticate the pendant, bind it to the owner, rotate keys, reject replays, audit every epoch change, and keep the emergency gesture local/offline-capable.
depends_on: A firmware emergency-stop gesture and signed envelope
Mac and browser workers checking the lease before every side effect
Durable action receipts with explicit unknown state
A reconnect protocol that delivers the latest revoked epoch before accepting work

changes.change: Add a durable Context Handoff Job protocol between pendant/relay, browser bridge, and Mac planner. A job has a triggerId, source allowlist, per-source TTL, sensitivity/redaction policy, evidence records (surface, tabId/app, URL/path, observedAt, content hash), and a deterministic output manifest. The relay fans out bounded reads to mac_read_sources and the browser bridge, polls Mac job receipts, runs redaction/summary in the background tier, writes an atomic Markdown+JSON packet under ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace/handoffs/<id>/, and publishes a compact audio summary plus a dashboard link. If any source is offline, the packet is still committed with explicit gaps and a retryable status rather than silently mixing stale context.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Task switching stops losing the state of work. The owner gets a trustworthy, resumable handoff rather than a vague AI summary, and can see exactly which calendar/mail/tab/file observations support it.
changes.effort: Medium: shared schema, relay durable job state, Mac atomic writer, browser current-tab extraction, redaction tests, and pendant queue integration.
changes.risk: Authenticated page text or private mail could be persisted incorrectly, or stale observations could look current. Mitigate with source allowlists, short TTLs, field-level sensitivity labels, hashes/provenance, explicit partial status, and a one-command delete/undo of the packet. Failure recovery resumes by triggerId without duplicating files.
changes.cost_impact: Small background-model and storage cost per handoff; no realtime generation beyond the trigger acknowledgment. Local disk usage is bounded by a configurable retention sweep.
changes.latency_impact: Immediate acknowledgment; 5–15 seconds for a complete packet, with durable completion notification if a source is slow.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by making provenance and redaction mandatory at the integration boundary; it does not expand permissions beyond existing read-only Calendar/Mail/browser access and local file writing.
depends_on: Implementation of mac_readonly_inspect or an equivalent foreground-tab read route
A relay durable-job/audio-queue endpoint for asynchronous completion
Browser bridge current-tab bounded extraction with provenance
Atomic local packet writer and packet retention/delete policy

changes.change: Create a cross-source commitment reconciliation layer. Normalize Calendar events, Mail commitments, and authenticated browser records into typed claims (subject, time range, location, status, source, observedAt, confidence), cluster claims by entity, detect conflicts and supersession, and emit an evidence bundle rather than a single merged fact. Add explicit source-precedence rules, freshness windows, and an owner-resolvable 'accept this source' decision that records the decision without altering the underlying systems.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask whether a plan is still valid and receive an honest answer when systems disagree, instead of acting on a stale calendar entry or missing an email change.
changes.effort: Medium-to-high: schema and normalization, browser extraction contract, conflict classifier, evidence UI/audio rendering, and tests for timezone, recurring events, cancellations, and duplicate reservations.
changes.risk: Incorrect entity matching or precedence could produce false certainty. Always expose competing claims, use uncertainty language, expire stale claims, and never mutate source systems from reconciliation alone. Recovery is to discard the derived bundle and recompute from fresh reads.
changes.cost_impact: Small durable storage cost; background model calls are modest but scale with the number of sources and claims compared.
changes.latency_impact: Adds several seconds for parallel reads and normalization; realtime response should remain a brief acknowledgement while the background job completes.
changes.security_impact: Creates a sensitive derived view combining Mail, Calendar, and private browser data. Encrypt or access-control evidence bundles, minimize retained snippets, apply field-level redaction, and provide deletion/retention controls.
depends_on: Typed browser extraction with provenance
Shared temporal/entity normalization library
Durable reconciliation job and evidence-bundle storage
Dashboard and pendant rendering for competing claims

changes.change: Implement a redacted cross-surface handoff coordinator as a durable job type. It should fan out bounded Calendar/Mail reads, an authenticated browser extraction request, and a read-only Mac workspace inspection; normalize each result into {source, observedAt, sensitivity, citation, confidence, expiry}; redact before relay storage; produce a Markdown/JSON packet and an audio item; attach both to one jobId with receipts, partial-failure states, retry limits, and DELETE-by-job retention cleanup. A pendant request should create the job and receive progress events, not resend raw source context on every turn.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask once, hands-free, and get a trustworthy current state even when one source is unavailable. They see exactly where each fact came from, can review the packet on the Mac, and do not get stale or silently fabricated answers when the browser is offline.
changes.effort: Medium-high: a relay fan-out state machine, redaction/provenance schema, Mac adapter, browser timeout/reconnect handling, packet/audio writers, and dashboard/pendant progress UI. Start with read-only sources and a 10-second deadline.
changes.risk: Partial results could be mistaken for complete results; prevent this with a prominent completeness banner and per-source status. Browser page content may contain secrets or prompt injection; isolate extraction, strip instructions, and never execute page-provided actions. Crashes could leave artifacts; use idempotency keys and TTL cleanup. Recovery is retrying only failed source branches or deleting the job.
changes.cost_impact: Low per invocation beyond existing reads; background summarization and TTS dominate, roughly $0.01–$0.04. Storage is small (typically <100 KB packet plus audio) and should expire automatically.
changes.latency_impact: Parallel fan-out keeps typical completion under 10 seconds; browser offline path completes in 2–3 seconds with an explicit unavailable marker. Progress acknowledgement is sub-second.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by making redaction, provenance, TTL, and source boundaries mandatory. No form submission or external sharing. Raw Mail/browser bodies remain on-device when feasible; relay receives only selected redacted excerpts.
depends_on: Implement mac_read_sources and mac_readonly_inspect rather than schema-only stubs
Browser bridge online/reconnect and bounded authenticated extraction endpoint
A relay durable job schema with partial completion and deletion/retention controls
Existing /briefing, /research, /capture, pipeline audio, and job receipt primitives

changes.change: Add a deterministic duplex budget governor to the live WebSocket: reserve a minimum uplink budget for pendant capture, classify each 60 ms downlink frame by urgency, and when acknowledgements/loss exceed thresholds, stop enqueueing nonessential TTS frames, switch the transcoder to the negotiated fallback profile, and emit a signed session QoS event. On recovery, require 10 seconds of hysteresis before restoring 24 kHz. The relay should also attach a short continuity marker (sequence range and profile transition) so the pendant and Mac receipt can say exactly what was degraded.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant stops competing with the assistant's speech for the same constrained radio link. The owner hears a complete answer more often, and if a transition still occurs they get an honest, concise indication rather than unexplained silence or clipped speech.
changes.effort: Medium: relay scheduler/transcoder changes, firmware profile negotiation, deterministic contention tests, and a small dashboard panel. No new model training.
changes.risk: Bad thresholds could make speech sound lower quality too often or cause profile flapping; hysteresis, bounded profiles, and a simulated loss test recover safely. If the relay crashes, the current fixed 24 kHz path remains the fallback. Never discard uplink frames solely to improve downlink quality.
changes.cost_impact: No meaningful API increase; modest relay CPU and a few QoS events per call. Firmware RAM about 1.5 KB for counters/profile state; no raw audio retention.
changes.latency_impact: Profile changes add at most one 60 ms frame and relay scheduling (<300 ms target); recovery waits for a 10-second stable window by design.
changes.security_impact: Encrypted audio path remains unchanged. QoS events carry sequence numbers/counters only, with rotating session IDs and short retention.
depends_on: pendant duplex_audio_congestion_guard skill
A negotiated Opus profile identifier shared by firmware and cloud-relay/opusTranscode.js
POST /pipeline/events accepting typed QoS events and durable audio receipts
An end-to-end half-duplex contention test harness

changes.change: For the wearable revision, separate radio/control from audio timing: retain the LTE-M modem but add a small audio companion (or an SoC with a hardware audio/DSP block and DMA) responsible for I2S capture/playback, Opus encode/decode buffering, and congestion counters. Give it independent 24 kHz playback timing and at least 256 KB audio-working RAM, while the modem MCU handles TLS and policy.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Full-quality speech will not collapse merely because the pendant is simultaneously encoding their voice, decoding a reply, and servicing the modem. It creates enough headroom for the adaptive path instead of making the owner choose between clarity and connectivity.
changes.effort: High and product-level: schematic/PCB/firmware port, power and RF validation, enclosure redesign, and a real wearable prototype rather than the current DK.
