transcript.text:
Round 97 findings:

- Mac agent is online and fully controlled; relay is reachable.
- Browser bridge is currently **offline** with **5 pending commands**, so authenticated browser workflows cannot reliably resume yet.
- Accessibility and Screen Recording remain disabled. AppleScript automation is available, but UI/vision interaction is not.
- The newly granted `mac_read_sources` and `mac_readonly_inspect` tools are only schemas at present; they have no implementation.
- The pendant is still a prototype nRF9160 DK with one button/LED and 211 KB application RAM, so cancellation/status signaling must remain very small and local.

I recorded two new items:

1. **“Do this when I’m free”** — stage work, wait for a safe Calendar/foreground/idle window, execute through Mac/browser, and report completion or cancellation on the pendant.
2. **Interruption-aware deferred-job coordinator** — durable eligibility rules, leases, retries, pendant cancellation, browser reconnect handling, and existing job receipts/undo integration.

What I still need for that capability:

1. A durable deferred-job state machine and worker, distinct from the immediate `/jobs` queue.
2. Implementations for bounded Calendar/Mail reads and read-only Mac context inspection.
3. Browser extension reconnection and reliable command acknowledgements.
4. Pendant protocol support for queued/running/completed/error states and one-button cancellation.
5. A dashboard showing eligibility, TTL, current lease, and receipts.
6. If UI-state or vision evidence is required, the owner must manually enable Accessibility and Screen Recording for **AI Pendant Agent**. I will not re-request those permissions from the orchestrator.

args.user_asks: “I’m leaving the Mac—package this exactly so I can resume it from the pendant later.” Preserve the current Mac app/document state, authenticated browser tabs, unsent drafts, evidence, and next safe step; let me ask the pendant what is waiting and resume or abandon it when I return.
args.why_useful: Today a task is split across a browser session, Mac files/apps, and conversation history; walking away loses the working set or forces the owner to reconstruct it. A resumable handoff would make the pendant a true continuation of the Mac rather than a separate voice endpoint. It is specifically a state-preservation and restoration capability, not a generic background job or page watch.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to summarize and validate the handoff capsule. Use realtime only when the owner asks the pendant for status or gives resume/abandon commands. Use a stronger model only to resolve conflicting state during restoration.
args.latency_budget: Create a capsule in under 5 seconds after the owner says to leave. Pendant status should answer in under 2 seconds. Restore should begin within 10 seconds of returning the Mac, with a clear partial-restore report.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.003–$0.02 per handoff, dominated by optional document/browser summarization. Deterministic file manifests, app identifiers, tab metadata, and action receipts should avoid model calls.
args.security_concerns: Capsules may contain private file paths, authenticated tab identifiers, drafts, and snippets. Encrypt them, keep the default retention short, bind browser data to the original session, exclude passwords/tokens and full page bodies unless explicitly requested, and provide a physical pendant abandon/delete command. Restoration must never silently send, submit, or delete anything.
missing: A cross-surface handoff-capsule schema with typed state, provenance, sensitivity labels, expiry, and a resumable step pointer
Mac snapshot/restore adapters for open documents, app context, unsaved draft locations, and the active project without requiring Accessibility for the basic tier
Browser extension export/import of tab/session identity and staged form state without exporting credentials
Relay storage and synchronization for encrypted capsules plus pendant-sized status summaries
A restoration reconciler that detects changed files/tabs and presents conflicts instead of replaying stale actions
A user-facing dashboard and pendant commands for list, resume, fork, abandon, and securely erase

args.user_asks: “Before you use my Mac or logged-in browser, show me exactly what private data will leave each device, what will stay local, and let me say ‘redact that’ or ‘local only.’ Then proceed with the least-data version and give me a receipt afterward.”
args.why_useful: The owner currently has maximum-control automation but no intelligible, per-task data boundary. This would let them use powerful cross-device actions without needing to understand prompts, tokens, browser sessions, or relay internals. It is a live privacy contract spanning the pendant, Mac, browser, and relay—not merely an execution confirmation.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic typed accounting for paths, snippets, tab origins, and payload sizes. Use a cheap model to phrase the summary for speech; realtime is only needed for the owner’s short redact/local-only replies.
args.latency_budget: Generate the data-flow preview in under 2 seconds for ordinary tasks. Apply redaction before any network submission. Final receipt should be available within 3 seconds of task completion.
args.cost_estimate: Usually below $0.005 per task because accounting is deterministic; model cost is only the short spoken explanation. Storage cost is small for hashed receipts and policy decisions.
args.security_concerns: The preview itself must not reveal the sensitive data it is describing. Use category labels, hashes, lengths, and destination names by default, with optional local-only reveal. Enforce the selected policy at every handoff, not just at planning time; fail closed if a new field appears. Keep the policy decision and receipt tamper-evident but avoid retaining raw content.
missing: A typed end-to-end data-flow ledger attached to every plan, browser command, Mac action, and relay message
A preflight transformation layer that can remove fields, replace values with local summaries, or force a computation to remain on the Mac
A small pendant interaction protocol for redact, local-only, allow-once, and revoke-current-task
Browser and Mac adapters that report actual outbound fields rather than only intended actions
Tamper-evident receipts showing destinations, categories, byte counts, and policy decisions
A dashboard view that lets the owner inspect and revoke standing data policies

args.user_asks: “If that multi-step task partly failed, figure out exactly what changed, what did not, and repair only the missing pieces—without repeating anything that already happened.”
args.why_useful: Cross-surface work can succeed in one place and fail in another: a file may be created while a browser update times out, or a draft may be staged while its evidence fetch fails. Today the owner must manually inspect every surface and risks duplicate actions. A bounded reconciliation mode would make failures recoverable rather than opaque.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic receipt/state comparison first; use a cheap background model to classify discrepancies and generate a repair plan. Realtime is only for announcing the failure and accepting “repair,” “leave it,” or “discard.”
args.latency_budget: Report partial failure within 3 seconds of detection. Produce a repair plan within 10 seconds for ordinary jobs; execute only the missing idempotent steps after the owner’s command.
args.cost_estimate: Low: receipts and hashes dominate, with roughly $0.002–$0.01 for discrepancy classification. Avoid re-running expensive browser extraction when prior evidence remains valid.
args.security_concerns: Never infer success from a timeout. Preserve before/after evidence, use idempotency keys, and treat unknown outcomes as requiring reconciliation. Repair plans must exclude irreversible steps unless explicitly reissued. Keep sensitive evidence local or hashed in relay receipts.
missing: A cross-surface transaction journal with per-step preconditions, postconditions, idempotency keys, and unknown-outcome status
State probes for Mac files/apps and browser pages that can verify postconditions without replaying actions
A reconciliation planner that computes the minimal missing-step set and detects conflicting external changes
A durable repair lease and retry budget shared by Mac and browser workers
Pendant and dashboard controls for inspect, repair, abandon, and export the failure receipt

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

1. **Cross-device resumable handoff** — preserve the exact Mac/browser working state so the owner can leave and resume from the pendant.
2. **Per-task data-flow control** — show what private data would leave each device, support “redact” or “local only,” and issue a tamper-evident receipt.
3. **Partial-failure reconciliation** — determine exactly which steps completed and repair only missing steps, avoiding duplicate actions.

They require new cross-surface state protocols, typed provenance and postcondition checks, durable encrypted capsules/receipts, browser and Mac state probes, and pendant controls for resume, redact, repair, or abandon.

args.user_asks: When I say “save this for later” while I’m looking at a page, capture the page and my spoken note as a sourced, searchable research card; later I can ask the pendant what I saved and have the Mac reopen the exact source.
args.why_useful: This turns an ephemeral browser tab plus a two-second pendant utterance into durable memory with provenance. It works across the surfaces: the browser has the authenticated page, the pendant supplies intent while away from the keyboard, the relay keeps the request alive, and the Mac creates/reopens a human-readable artifact. It is materially safer than an unsourced memory because every claim points back to URL, tab, timestamp, and excerpt.
args.model_tier: Realtime tier only parses the short capture command and acknowledges it. A cheaper background model normalizes the note, extracts a short title/topics, deduplicates against existing cards, and generates a citation-preserving summary. Retrieval is semantic plus exact-topic matching; no model call if the user asks for a title/URL lookup.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the pendant within 500 ms, enqueue capture in under 2 s, and finish the card in 5–15 s. Retrieval should return the top cards in under 2 s and open the chosen source on the Mac in another 1–3 s.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.01 per capture depending on page length and summarization; retrieval usually under $0.001. Dominant costs are extracting long authenticated pages and background summarization, so cap captured text and hash unchanged excerpts.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated page content and the spoken note leave the browser/Mac only to the owner's relay and memory store; redact secrets and form fields before persistence. Store URL, title, excerpt hash, and source timestamp by default, with full text opt-in. Never submit forms or alter the page. Reopening a private URL must preserve its browser session and should fail closed if the session is gone. The pendant acknowledgement should not read the captured page aloud in public.
missing: A browser-extension command that returns the active tab's selected/semantic content with URL, tab ID, and stable excerpt locators
A durable research-card schema joining capture key, browser provenance, normalized text, and context-graph entities
A background indexing/deduplication worker and retention controls for private captures
An implementation of the granted Mac read-only inspection/sources tools so retrieval can verify the target tab and calendar context
A relay-to-Mac resumable enqueue/receipt path for captures made while the Mac is temporarily offline

args.user_asks: Tell me before my important logged-in browser sessions expire or get signed out, and when I’m back at the Mac, open only the affected sign-in pages so I can restore them without exposing page contents.
args.why_useful: Silent session expiry is a recurring failure mode for every authenticated workflow: a morning brief can look empty, a form can be half-filled, or a watch can stop silently. This gives the owner an actionable warning from the pendant while keeping private page contents out of the alert, then uses the Mac only for the narrowly scoped recovery step.
args.model_tier: No expensive model for detection: a deterministic browser heartbeat/session-state classifier runs on the relay or extension. Use the realtime tier only to understand a spoken request such as “which account needs attention?” and a cheap background model to rank urgency from session age and scheduled watches.
args.latency_budget: Heartbeat every 5–15 minutes with <1 s relay processing; alert within one heartbeat of an auth transition. On request, enumerate affected sessions in <2 s; Mac opens the recovery pages in 1–3 s.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost; roughly a few thousand lightweight heartbeat events per month. The dominant cost is relay/browser storage and any optional notification audio, not inference.
args.security_concerns: Transmit only state (session ID, origin, auth-needed/healthy, last-seen), never cookies, tokens, DOM text, screenshots, or typed credentials. Keep an allowlist of origins and let the owner pause monitoring from the pendant. Never auto-enter credentials or submit MFA; opening a sign-in page is the maximum automatic action. Expiry records should have short retention and be deletable.
missing: A browser-extension heartbeat payload that can distinguish healthy, expired, MFA-required, and network-failed without exposing page content
Durable per-origin watch policy with quiet hours and a last-alert fingerprint to prevent repeated alerts
A relay alert queue that can reach the pendant and retain the event while the Mac is offline
A Mac action that opens only the affected origin's re-auth URL and returns a receipt
A small dashboard showing session state and allowing per-origin pause/delete

args.change: Implement the two newly granted bounded read-only Mac tools rather than exposing schema-only stubs: mac_readonly_inspect should call a signed local helper for running apps, foreground app, browser tab metadata, accessibility state, UI snapshot, and allowlisted directory listings; mac_read_sources should use AppleScript/read-only EventKit/Mail queries for calendar and mail, enforce account_scope, redact by default, cap result sizes, and emit source timestamps plus receipts. Keep them separate from mac_run_actions and do not grant arbitrary shell access.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The assistant can currently act on the Mac but cannot reliably see what is open or read a bounded calendar/mail brief through the granted interfaces. Implementing these makes “what am I looking at?”, meeting preparation, and recovery from failed browser jobs dependable without scraping or mutating anything.
args.effort: Medium: local helper adapters, permission/error normalization, redaction and tests for each source; browser tabs require extension bridge integration. UI snapshots remain unavailable until the owner grants Screen Recording/Accessibility to the correct binary.
args.risk: Calendar/Mail queries could leak private content if scoping or redaction fails; mitigate with snippets-only defaults, strict size limits, account allowlists, audit receipts, and explicit unavailable states. UI inspection must never fall back to mouse or keystrokes. Recover by returning a typed permission/offline error, not guessed state.
args.cost_impact: Low ongoing API cost; bounded local reads are cheaper than model vision. Engineering cost is the main expense. UI snapshots may add local image storage/transport cost and should be opt-in.
args.latency_impact: Typically 100–800 ms for app/tab/source metadata; UI snapshots may take 1–3 s and should be requested only when needed.
args.security_impact: Read-only boundary materially reduces risk, but browser URLs/titles and mail/calendar snippets are sensitive. Keep data local where possible, redact by default, and attach provenance/TTL to every returned fact.
depends_on: mac_readonly_inspect and mac_read_sources granted schemas need real implementations
A signed localhost helper with the existing bearer-token boundary
Owner TCC grants only for UI snapshot features; non-visual app/browser/source reads should work without them

args.model_tier: Use a cheap background model for entity resolution and dependency/risk ranking; use realtime only when the owner asks for the impact or wants the prepared cleanup read aloud. Deterministic connectors should detect source changes and produce diffs before any model call.

args.user_asks: “I’m leaving my desk—freeze this work exactly where it is, and when I come back, restore the useful parts and remind me what I was doing.”
args.why_useful: The owner loses working context whenever they close the laptop, move between locations, or return after an interruption. Today the system can act on individual Mac or browser jobs, but it cannot preserve the human’s live workspace as a resumable handoff: which documents and tabs mattered, what was unsaved, what the next intended action was, and what must not be reopened. This would create a private, time-bounded work capsule rather than another task queue.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to label the captured workspace and produce a short resume note; use the realtime model only if the owner asks follow-up questions through the pendant.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the freeze in under 2 seconds, capture a bounded manifest within 10 seconds, and restore or explain unavailable items within 20 seconds after the Mac returns.
args.cost_estimate: Usually below $0.02 per capsule; the dominant cost is one small summarization call. Keep document contents local and summarize only metadata and explicitly selected snippets.
args.security_concerns: The capsule may expose sensitive filenames, URLs, and unsaved text. Encrypt it, give it an expiry, allow an immediate pendant delete gesture, redact secret-like fields, and never silently reopen a private page or send a draft. Restoration should show a manifest first and require confirmation for reopening sensitive tabs or unsaved files.

An encrypted, expiring capsule format shared by relay and Mac, with a local-only option

A resume planner that distinguishes safe reopening from potentially destructive restoration and produces a cited next-step note

args.user_asks: “When you finish something for me, tell me at the first moment I can actually absorb it—not while I’m presenting or driving—and escalate only if it is genuinely time-critical.”

args.latency_budget: Failover detection and route activation within 5–15 seconds; status should be visible locally within 1 second. Throughput is deliberately best-effort and bounded by LTE-M, with large downloads blocked or deferred.

transcript.text:
This round I established:

- The granted Mac inspection tools are still schemas without implementations; calls to inspect running apps, foreground app, or browser tabs fail immediately.
- `/browser/status` currently reports `home-chrome` online with **7 pending commands**, but there is no indication whether those commands are fresh, leased, or stale.
- Routing is working, with 57% of recent requests handled outside the expensive planner tier.
- I proposed a new cross-surface recovery capability: durable intent IDs, device-epoch leases, idempotent step replay, and one merged receipt timeline across relay, Mac, and browser.
- I also proposed the corresponding integration change and notified the browser-extension agent so stale-command quarantine can participate in the same protocol.

What I still need:

1. **Implementation of `mac_readonly_inspect`** so I can safely determine foreground app, active browser tabs, and current Mac state without using side-effect-capable execution.
2. **A durable cross-surface intent ledger** connecting `/plan`, `/execute`, Mac job receipts, browser command results, and relay events.
3. **Browser device liveness epochs and stale-command quarantine**, especially since the live queue already contains seven pending commands.
4. **A stable correlation ID and checkpoint contract** joining Mac receipts with browser step results.
5. Accessibility/Screen Recording permission remains owner-blocked; I would use it for richer UI-state recovery, but the system should continue operating through AppleScript and browser APIs without assuming those permissions.

args.user_asks: “Tell me when my Mac, browser, and pendant disagree about whether something happened, and help me reconcile it without repeating the action.”
args.why_useful: Today a timeout, sleep, or reconnect can leave conflicting evidence: the browser may show a changed page while the Mac has no receipt, or the Mac may report completion while the authenticated page still shows the old state. The owner needs an evidence-based contradiction alert, not a guessed success or an unsafe retry.
args.model_tier: Deterministic evidence matching and state-machine logic first; background model only to summarize the contradiction in plain language. Realtime is used only when the owner asks for the short spoken explanation.
args.latency_budget: Detect contradictions within 2 seconds of receiving a new receipt or page observation; spoken alert under 2 seconds when requested. Reconciliation can take up to 30 seconds because it may require a fresh browser read.
args.cost_estimate: Under $0.01 per contradiction in the common case; most work is receipt comparison and one read-only verification. Planner escalation is reserved for genuinely ambiguous evidence.
args.security_concerns: Evidence must remain account-scoped and redact private page contents in pendant audio. Never retry an uncertain mutation automatically. Show URLs, timestamps, action IDs, and before/after snippets only in the protected Mac/dashboard view; require a fresh owner instruction for any corrective mutation.
missing: A typed shared state vocabulary for Mac actions, browser observations, and pendant acknowledgements, including unknown and contradicted states
A causal evidence graph that links receipts, page observations, device epochs, and timestamps rather than treating each surface's success flag as authoritative
A read-only verification workflow for authenticated browser pages and Mac state after a contradiction
A dashboard and pendant event format that explains the conflict and offers safe choices: verify again, mark resolved, or prepare (but not execute) a correction

args.change: Create a contradiction-aware evidence graph rather than a flat action log. Normalize Mac receipts, browser observations, relay delivery events, and device liveness into immutable claims with source, timestamp, causal parent, confidence, and supersession rules; derive explicit states such as confirmed, unverified, contradicted, and resolved.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner would know exactly when the system is uncertain instead of receiving a confident but wrong 'done'. They could resume work after a crash without duplicating a submission, and later inspect why the system reached its conclusion.
args.effort: Medium: shared schema, ingestion adapters for existing Mac/browser/relay records, conflict rules, retention/redaction policy, and a small protected timeline UI.
args.risk: Incorrect normalization could create false conflicts or hide a real one. Keep raw source records immutable, expose both claims side by side, and default unresolved conflicts to non-action rather than silently choosing a winner.
args.cost_impact: Low storage and compute cost; deterministic graph updates are cheap. A small background model call may be used only to phrase a human-readable explanation.
args.latency_impact: Negligible for ordinary actions; conflict derivation should complete in under a second after each receipt, with verification reads adding network latency only when needed.
args.security_impact: Evidence may contain private URLs, filenames, and snippets. Enforce per-owner encryption and field-level redaction; pendant output should contain only minimal labels and no sensitive content by default.
depends_on: A shared typed claim schema across Mac, browser, relay, and pendant events
Stable causal IDs on Mac job receipts and browser command results
Read-only verification adapters for authenticated browser state and Mac state
A protected dashboard/timeline surface for raw evidence and resolution actions

Recorded a new capability: **safe cross-surface failure replay and first-divergence diagnosis**.

args.user_asks: If something I asked you to do in a logged-in browser fails because the bridge is offline, tell me what failed, keep the safe read-only part, and resume it automatically when the browser reconnects—without replaying a stale form submission or click.
args.why_useful: The live Mac agent has seven pending browser commands while the bridge is offline, and prior navigations have timed out. Today the owner gets opaque failures and cannot know whether retrying could duplicate a mutation. This makes the wearable, relay, Mac, and authenticated browser behave as one recoverable system: the pendant can report the interruption, the relay can retain the work, the Mac can reattach, and the browser can revalidate before continuing.
args.model_tier: Use the cheap background model for queue classification, URL/title revalidation, and compact failure summaries; reserve realtime only for the spoken interruption/recovery sentence. No model is needed for idempotency, tab affinity, or mutation quarantine.
args.latency_budget: Detect disconnect within one heartbeat (about 5–10 seconds), speak a short status on the next available relay turn, and resume read-only extraction within 10 seconds of a healthy browser heartbeat. Never auto-resume a write step; stage it for the owner.
args.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per interrupted job; most work is deterministic state and browser polling. Realtime/TTS cost occurs only for the brief spoken alert, and background summarization dominates when a long page must be re-explained.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated page text must remain local to the Mac/relay policy and be redacted before any spoken alert. Persist tab/session IDs, URL, title, step hashes, and before/after evidence—not passwords or full page bodies. A reconnect must prove the same tab/session and a fresh URL/title/DOM fingerprint; otherwise quarantine and ask. Never replay submit/send/delete/purchase or arbitrary click steps automatically, even though the owner permits broad Mac access.

A deterministic rule that permits automatic retries only for reads/navigation and converts mutations into a reviewable plan with evidence

Expired or mismatched capsules are discarded with an explicit reason instead of replayed.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When the browser bridge goes offline, the owner gets a truthful one-sentence status and later receives the safe result without duplicated clicks or submissions. A stale logged-in tab can never silently consume an old command after reconnect.

args.risk: A false fingerprint mismatch may leave safe work waiting; recover with a visible Retry after revalidation. args.cost_impact: Negligible storage and polling overhead; one short background classification per multi-step job at most. No additional realtime calls except optional spoken alert/TTS.
args.latency_impact: Adds one heartbeat/fingerprint round trip before resuming, typically under 1–2 seconds; prevents 45-second browser timeout loops by failing fast when offline.
args.security_impact: Improves security by binding commands to a tab/session and retaining redacted evidence only. Authenticated content remains on the Mac/approved relay path; no credentials are persisted. Mutations remain owner-reviewed.

It is beyond a generic durable job runner because it reconciles Mac receipts, browser tab/session identity, and pendant-delivery state, preventing duplicate submissions after reconnect.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background worker/state machine for heartbeat monitoring, checkpoint reconciliation, retry classification, and delivery; use the realtime tier only for the owner's short spoken request and an urgent interruption notice. Escalate to the stronger planner only when a failed step is ambiguous or the page has materially changed.
args.latency_budget: A reconnect should be noticed within 10–20 seconds of browser heartbeat recovery; deterministic reconciliation should take under 2 seconds. Pendant interruption/complete notices should be queued for offline delivery and spoken on next contact. No polling or model call is needed while all surfaces are healthy.
args.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per task, dominated by occasional background model recovery for ambiguous page changes; healthy tasks use only D1/R2/worker operations. TTS/audio delivery is the secondary cost when a notice is actually spoken.
args.security_concerns: Persist only task IDs, step receipts, tab/session IDs, URL hashes, and minimal redacted evidence; never copy page secrets into the pendant queue. Resume must require an idempotency key and verify the same tab/session plus a precondition (URL/title/semantic fingerprint) before any browser write. A changed page becomes paused and asks the owner; no automatic retries of submit/send/purchase steps. The owner can ask the pendant for status and cancel, while existing maximum-control policy remains unchanged.
missing: A durable cross-surface checkpoint record linking each Mac action receipt to its browser command and pendant delivery acknowledgment.
A reconnect coordinator that consumes browser heartbeat changes, reconciles pending commands against receipts, and distinguishes safe read/retry steps from non-repeatable writes.
A compact offline status envelope on the relay/pendant (queued, resumed, paused-needs-owner, completed) with deduplication and expiry.
An explicit browser precondition/fingerprint check and idempotency key carried through /browser/poll and /browser/result before resuming.

args.user_asks: “When I’m in a focus block or meeting, keep interruptions out of my way, but collect anything important and give me one short catch-up when it ends.”
args.why_useful: The pendant is the one surface that can start or end a focus block without the owner touching the Mac, while the relay can hold alerts during a dropped link, the Mac can change local notification state and collect Calendar/Mail context, and the browser can stop surfacing non-urgent page-watch changes. Existing routines and briefings do not provide a shared interruption contract or a single end-of-block digest.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic rules and a small background model to classify queued events by urgency and deduplicate them. Use the realtime tier only for the pendant's start/end acknowledgment and when the owner explicitly asks for an interruption. Generate the end digest with a cheaper batch model, grounded in collected source snippets.
args.latency_budget: Start/stop acknowledgment under 1 second when connected; if offline, persist the state locally and replay it on reconnect. Suppression decisions are immediate and rule-based. End-of-block digest in under 10 seconds, with no need to wait on every source if one is unavailable.
args.cost_estimate: Typically <$0.01 per focus block: mostly event storage and one small digest call. TTS costs only for the final spoken catch-up. No model call is made for routine low-priority events.
args.security_concerns: The relay stores event metadata and redacted snippets with a user-configurable retention window; sensitive mail/browser bodies stay on the Mac unless explicitly included. Urgency classification must show source links and why an item was held. Emergency/allowlisted senders, alarms, and explicit owner interrupts bypass suppression. Never alter or send messages; this is notification control and summarization only.
missing: A shared focus-state lease with owner/device origin, start/end time, timezone, and offline replay semantics.
A relay-side held-event queue with urgency/allowlist rules and deduplication across Mail, Calendar, browser watches, and Mac jobs.
Mac/browser adapters that apply and restore notification suppression without losing the prior user state.
An end-of-block reconciliation job that cites every surfaced item and reports anything that could not be inspected.

args.change: Add a cross-surface event ledger and focus-state lease in the relay. Each incoming alert or completion event gets a stable event ID, source (pendant/Mac/browser), sensitivity class, urgency, focus-block ID, and delivery acknowledgments. The relay exposes a compact delta feed; Mac and browser adapters report applied notification state and restore tokens. On focus end, a worker joins undelivered deltas with Calendar/Mail/browser citations, emits one digest, and marks each item delivered or unavailable. Expire leases and held payloads automatically, and make replay idempotent.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can press one pendant control to get uninterrupted work without losing important things, even if the Mac or browser disconnects. They get one trustworthy catch-up instead of duplicate alerts, silent loss, or a permanently altered notification setting.
args.effort: Medium-high: new D1 schema/state machine, relay endpoints, Mac notification adapter, browser event adapter, and pendant start/stop/replay protocol; add fault-injection tests for disconnects and duplicate delivery.
args.risk: A stale lease could suppress an urgent event or fail to restore the prior notification state. Mitigate with hard lease expiry, emergency bypass rules, visible active-state feedback on the pendant, restore tokens, and a recovery sweep that replays anything unacknowledged. If the digest worker fails, retain the queue and report its unavailable state rather than dropping data.
args.cost_impact: Low storage and worker cost; one inexpensive digest inference per focus block, plus optional TTS. No continuous realtime model use.
args.latency_impact: State changes and suppression deltas are sub-second when online; reconnect replay is bounded by the next heartbeat. Digest generation is asynchronous and should complete within 10 seconds.
args.security_impact: Sensitive content remains on the Mac by default; the relay holds IDs and redacted snippets only, encrypted with short retention. Every digest item carries provenance and a reason for inclusion. Focus state is scoped to the owner's authenticated devices.
depends_on: A pendant-side focus start/stop event and offline persistence skill
A relay-held alert queue with TTL and urgency policy
Mac notification-state read/restore adapter (AppleScript where possible)
Browser watch/event adapter that can pause and resume cleanly

args.user_asks: “Keep a private list of promises and follow-ups I make across email, meetings, and logged-in sites; remind me only when one is genuinely at risk, and let me close it with evidence.”
args.why_useful: Today the system can read sources or produce briefings, but it cannot maintain a single, provenance-backed lifecycle for commitments that begin in one surface and are completed in another. The owner should be able to say this once on the pendant and have the relay monitor deadlines, Mac inspect Calendar/Mail, and the browser verify a completed ticket/order/form without turning every unchanged update into noise.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background extraction/classification model on new or changed source snippets, with deterministic deadline and status rules. Use the realtime tier only when the owner asks about a commitment or when an urgent deadline needs a spoken alert. Use a stronger model only to resolve ambiguous people, dates, or evidence links.
args.latency_budget: Capture an explicitly spoken promise immediately into a pending record. Process new source deltas within a few minutes; deadline-risk alerts should be delivered within the configured window. A status question should answer in under 3 seconds from the ledger, with source inspection performed asynchronously when needed.
args.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.02 per day for a normal owner: event-driven extraction over short redacted snippets and one compact risk digest. TTS is incurred only for spoken reminders. No continuous realtime inference.
args.security_concerns: Keep the ledger private and minimize content: store commitment text, parties, due window, source IDs, sensitivity, and hashes rather than full mail/page bodies. Require explicit opt-in source scopes and quiet hours. Never mark a promise complete solely from a model guess; completion needs an owner utterance or cited evidence from the same account/context. Alerts must include why they fired and an easy dismiss/snooze action.
missing: A durable commitment schema with states (captured, clarified, active, at-risk, done, dismissed), due-window uncertainty, owner/source provenance, and evidence links.
Cross-surface entity resolution for person, project, and account without copying secrets into relay memory.
Delta-driven extractors for Mail/Calendar and authenticated browser changes, plus a deduplicating risk scheduler.
A pendant action protocol for confirm, clarify, snooze, and mark-done-with-evidence, including offline replay.

This is genuinely cross-surface: the pendant supplies the low-friction trigger, the relay persists the capsule while the Mac sleeps, the browser supplies authenticated tab identity, and the Mac reopens only the chosen context.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to recognize the short park/resume utterance and speak the recap; use a cheaper background model to normalize the capsule, rank relevant tabs/apps, and redact volatile or sensitive fields.
args.latency_budget: Park acknowledgement under 2 seconds; resume acknowledgement under 2 seconds, with Mac/browser restoration continuing asynchronously and a completion receipt within 15 seconds.

args.effort: Medium: heartbeat validation, command lease/dead-letter state, replay classification, dashboard status, and a small relay notification adapter.
args.risk: A false degraded state could delay a legitimate read; recover by accepting a fresh tab-bound heartbeat and allowing explicit replay from the dashboard. Never delete quarantined commands automatically; retain receipts and audit history.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a few D1/local JSON records per command and one periodic watchdog invocation.
args.latency_impact: Adds no delay to healthy commands; degraded detection occurs at heartbeat/lease expiry, with recovery in one heartbeat interval.
args.security_impact: Improves security by preventing stale commands from being applied to a different authenticated tab or account. Quarantined payloads should be redacted in dashboard/pendant views and retained under existing private-session policy.

This would make private-account automation trustworthy without ever moving passwords or session cookies through the relay.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to resolve the owner's short authorization utterance and read back the account/display name. Use deterministic local code for capability-token issuance, tab binding, field-diff verification, and receipts; use a cheaper background model only to summarize the final proof in plain language.
args.latency_budget: Authorization and account read-back under 2 seconds; preflight proof under 5 seconds; final field-diff receipt within 10 seconds after the browser reports completion.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for most invocations; a small deterministic token/receipt record per task. Optional summarization costs under $0.005 per completed task.
args.security_concerns: The relay must never receive cookies, passwords, page bodies beyond the approved fields, or reusable bearer tokens. Issue a one-task, short-lived capability bound to account identifier, extension device, tab/session id, action hash, and expiry; require a physical pendant confirmation for account-scoped mutations. args.risk: Pairing loss or extension updates could invalidate authorization; recover with an explicit re-pair flow and never silently fall back to an unbound session. An account label could itself be sensitive, so redact it in relay logs and expose only a user-chosen alias.
args.cost_impact: Negligible per-task API cost; engineering and secure-key storage are the main cost. Requires a small key record on the pendant and short-lived records in relay/bridge storage.
args.latency_impact: Adds one local attestation round trip, typically 100–500 ms on a healthy link; no model latency on execution.
args.security_impact: Materially reduces confused-deputy and stale-tab risk while preserving the owner's maximum-access policy. It does not block ordinary unscoped local actions, only account-scoped browser work lacking a valid envelope.

args.user_asks: If I ask you to do something while my Mac or browser is offline, remember the intent, wait for the right device to reconnect, then carry it out safely and tell me exactly what happened — without losing it or doing it twice.
args.why_useful: Today the pendant can hear an intent while the browser is offline and the Mac may reconnect later, but there is no owner-visible, cross-node reconciliation contract. This would turn intermittent connectivity into a dependable assistant: one request ID, durable pending state, deduplication, conflict detection, and a short spoken result when the action is finally applied. It is specifically multi-node: pendant captures intent, relay persists and arbitrates, Mac/browser execute, and the pendant reports the receipt.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to normalize the spoken request and clarify ambiguity; use a cheap background model (or deterministic rules) to reconcile queued intents, device capabilities, and receipts after reconnect.
args.latency_budget: Capture acknowledgment under 1 second offline; reconnect reconciliation within 10 seconds of a device heartbeat; spoken completion within 3 seconds after receipt. No waiting loop on the pendant.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.01 per request, dominated by optional normalization/reconciliation; most retries, dedupe, and receipt matching should be deterministic. Small durable relay storage per intent and receipt.
args.security_concerns: The relay must store only a minimized intent capsule, not page contents or secrets, with encryption, expiry, and device-scoped bearer authorization. Never replay destructive actions (send mail, delete, purchase) from an offline capsule without a fresh owner confirmation; reversible/read-only actions may replay according to owner policy. Surface conflicts such as changed URLs, stale files, or changed calendar state instead of guessing. Dashboard must expose cancel/expire and the full action/receipt chain.

args.why_useful: The live trace proves 24 kHz TTS is being rendered and accepted (75,734-byte PCM), but the measured LTE-M link drops about 7.8 seconds of uplink when 24 kbps downlink overlaps it. This capability turns the current demo into a conversation that remains usable under the exact condition the owner will encounter.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the conversational turn; deterministic firmware/relay control for congestion decisions; no planner-tier model call.
args.latency_budget: Add no more than one 20–40 ms control interval. Keep audio playout under 120 ms of additional buffering; a codec-mode change may take one frame (60 ms).
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost. Relay CPU/storage rises modestly for packet statistics and short Opus transcode buffers; LTE data may fall because the adaptive mode lowers bitrate during contention.
args.security_concerns: Only transport quality metrics, codec mode, and packet sequence numbers leave the pendant; never audio-derived content. Persist no speech beyond existing retention. No confirmation is needed because this changes transport quality, not an external side effect.
missing: Firmware telemetry for sequence gaps, jitter-buffer depth, modem send-queue occupancy, and button/turn state
A relay codec-negotiation and prioritization state machine that can lower uplink bitrate or pause nonessential downlink frames without dropping speech
Mac TTS output packetization that can emit a negotiated Opus profile instead of always uploading a large 24 kHz PCM blob
An end-to-end fault-injection test that overlaps owner speech and reply audio and verifies bounded loss/recovery

args.change: Add a closed-loop AudioQoS session shared by pendant firmware, Cloudflare relay, and Mac audio pipeline. The pendant emits compact 1-second counters (uplink loss, jitter, queue depth, playout underruns); relay computes a mode (normal, uplink-protect, recovery) and sends a signed mode update; Mac TTS packetizer and relay Opus transcode honor that mode. In uplink-protect, cap/reshape downlink and reserve modem budget for microphone packets; in recovery, refill the jitter buffer gradually. Record the mode and counters in the existing pipeline event/receipt stream so each call can be diagnosed without retaining speech.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner speaks while the agent replies, their words will no longer vanish for several seconds, and a degraded connection will recover gracefully instead of producing silence or a late burst of audio. The owner also gets an honest explanation in a completion receipt when quality was reduced.
args.effort: Medium-high: a firmware telemetry packet and state machine, relay session state and packet scheduler, Mac/Opus packetizer changes, plus an automated contention test. This is a focused vertical slice rather than a new surface.
args.risk: A bad mode update could starve replies or cause oscillation. Use monotonic sequence numbers, hysteresis (minimum 2 seconds per mode), a 5-second local timeout to return to normal, and retain the current static 24 kHz path as fallback. Recovery is automatic on reconnect.
args.cost_impact: No additional model calls. A few dozen bytes/sec of telemetry and small relay memory per active call; adaptive mode should reduce LTE airtime during contention. Engineering/test cost is the dominant cost.
args.latency_impact: Telemetry/control under 1 second; at most one 60 ms codec frame to change mode, with up to 120 ms intentional jitter buffering during recovery.
args.security_impact: Telemetry contains transport statistics only. Authenticate mode updates to the paired pendant; do not upload raw microphone samples beyond the existing audio path, and keep diagnostic counters under the existing audio-retention policy.
depends_on: Pendant firmware support for loss/jitter/queue counters and a local fallback mode

Mac TTS/Opus packetizer that can honor a per-session audio mode
A contention/fault-injection harness covering simultaneous uplink and downlink

transcript.text:
Round 117 findings:

- `/browser/status` reports the bridge offline with **9 pending commands**.
- Browser jobs can wait roughly **45 seconds** before failing, and stale commands remain queued.
- `/observe` reports the foreground app as Claude and confirms that synthesized UI input currently **does not reach the screen**: Accessibility is not trusted for the running AI Pendant Agent binary.
- The pipeline has emitted “Waiting for your approval” even though `FULL_CONTROL_MODE` is configured to run without approval gates. This is a state-reporting inconsistency.

I recorded three new proposals:

1. **Connectivity-aware browser task continuation**  
   Immediately tell the owner whether a task is queued, waiting for the browser, resumed, or abandoned; checkpoint authenticated steps; quarantine stale commands; resume only after a fresh tab/session check.

2. **Execution-policy reconciliation**  
   Make pipeline events use the actual executor policy, so the system cannot claim approval is required when the task is running under maximum-access mode.

3. **Reachability-aware Mac actions**  
   Before UI actions, consume `/observe`; use AppleScript fallbacks where safe, or return `not_reached` rather than falsely reporting success when Accessibility is unavailable.

What I still need:

- **Browser bridge recovery or an explicit queue-drain/quarantine implementation.** The current offline queue is the most urgent operational gap.
- A single authoritative **effective execution-policy/version** exposed to both the executor and pipeline recorder.
- A typed receipt state for **executed / failed / not_reached**, plus AppleScript adapters for common named-app operations.
- If reliable GUI automation is required, the owner must manually grant Accessibility to the exact running binary `/Users/evanliu/Applications/AI Pendant Agent.app`; this cannot be granted from the harness.

The pendant could give a short spoken ‘you were here’ summary, while the Mac could restore the workspace and detect conflicts before touching files or tabs.

Store sensitive locators and browser session identifiers only on the Mac; relay receives an opaque capsule ID and redacted summary. transcript.text:
Recorded two proposals:

1. **Crash-safe cross-device work capsules**  
   Save the owner’s exact Mac/browser work context and let the pendant recall or restore it later, with conflict detection so changed files or tabs are never overwritten.

2. **Pendant-presence-gated sensitive work**  
   Let the Mac prepare private work while the owner is away, but require authenticated physical pendant proximity before restoring sensitive context. This would use rotating BLE challenges rather than trusting RSSI or relay connectivity.

Both require new connective infrastructure rather than merely exposing today’s routes: capsule schema and conflict handling, browser context export, relay state, authenticated pendant–Mac presence, key revocation, and local privacy boundaries.

args.name: audio_path_diagnostic_fixture
args.what_it_does: On a deliberate diagnostic trigger, the pendant emits timestamped sequence-numbered synthetic uplink frames and plays a fixed 24 kHz verification fixture. It reports capture clock, Opus encode duration, modem send/drop counters, playback decode duration, resampler underruns, and fixture completion; it never records or persists microphone content. It can stop immediately on button press or server command.
args.why_not_server_side: Only firmware can measure the real I2S clock, Opus CPU budget, modem queue drops, and speaker-side underruns at the exact frame boundary, and it must work when the LTE link is degraded.
args.trigger: Long button press, or a signed diagnostic command from the relay during an explicitly requested test; never on ordinary calls.

args.why_useful: This turns scattered obligations into one actionable view: a meeting promise in Mail, a due date in a private portal, and a calendar collision are linked as one item rather than three separate alerts. The Mac leaves an auditable board the owner can review later, while the pendant gives only the highest-priority exceptions.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model for extraction, deduplication, deadline/conflict reasoning, and board generation; reserve realtime only for the spoken request and a brief answer. Use no realtime context replay for the overnight/background work.
args.latency_budget: Spoken acknowledgement under 1 second; initial answer in 10–20 seconds when browser is healthy. If private tabs are unavailable, say so immediately and complete Calendar/Mail-only results rather than hanging. Background board can finish asynchronously.
args.cost_estimate: One background text invocation per request plus bounded authenticated-page extraction; dominant cost is browser page reads and context, not the short realtime acknowledgement. TTS is a few seconds of generated PCM and should be cached with the board.
args.security_concerns: Calendar/Mail and logged-in page contents leave the Mac only as scoped extracts; redact message bodies by default and retain source URLs, timestamps, and snippets rather than whole pages. Never submit forms or send mail. Browser session IDs and tab URLs must be kept out of the pendant transcript; require explicit owner action later for any mutation.

A review-board writer that atomically creates/updates one dated folder with a brief, evidence manifest, and draft suggestions

args.change: Add a cross-surface browser-queue reconciler in the Mac planner: correlate each pending browser command with its local jobId, journal/receipt, tab/session lease, and last heartbeat; classify it as runnable, duplicate, orphaned, or stalled. A command with no live tab, an expired lease, or a high attempt count must be quarantined (not replayed), emit one durable diagnostic event, and expose a resume/ discard operation. Reconcile after every browser heartbeat and before any new browser action, then surface a compact Mac review item and, when appropriate, a pendant alert. Keep the existing owner policy of maximum access: this is observability and replay prevention, not an approval gate.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops getting silent duplicate clicks or 45-second hangs after Safari/Chrome closes. They receive one clear explanation—what was attempted, whether it changed anything, and whether it can safely resume—instead of the system repeatedly acting on a stale private tab.
args.effort: Medium: a small persistent ledger and state machine in local-agent, adapters for /browser/status, /browser/poll, /browser/result/:commandId, /jobs/:jobId/receipts, and journal events, plus dashboard/briefing presentation and tests for restart/heartbeat races.
args.risk: Incorrect classification could quarantine a valid long-running read or discard a command whose result is merely delayed. Preserve the raw command and receipt, use lease expiry plus attempt/time thresholds rather than attempts alone, and make resume/discard explicit operations. Recovery is replay from the preserved command only after a fresh tab/session binding.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one lightweight ledger write per heartbeat/command and bounded diagnostic context. No extra model call unless generating the human summary.
args.latency_impact: Adds tens of milliseconds before a browser action; removes the current worst-case 45-second blocking wait for commands that can never complete.
args.security_impact: Improves privacy by preventing stale authenticated commands from replaying into a different tab. Store opaque session/tab IDs and hashes, not page contents; redact URLs in pendant alerts.

args.user_asks: When I miss or am about to miss a commitment, tell me what is at risk, find the smallest set of recovery options across my Calendar, Mail, and logged-in work pages, and prepare a choice card on my Mac with draft messages and proposed times—then let me choose one from the pendant. Never send, submit, or reschedule without my explicit choice.
args.why_useful: Today the system can summarize sources, but it cannot connect a slipping commitment to concrete, evidence-backed recovery choices. This would turn “I’m late” into a calm decision: what can be moved, who needs a draft notice, what deadline is hard, and which option causes the least downstream damage.
args.model_tier: Use a background model for monitoring, commitment extraction, dependency analysis, and generating alternatives. Use the realtime tier only for the pendant’s brief alert and the owner’s selection. Use a cheap deterministic rules layer for time arithmetic, conflict checks, and redaction.
args.latency_budget: A risk alert should reach the pendant within 30 seconds of a detected change or missed start. A choice card should appear on the Mac within 1–2 minutes; selecting an option should acknowledge in under 1 second and queue the selected plan for explicit execution.
args.cost_estimate: Periodic checks are mostly deterministic and low-cost; one background model call only when a commitment changes or crosses a risk threshold. Browser extraction and authenticated session availability dominate cost and latency; spoken alerts are short cached audio.
args.security_concerns: Private calendar, mail, and portal evidence must remain scoped to the relevant commitment, with source snippets and timestamps rather than whole-page retention. Drafts must be visibly marked unsent. No browser form submission, email send, or calendar mutation may happen from the alert alone; the chosen option must produce a human-readable before/after plan and a second explicit execution request.
missing: A commitment lifecycle model with planned, at-risk, missed, recovered, and dismissed states, including evidence and dependency edges
A cross-surface change detector that compares Calendar/Mail/browser observations over time instead of only answering on demand
A choice-card renderer and pendant selection protocol that carries an opaque option ID back to the Mac without replaying private content
A transactional action bundle that can execute a selected multi-app recovery plan and return per-step receipts or restore the prior draft state

args.change: Add a commitment-risk and recovery transaction layer that consumes timestamped Calendar/Mail/browser observations, maintains a state machine (planned → at-risk → missed → recovery-pending → chosen → executed), and emits an option envelope rather than an action. Each envelope contains 2–3 ranked recovery plans with evidence IDs, affected apps, exact proposed changes, and an opaque selection token. The pendant can select an option; the Mac then materializes drafts/previews, executes only the selected reversible bundle, and records per-step receipts plus a compensating plan.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets an immediate, concrete way out of a missed obligation instead of another passive summary: choose the least damaging recovery plan from the pendant, with the Mac preparing the exact drafts and schedule changes for review.
args.effort: High: new durable state and evidence schema, cross-source diffing, option ranking, pendant option-selection messages, transactional multi-app planner, and receipt/compensation handling.
args.risk: A false positive could cause stressful alerts or propose an inappropriate message. Require confidence and quiet hours, suppress duplicate alerts, preserve drafts only, and make every mutation a separate explicit execution step. If execution partially fails, leave a discrepancy card with receipts rather than guessing.
args.cost_impact: Low-to-moderate background model cost only on state transitions; storage and deterministic conflict analysis dominate routine operation. No additional realtime model call beyond the short alert/selection exchange.
args.latency_impact: Detection depends on source polling, but once an at-risk transition is observed, option generation should complete in 1–2 minutes; pendant acknowledgement remains sub-second.
args.security_impact: The option envelope sent to the pendant contains opaque IDs and short redacted labels, never private message bodies or portal content. Evidence and drafts remain on the Mac/relay under existing authenticated scope; execution logs record app and field changes.
depends_on: A durable commitment lifecycle and cross-source observation diff store
A pendant protocol for presenting/selecting opaque option IDs
A transactional multi-app action bundle with per-step receipts and compensating recovery
Reliable authenticated browser observation with tab/session continuity

args.user_asks: “Start meeting mode.”
args.why_useful: With one pendant press or spoken command, the hive should recognize the current/next meeting, quietly assemble the agenda and relevant mail/calendar context, keep a live 24 kHz audio sidecar while the owner talks, and after the meeting leave a cited recap with decisions, open questions, and draft follow-ups—never sending anything automatically. The pendant supplies an immediate, hands-free trigger and audio; the Mac knows which meeting app/window is active and can read Calendar/Mail; the browser bridge can inspect the authenticated agenda or project tab; the relay keeps the session alive and delivers the recap when the Mac or pendant link briefly drops.
args.model_tier: Realtime model only for the live turn-taking/audio control; use a cheaper background model for agenda extraction, transcript cleanup, decision/action-item synthesis, and draft generation.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the pendant trigger in under 300 ms, select the meeting context in under 2 s, and keep audio playout below 250 ms end-to-end. Post-meeting recap can take 1–3 minutes and should be resumable.
args.cost_estimate: One realtime session plus roughly 2–5 minutes of background transcription/synthesis; dominant cost is live audio tokens, so only the meeting interval should use realtime and the recap should use the slower tier.
args.security_concerns: Calendar/Mail and authenticated browser content leave the Mac only as redacted, cited excerpts; raw audio/transcript needs explicit retention (default delete after recap). Never submit/send a draft. Starting capture must be an explicit button or spoken command with a clear LED/audio acknowledgment; meeting mode must show an obvious active indicator.
missing: A meeting-context correlator joining the next Calendar event to the foreground Mac app and optionally an authenticated browser tab
A session-scoped audio/transcript capsule that survives a dropped Mac link and supports resumable post-meeting processing
A citation-preserving recap/draft artifact written to the owner's AI-Pendant-Workspace with a dashboard review state
A true 24 kHz capture/uplink path: current pendant capture is 15,625 Hz and 16 kHz Opus uplink even though playback decodes 24 kHz

args.change: Make the audio contract genuinely symmetric at 24 kHz: capture 24 kHz from the microphone (or oversample at 48 kHz and decimate), encode 24 kHz Opus uplink, and advertise the negotiated sample rate in the pipeline handshake. Keep the current 24 kHz decoder for downlink, but add bounded jitter buffering and a relay pass-through mode so the relay does not silently transcode 16 kHz speech back into 24 kHz. Measure encode+decode CPU, heap high-water, packet loss, and glass-to-glass latency in a hardware-in-the-loop fixture; refuse the mode and fall back to 16 kHz before audio underruns if the budget is exceeded.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner's voice and the assistant's reply would stop being upsampled on one direction: meeting mode, voice notes, and ordinary conversation would sound noticeably more natural and intelligible, especially for names and consonants. A negotiated fallback means a weak link becomes lower fidelity rather than a broken conversation.
args.effort: Medium-to-high: firmware microphone clock/driver and Opus application mode, relay negotiation/transcode changes, bridge clock validation, and a repeatable HIL latency/packet-loss test. The current nRF9160 prototype has only 211,608 B app RAM and both encode/decode already consume about 87% of one core, so profiling must precede enabling it by default; the eventual product board may need a codec/DSP or faster MCU.
args.risk: 24 kHz capture can exhaust CPU, increase radio bitrate and battery drain, or expose clock drift between the nRF9160 and ESP32. Recover by capability negotiation, a watchdog on underrun, and automatic 16 kHz fallback; retain diagnostic counters rather than dropping the session.
args.cost_impact: No incremental API cost for codec changes; 24 kHz Opus likely increases radio airtime and energy roughly in proportion to bitrate. Hardware cost is TBD, but a production audio codec/DSP or faster MCU may add roughly $3–$10 BOM and tens of mW compared with this development kit.
args.latency_impact: Potentially +10–30 ms from larger capture/codec work unless frames stay bounded; target under 250 ms glass-to-glass and measure p50/p95. Fallback must happen within one failed negotiation/underrun window.
args.security_impact: Audio remains encrypted in transit; higher-fidelity raw audio increases sensitivity and should use the existing short-retention/deletion policy. Do not persist PCM on the pendant or relay except bounded diagnostic samples with explicit opt-in.
depends_on: A pipeline handshake carrying sample rate/codec/bitrate and a relay pass-through path
The pending audio-path diagnostic/HIL fixture and offline delivery retry behavior
A production hardware decision if nRF9160 CPU headroom cannot meet simultaneous encode/decode
An end-to-end 24 kHz capture test using the actual microphone clock rather than resampling a 16 kHz source

args.user_asks: “Move this conversation to my Mac.”
args.why_useful: The owner should be able to begin a thought hands-free on the pendant and continue it at the desk without repeating the request or losing the assistant's working context. The pendant marks the exact turn and provides a short spoken acknowledgment; the relay seals a resumable conversation capsule; the Mac opens the relevant workspace, browser tab, or draft and presents the same pending decision; the owner can then type, inspect sources, or continue by voice. When they leave the desk, a single pendant press should hand the unfinished state back, including what was already done and what remains.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the handoff acknowledgment and any continuing live speech. Use a cheaper background model to compress the conversation capsule, select relevant files/tabs, and generate the Mac-side continuation view.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 300 ms, persist the capsule before replying, and have the Mac workspace ready within 3 seconds. Returning to the pendant should require only a short state summary, not a full replay.
args.cost_estimate: One small realtime turn per handoff; background compression and workspace selection should be a low-cost model. Storage is a small encrypted capsule plus references, so the dominant cost is not storage but repeated context if the capsule is not compact.
args.security_concerns: The capsule may contain private speech, authenticated URLs, and draft text. Encrypt it, retain it only until the task is completed or for a user-configurable short TTL, and redact secrets from dashboard previews. Opening a file or tab is reversible; sending, deleting, purchasing, or submitting must remain an explicit separate action. The owner must see which Mac surfaces will be opened before the handoff executes.
missing: A versioned, encrypted handoff-capsule format with turn boundary, task state, completed actions, pending decisions, source references, and expiry
A relay-to-Mac handoff route with idempotency and acknowledgement, plus a Mac-to-pendant resume route
A workspace resolver that maps capsule references to an existing Mac file/tab without leaking authenticated page contents into the relay log
A dashboard/menubar continuation card showing capsule provenance and allowing discard or resume

args.change: Replace the prototype nRF9160-plus-ESP32 audio split with a production pendant audio front end: a low-power 24/48 kHz codec or DSP with hardware sample-rate conversion, a small secure ring-buffer SRAM, and a shared clock exposed to the modem MCU. Keep the nRF9160 for LTE-M/NB-IoT control and negotiation, but move Opus pre/post-processing and jitter-buffer servicing off the 64 MHz application core. Add a physical recording-status indicator driven independently of firmware task load.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They would get natural, stable 24 kHz speech without the pendant becoming hot, stuttering, or dying quickly, and the recording indicator would remain trustworthy even if the network or application task is wedged. It makes long conversations and meeting handoffs dependable rather than a lab-only mode.
args.effort: High: select codec/DSP and PMIC, redesign the board and clock tree, update Zephyr drivers and the ESP32 bridge contract, validate RF coexistence and acoustic performance, and manufacture a small pilot. This is intentionally a product redesign rather than a software workaround for the development kit.
args.risk: New clock domains can introduce drift, RF noise, boot failures, or a more difficult firmware update path. Recover with a bypass path to the existing I2S wiring, a hardware watchdog, signed dual-image firmware, and a 16 kHz compatibility mode. Validate on a pilot batch before replacing the prototype fleet.
args.cost_impact: Roughly $5–$15 additional BOM depending on codec/DSP, SRAM, PMIC, and indicator choices, plus one-time board/NRE cost; active audio power should fall versus spending most of the nRF9160 core on codec work, though idle BOM power rises slightly.
args.latency_impact: Hardware buffering should reduce codec CPU contention and make p95 latency more predictable; target under 50 ms local audio buffering and under 250 ms glass-to-glass. Clock conversion must be bounded and measurable.
args.security_impact: A hardware ring buffer must be volatile by default and zeroized on stop; do not add persistent raw-audio storage. The independent indicator must be fail-safe—if capture power is enabled, it should indicate capture even when the main MCU is unresponsive.
depends_on: A measured 24 kHz end-to-end audio contract and HIL test vector
A product-board decision replacing the explicitly provisional Nordic development kit
Relay negotiation for codec/sample-rate capability and a bridge firmware protocol version
A hardware privacy-indicator review with the owner

args.subject: New gap: interruption-safe resume capsule
args.body: I see a gap beyond existing briefs/watchers: owner says 'save this and remind me when I'm back/at 3'. Need cross-surface resume capsule: Mac read-only snapshot foreground app + browser tabs + active project/selection, relay stores redacted capsule and schedule, then Mac reopens exact apps/tabs and pendant gives 20-sec spoken resume with source links. Distinct from generic long-running jobs/meeting prep.

args.user_asks: “Save where I am and remind me at 3—or when I get back to my Mac—then put me back exactly where I left off and give me the short version.”
args.why_useful: Interruptions currently lose the relationship between the pendant request, the Mac's active work, and authenticated browser state. A resume capsule would let the owner safely switch contexts without re-finding tabs, files, or the last unfinished step. It is genuinely multi-surface: the pendant supplies intent and timing, the always-on relay persists a compact capsule, the Mac observes and restores desktop state, and the browser reattaches private tabs.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to parse the spoken save/resume intent and answer the immediate acknowledgment. Use a cheaper background model to compress the snapshot into a structured capsule, classify stale/unsafe restoration steps, and generate the short spoken brief. The relay scheduler delivers the reminder without an LLM call unless the capsule needs summarization.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second; capture in 3 seconds. At the scheduled time, deliver the reminder immediately, then restore reversible app/tab state in under 10 seconds and speak a 20–30 second summary. If the Mac or browser is offline, retain the reminder and report the missing surface rather than silently pretending to restore it.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.01 per save/resume, dominated by one small background summarization call; scheduled reminders and deterministic state capture cost no model tokens. A long or noisy snapshot should be truncated before model use.
args.security_concerns: Capsules can contain private URLs, window titles, document names, and snippets from logged-in tabs. Store only an owner-selected allowlist (active app, tab titles/URLs, file path, explicit note), redact page bodies and secrets by default, encrypt at rest, attach an expiry, and show provenance on the Mac. Never replay clicks, submits, sends, purchases, or destructive actions during restore; reopen/read only and ask the owner separately. The pendant should support a physical privacy cancel before saving a sensitive capsule.
missing: A durable resume-capsule schema with redaction, sensitivity, expiry, and provenance fields
A trigger that combines a one-shot schedule with Mac-return/foreground-online presence
Read-only capture of active window, caret/selection, workspace, and authenticated browser tab metadata in one atomic snapshot
Browser session/tab reattachment by stable session and tab identifiers, with stale-tab detection
A deterministic restore plan that opens apps/files/URLs but never performs consequential UI mutations
A pendant delivery path for capsule reminder plus a concise audio summary and a dashboard listing/expiry control

args.user_asks: “Protect my focus: interrupt me on the pendant only for something genuinely urgent; queue everything else and give me one concise catch-up when I’m free.”
args.why_useful: The system can already produce briefs, watch pages, and finish Mac jobs, but it lacks a shared attention policy. Today each surface can alert independently, causing duplicate or badly timed interruptions. This capability turns the pendant into one attention gate: browser changes, mail/calendar signals, and Mac job receipts are deduplicated, ranked against the owner's current focus and calendar, then either delivered now or batched for a quiet window.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic rules for urgency, duplicate suppression, quiet hours, and calendar conflict. Use the cheaper background model to rank ambiguous changes and write the batch digest. Reserve realtime for an explicit spoken override such as “what am I missing?” or “interrupt me now.”
args.latency_budget: Ingest events within 30 seconds and make the interrupt/batch decision in under 2 seconds without an LLM. Urgent delivery should reach the pendant within 5 seconds. A batched digest can be generated at the next quiet window in under 30 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for rule-based event routing; roughly $0.002–$0.02 per digest depending on queued item count. Cost is dominated by one compact summarization call, not by every event.
args.security_concerns: The policy engine sees sensitive mail subjects, private browser changes, calendar titles, and Mac job details. Keep raw content on the originating surface, pass only minimal typed event facts to the relay, encrypt queues, set per-source sensitivity and retention, and make high-sensitivity events opt-in. Never infer urgency from message content without retaining source/provenance. A physical pendant gesture must pause all delivery immediately; dashboard must expose why each item was interrupted or deferred.
missing: A shared attention-policy object with urgency thresholds, source sensitivity, quiet windows, batching limits, and a physical pause state
An event envelope and idempotent deduplication key shared by browser watches, Mac receipts, calendar/mail readers, and relay jobs
A relay-side policy evaluator that can fan out one event to pendant audio/haptics, Mac notification, or a deferred queue
A cross-surface urgency classifier with provenance and an explainable 'why now' result
A durable queue with expiry and a one-tap spoken review/acknowledge flow
Dashboard controls for previewing, editing, and temporarily overriding the policy

args.change: Add a cross-surface causal event ledger. Every spoken request, relay event, browser command, Mac job, and pendant delivery receives a correlation ID, parent ID, origin surface, intended effect, sensitivity, and terminal outcome. The relay maintains a lease per correlation ID so reconnects cannot duplicate a reminder or action; Mac and browser receipts append typed evidence, and the pendant can ask 'what happened to that?' and get the same timeline. Expire abandoned leases and expose a compact redacted timeline in the dashboard.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets one trustworthy answer about whether a request was heard, queued, acted on, or failed, instead of duplicate Mac actions, repeated browser submissions, or a pendant saying 'done' when a surface was offline. It also makes recovery after Wi‑Fi loss understandable without exposing raw private content.
args.effort: Medium-high: define the event/receipt schema, add correlation propagation to relay, browser and Mac adapters, persist an append-only or compacted ledger, and add reconciliation tests for retries and reconnects.
args.risk: A schema or clock mismatch could make work appear stuck or incorrectly completed. Recover by treating terminal receipts as immutable, using monotonic sequence numbers per job, and providing a replay/reconcile worker. Never infer success from a timeout.
args.cost_impact: Small D1/R2 storage and negligible compute; compact old entries and retain only hashes/metadata by default. One additional receipt write per cross-surface step; no model cost.
args.latency_impact: Usually under 20 ms per event write; reconciliation is asynchronous. A first response can be acknowledged before the ledger is fully compacted.
args.security_impact: The ledger is a sensitive activity trail. Store redacted metadata by default, encrypt it, scope reads to the owner/session, and hash or omit URLs, snippets, file names, and message contents unless explicitly requested. Correlation IDs must be unguessable.

When browser/status reports offline or a command exceeds its deadline, stop issuing retries, atomically mark the command blocked_on_surface with the last heartbeat and reason, and expose a single resumable queue entry. The owner gets one honest message—browser unavailable, N items held—and automatic safe recovery when the extension returns.
args.effort: Medium: implement heartbeat-aware queue state transitions, deadlines, deduplication, typed read/write replay rules, and a small reconciliation worker plus tests for disconnect/reconnect and stale tabs.
args.risk: A false offline signal could delay a harmless read, or a tab may change between disconnect and reconnect. Recover by expiring leases, rechecking URL/title/session IDs, and requiring a fresh plan for any mutation. Keep held commands inspectable and cancellable.
args.cost_impact: Negligible model cost; a few D1/local queue writes and one heartbeat check per interval. Reduces wasted browser action retries and their associated latency.
args.latency_impact: Failures become fast (seconds rather than 45-second timeouts); safe reads resume within one heartbeat plus validation. Writes never replay automatically.
args.security_impact: Do not retain page bodies in the held queue. Store only command type, redacted session/tab identifiers, deadline, and reason. Encrypt queue records and ensure stale authenticated commands cannot replay against a different tab.

args.user_asks: “Use what I’m looking at on my Mac: read the selected text or page, answer my question about it on the pendant, and—when I say so—put the result back into the right document or browser field.”
args.why_useful: Today the owner must manually copy context from the Mac into the pendant conversation and then manually carry the answer back. This would make the wearable a hands-free companion to the exact desktop focus: a selected paragraph, spreadsheet cell, document, or authenticated page. It is not a generic Mac command or a browser watcher; it is a secure, ephemeral semantic bridge from current desktop context to pendant conversation and back.
args.model_tier: Use a small background/text model for extraction cleanup and question answering; use realtime only for the live spoken exchange.
