args.body: I proposed USB-tethered button context, focus session, and hardware test. What cross-surface capability gap do you see that isn't in backlog?

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

transcript.text:
Round 160 produced three new proposals:

1. **USB-tethered one-button context**
   - Press the pendant button while connected to the Mac.
   - Mac reads the foreground app, active Safari tab, and relevant calendar context.
   - Relay returns a concise spoken “what am I looking at / what next?” response.
   - Designed to work immediately without LTE registration.

2. **“Start a focused work session”**
   - The pendant supplies the trigger.
   - Mac and browser identify the current task.
   - The system creates a bounded workspace: note, checklist, and only the necessary URLs.
   - No form submissions, messages, or other irreversible actions.

3. **“Test my pendant and audio bridge”**
   - Deterministically exercises the nRF9160 button/LED, both serial links, reconnect behavior, and a synthetic ESP32 audio fixture.
   - Does not open the microphone or upload captured audio.
   - Produces per-component receipts and a clear diagnosis.

I also proposed the **USB-tether coordinator** needed to make these real: a Mac service that owns both serial devices, assigns monotonic event IDs, reconnects safely, and publishes authenticated events to the relay without duplicate actions.

What is still needed:

- A documented serial event/command protocol for the nRF9160 and ESP32.
- A Mac serial listener and response/audio framing path.
- A relay endpoint for authenticated tethered-device events.
- A deterministic synthetic audio test fixture.
- A small dashboard view for tethered status and hardware-test history.
- The existing Mac tools/routes are sufficient for context collection and action execution; the missing work is the physical-device-to-relay wiring between them.

args.user_asks: “Use my pendant as a physical presence key: when it is with me, put my Mac into my private workspace, and when it leaves, lock or redact sensitive views.”
args.why_useful: The pendant would provide a physical, non-password presence signal that coordinates the worn device and Mac. It could automatically switch between a private work profile and a safe-away profile, reducing accidental exposure when the owner walks away from the desk. This is materially different from ordinary Mac automation because presence is supplied by the worn hardware.
args.model_tier: No model required for presence detection or policy execution; use a cheap background model only to explain state changes.
args.latency_budget: Presence transitions should be detected within 2–5 seconds; workspace changes should complete within another 2 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero API cost. Hardware/firmware integration and reliable presence detection dominate.
args.security_concerns: A stolen or spoofed pendant must not grant unrestricted access. Use a locally paired cryptographic identity, short-range USB/BLE proof, explicit safe profiles, and never transmit private workspace contents to the relay. Locking behavior must fail closed.
missing: A cryptographic device-identity and pairing protocol
A presence signal independent of an easily copied serial string
A Mac profile broker that can lock, hide, or restore approved applications and windows
Owner-configurable safe/private workspace policies

args.user_asks: “When I leave my Mac mid-task, preserve the exact state of my work and restore it when I return with the pendant.”
args.why_useful: The owner would not have to remember which windows, browser tabs, files, drafts, and next action were active. The pendant’s departure/return events would delimit a real work interval, while the Mac records a compact, privacy-filtered state capsule and reconstructs the workspace on return. This is a physical continuity primitive, not another scheduled briefing.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic local state capture first; use a cheaper background model to summarize the next action and resolve ambiguous window labels. Realtime is unnecessary.
args.latency_budget: Capture under 3 seconds on departure; restore a first useful workspace within 5 seconds of return.
args.cost_estimate: A few cents only when semantic summarization is needed; local window/tab/file metadata is the dominant implementation work.
args.security_concerns: State capsules may contain sensitive URLs, filenames, or draft text. Keep raw state on the Mac, encrypt any relay copy, apply per-app exclusions, and offer a hardware long-press to cancel capture.
missing: Reliable pendant departure/return detection
Read-only window and document-state capture beyond current app/tab metadata
A reversible workspace snapshot/restore engine for Mac and Safari
Encrypted local capsule storage with retention controls

args.user_asks: “If my Mac loses the network while I’m wearing the pendant, keep a local queue of tiny commands and execute them when the link returns, telling me which ones actually happened.”
args.why_useful: The owner would get dependable command continuity across a real connectivity gap: simple approved local actions such as opening a note, creating a reminder, or saving a capture can be accepted over the tether and persisted locally, then reconciled after reconnection. The important benefit is truthful completion status rather than silently losing a spoken request.
args.model_tier: No realtime model is needed for queueing or reconciliation; use the realtime tier only to parse an ambiguous spoken command before enqueueing, and a cheaper model for post hoc summaries.
args.latency_budget: A local acknowledgement within 500 ms; replay starts immediately on reconnection and reports each receipt.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost for deterministic commands; storage and reconciliation logic dominate.
args.security_concerns: Only commands with an explicit idempotency key and bounded local effect should survive offline. Never queue sends, purchases, deletions, or browser submissions. Encrypt queued payloads and expire them by policy.
missing: A pendant-to-Mac offline command envelope
A durable, idempotent local queue with replay receipts
A connectivity detector spanning serial, relay, and browser links
A command allowlist and conflict-resolution policy

args.user_asks: Use my pendant as a physical handoff key: when I say “approve this” and hold its button, authorize exactly the prepared browser or Mac transaction that is shown in the receipt, then tell me what changed.
args.why_useful: It turns the wearable into a trustworthy, eyes-free confirmation device for work prepared across private browser tabs and Mac apps. The relay can keep working while the owner is away; only the pendant's deliberate gesture releases the one exact mutation, with no broad approval prompt or accidental replay.
args.model_tier: Realtime for parsing the spoken approval and matching it to the pending transaction; background model for preparing and validating the transaction and generating the receipt.
args.latency_budget: Preparation may take seconds in the background; approval-to-action should be under 2 seconds and the pendant should speak a one-sentence receipt.
args.cost_estimate: Low per approval: one short realtime turn plus browser/Mac execution; browser and Mac calls dominate latency, not tokens.
args.security_concerns: The relay must bind a nonce to exact action list, tab/session, before-state hashes, expiry, and device identity; never accept a generic “approve.” Do not transmit page secrets to the pendant; require a fresh physical gesture and report before/after evidence. Sending mail, deletion, and purchases remain explicitly confirmable transactions.
missing: USB-serial pendant challenge/response and button gesture firmware
short-lived transaction approval endpoint in relay
browser/Mac executor support for nonce-bound prepared transactions
receipt UI/audio that shows the exact pending mutation

args.user_asks: Keep me in the right attention mode automatically: when Calendar says I’m in a meeting or my Mac is presenting, silence routine pendant replies and queue them; break through only for a genuinely urgent item, then give me the queued one-sentence digest when I’m free.
args.why_useful: The system can finally be present without being disruptive. It combines calendar truth, live Mac foreground/presentation state, browser urgency, and the pendant's output path—something none of those surfaces can determine alone.
args.model_tier: Cheap background classifier for urgency and queue compression; realtime only for the eventual spoken digest or an owner interruption request.
args.latency_budget: State changes should propagate within 5 seconds; routine items wait silently, urgent escalation should speak within 2 seconds once classified.
args.cost_estimate: Very low: event-driven state checks and one batched summary; no model call for ordinary suppressed events, cheap model only when ranking a batch.
args.security_concerns: Calendar titles, browser snippets, and foreground-app names are sensitive; keep raw data on the Mac/relay, send only urgency labels and short redacted summaries to the pendant. Never infer emergency from arbitrary page text without a clear policy and audit trail.
missing: Mac presentation/meeting-state detector without relying on Screen Recording permission

args.why_useful: This is usable today while the nRF9160 is USB-attached but unregistered: the wearable remains an interface instead of becoming dead hardware whenever cellular is unavailable. It combines the pendant's physical button/audio, the ESP32 bridge, Mac serial, local agent, and later relay reconciliation.
args.model_tier: Local/cheap model for short offline commands and deterministic local intents; realtime model only after connectivity returns for complex interpretation or reconciliation.
args.latency_budget: Button-to-local acknowledgement under 500 ms; simple Mac result under 5 seconds. Unsynced events persist until connectivity returns, then reconcile in the background.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero while offline for deterministic commands; later sync costs a small batch request. USB serial and audio bridge dominate engineering, not API spend.
args.security_concerns: Treat USB as an explicitly paired local link, not an open serial console. Encrypt or authenticate queued transcripts and receipts, cap offline command scope, and prevent replay with monotonic counters. Never queue destructive actions for later execution; queue only drafts and read results.

args.user_asks: When I plug my pendant into another trusted Mac, restore my work exactly where I left off: reopen the right apps and files, reattach my browser workspaces without exposing passwords, and show pending jobs and drafts so I can continue immediately.
args.why_useful: The pendant becomes a portable continuity anchor rather than a single-computer accessory. A lost, replaced, or borrowed Mac would not strand the owner's active work, while browser secrets remain in the browser's own authenticated profile instead of being copied into the cloud or pendant.
args.model_tier: Background/cheap model to summarize and rank resumable work; deterministic state capture and restoration should not spend realtime-model tokens. Realtime is only needed if the owner asks for a spoken explanation of conflicts.
args.latency_budget: Capture on detach or explicit command within 10 seconds; restoration should show a usable workspace within 30 seconds, with browser tabs reattached opportunistically.
args.cost_estimate: Low API cost; storage and local state transfer dominate. A compact manifest is cheap, while optional summaries are a small background-model call.
args.security_concerns: The pendant must hold only a hardware-backed device key, never passwords or raw session cookies. Relay stores encrypted, per-device workspace manifests with expiry and revocation. A new Mac must be explicitly paired; browser extension proves tab ownership locally. Do not restore destructive queued actions automatically—restore them as drafts with receipts.

Mac capture/restore adapters for apps and files
Browser extension reattachment protocol that preserves authenticated sessions without exporting credentials

transcript.text:
Recorded a new capability:

**Portable work continuity via the pendant** — plugging the pendant into another trusted Mac restores the owner’s active apps, files, browser workspaces, drafts, and pending jobs without exporting passwords or session cookies.

Required changes:

- Hardware-backed pendant identity and pairing/revocation over USB serial.
- Encrypted relay-stored workspace manifests.
- Mac adapters to capture and restore app/file state.
- Browser-extension reattachment that preserves authenticated sessions locally.
- Conflict handling when multiple Macs diverge.
- Draft-only restoration for potentially destructive pending actions.

args.user_asks: When I tap the pendant twice, save a private, time-stamped thought with the Mac's current app and open browser context, acknowledge it on the pendant, and let me ask for the unsorted captures later—even if LTE is unavailable.
args.why_useful: A thought can be safely captured in the moment without opening a phone or losing what the owner was looking at. The USB-attached pendant is usable today despite the relay being offline, and the context makes each fragment recoverable rather than an orphaned note.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the spoken acknowledgement; deterministic local code records and indexes the event, while a cheaper background model clusters or summarizes captures on request.
args.latency_budget: LED/serial acknowledgement under 150 ms; local capture under 1 s; semantic grouping can take seconds in the background.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible per capture when local; roughly $0.001–$0.01 for optional background grouping depending on batch size. The dominant cost is model summarization, not serial or Mac inspection.
args.security_concerns: Context may include private tab titles and the foreground app. Keep raw context on the Mac by default, redact secrets before relay upload, and require an explicit request to export or summarize remotely. Never transmit the known secret capture fields.
missing: A Mac USB-serial pendant gateway that maps button/serial frames to authenticated /capture records
A small local capture store with ordering, deduplication, and replay/export
Firmware event frames and an acknowledgement command over /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658*
A background capture-clustering routine distinct from the existing generic capture endpoint

args.user_asks: Start a focus session from the pendant: mute distracting Mac notifications, route the bridge audio to my headphones, show the session end time, and when I tap again restore everything and turn the session's spoken action items into reminders.
args.why_useful: The owner can enter and leave deep work without touching the Mac, while the same physical gesture brackets the work period. It joins wearable intent, Mac state, audio hardware, and later reminder creation instead of treating focus mode as a desktop-only toggle.
args.model_tier: Realtime handles only the short start/stop confirmation; local scripts and a deterministic state machine control Focus/audio, and a cheaper background model extracts action items from the session transcript.
args.latency_budget: Start/stop acknowledgement under 500 ms; notification and audio changes under 2 s; action-item extraction after the session may take 10–30 s.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for state transitions; approximately $0.01–$0.05 per session for transcript/action-item extraction. Audio transport and Apple Shortcuts dominate engineering complexity, not API spend.

args.user_asks: Before speaking or displaying anything sensitive, ask the Mac what context I am in—current meeting, foreground app, and active browser account—and have the pendant give me a discreet safe/unsafe signal; if unsafe, defer the answer into a private queue instead.
args.why_useful: Today the system can retrieve private information but cannot reliably know whether it is safe to reveal it at this exact moment. This prevents an embarrassing spoken disclosure in a meeting or in front of another person without requiring the owner to remember a manual privacy command.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic context and account classification first; use realtime only when the owner asks an ambiguous safety question. No model is needed for ordinary allow/defer decisions.
args.latency_budget: Safety verdict under 300 ms from local context; deferred response available within 2 s after the context becomes private.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for local checks; occasional realtime clarification costs less than a cent. The expensive part is integrating reliable context signals, not inference.
args.security_concerns: The safety service itself handles sensitive meeting and account metadata. Keep it local, expose only a boolean plus reason category to the relay, encrypt the deferred queue, and expire it automatically. A false-safe verdict is the primary hazard, so unknown context must default to defer.

args.change: Add a local USB pendant/ESP32 session supervisor on the Mac: discover /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* and /dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA, attach monotonic session IDs, tail framed UART diagnostics, detect silence/boot loops/audio underruns, and expose a single health event stream to relay and dashboard. On reconnect, send only an idempotent status request (never replay queued browser or voice commands), then publish a spoken/LED-safe 'pendant attached but relay-unregistered' state.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Today the owner cannot tell whether a failure is LTE, relay registration, the USB cable, or the audio bridge. This would make the prototype self-diagnosing at the exact moment it fails and prevent stale commands from unexpectedly running after reconnect.
args.effort: Medium: a Mac launch agent plus two protocol adapters, a small event schema, and relay/dashboard display; firmware needs a read-only diagnostic/status frame if the current UART has none.
args.risk: Serial probing can contend with an active flasher or firmware console; use exclusive-open, bounded reads, and never write except an explicit status opcode. If the supervisor crashes, the devices continue unchanged; disable it with one launch-agent toggle.
args.cost_impact: No meaningful API cost; approximately 20–40 MB resident Mac process and a few KB/day of local logs. Hardware cost $0 using the already connected boards.
args.latency_impact: Health events within 1–2 seconds of cable or firmware failure; no voice-path latency change.
args.security_impact: UART logs may contain transcripts, identifiers, or tokens; redact payload bytes by default, hash device IDs, and keep raw logs local with a short retention window.
depends_on: A framed, read-only diagnostic/status opcode in pendant and ESP32 firmware
A local relay endpoint accepting device-health events
A real implementation of read-only Mac inspection or a dedicated serial supervisor route

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

1. **Task privacy ledger** — show exactly what sources, excerpts, model handoffs, and mutations were used, with verified task-scoped purge.  
   **Needed:** provenance instrumentation across relay, browser, and Mac; encrypted ledger; dashboard and purge endpoint.

2. **Pendant-confirmed action escrow** — prepare an authenticated Mac/browser transaction now, then execute it only after the pendant confirms the exact final details.  
   **Needed:** canonical transaction hashes, device-bound challenge/response, durable expiring escrow, and final precondition checks.

3. **One-button audio/link health check** — identify whether the mic, I2S path, USB, ESP32 Bluetooth bridge, LTE, relay, or Mac is broken without recording or starting a conversation.  
   **Needed:** synthetic firmware diagnostics, ESP32 loopback acknowledgement, relay and Mac probes, and a typed result schema.

args.user_asks: If I walk away or the pendant disconnects while you are working on my Mac, pause safely, remember exactly where you were, and resume automatically when I reconnect—then tell me on the pendant what finished and what still needs me.
args.why_useful: Long Mac/browser tasks stop being fragile when the owner closes the lid, walks out of USB range, or has a transient relay outage. They return to a truthful continuation rather than a half-completed mystery.
args.model_tier: Cheap background model for checkpoint classification and resume validation; realtime only for the short pendant status message.
args.latency_budget: Checkpoint within 2 seconds of disconnect; resume within 10 seconds of reconnect; completion status under 3 seconds after the final action.
args.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per task in background inference; dominant cost is browser/Mac polling and any long-running page work, not model tokens.
args.security_concerns: A disconnect must never be interpreted as permission to continue blindly. Persist only action IDs, completed receipts, and redacted state; revalidate page/session identity after reconnect and stop on changed context. No secrets leave the Mac except through existing authenticated relay paths.
missing: Pendant USB-serial presence/disconnect event and reconnect handshake
Durable checkpoint/resume state machine spanning POST /execute jobs and browser sessions
A Mac bridge watcher that can pause an active job without killing its receipt chain
A bounded resume validator for stale tabs, files, and app state

args.user_asks: Only treat my private Mac and logged-in-browser requests as mine while my paired pendant is physically connected; if it disconnects, freeze new private actions, show me the exact pending plan, and let me resume when it returns.
args.why_useful: The pendant becomes a continuously present, local proof of the owner's intent. A stolen laptop session, unattended browser, or stale relay command cannot silently keep acting after the owner leaves.
args.model_tier: No expensive model for the security decision: firmware/bridge cryptographic verification and deterministic policy. Use a cheap model only to explain a blocked action in plain language.
args.latency_budget: Presence loss detected and private dispatch frozen in under 500 ms; reconnect attestation under 2 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible inference cost; small engineering cost for key provisioning, serial framing, and durable key rotation.
args.security_concerns: Use a per-device asymmetric key and nonce challenge, never a reusable bearer token or audio phrase. This is a presence control, not a human confirmation gate.

args.change: Replace the prototype-only presence assumption with a production pendant security path: add a small secure element (for example, an ATECC608-class device) on I2C, provision a non-exportable device key at manufacture, and expose nonce-signing to the nRF9160 firmware over a narrow command. The Mac bridge challenges it over the existing USB serial connection before dispatching private browser/Mac work.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner's worn device can prove that it is physically present without putting a reusable secret in the laptop, relay, or firmware image. Losing an unlocked Mac or a copied session no longer leaves private automation running unattended.
args.effort: Medium hardware spin plus firmware driver, manufacturing provisioning, bridge attestation protocol, and revocation/re-pair UX. Prototype first with the nRF9160's protected key storage, then validate the secure element before productizing.
args.risk: A failed challenge could strand private automation; recover with an explicit re-pair flow and public/read-only fallback. Physical extraction, supply-chain provisioning mistakes, and USB impersonation remain threats and need manufacturing tests.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $0.50–$2 BOM increase in volume, negligible steady-state power, plus one I2C peripheral and a few KB of firmware/driver space.
args.latency_impact: Approximately 50–300 ms per private-job session attestation; cache only a short-lived bridge session, not a permanent authorization.
args.security_impact: Material improvement: private keys never leave the secure element. Requires key revocation, per-owner pairing records, nonce freshness, and clear handling when the pendant is absent.
depends_on: Pendant firmware nonce-signing command
Mac USB-serial presence daemon on /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658*
Private/public job labeling in the Mac dispatch path
Pairing and revocation storage in the relay

args.user_asks: When I put the pendant back on after being away, tell me what changed on my Mac and in my open private browser sessions while I was gone—new files, app changes, page changes, and important notifications—then offer a compact list of things I should act on.
args.why_useful: The owner gets a reliable re-entry brief instead of reopening every app and trying to remember where they left off. It turns the physical pendant's absence and return into a useful boundary for personal continuity without recording a microphone.
args.model_tier: Cheap background model compares normalized event snapshots and ranks changes; realtime is used only to read the final brief aloud when the pendant reconnects.
args.latency_budget: Capture a baseline within 10 seconds of departure, detect return within 2 seconds, and produce the first brief within 20 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per return brief; local snapshotting is the dominant work and model cost scales with the number of changed items.
args.security_concerns: Snapshots remain on the Mac by default and contain hashes, app/page identifiers, and redacted notification text rather than full content. Private browser data is scoped to explicitly paired sessions. The owner can exclude directories, apps, and sites; never infer that absence means deletion.
missing: A Mac-side append-only, privacy-filtered activity journal for app, file, notification, and browser-session changes
Pendant presence transition events over the USB serial link and a departure/return session identifier
Browser bridge support for normalized before/after page fingerprints on already-open authenticated tabs
A relay endpoint that asks the Mac for a bounded delta and sends a short result to the pendant

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities the owner cannot have today:

1. **Return-from-away delta brief** — detect what changed on the Mac and in private browser sessions while the pendant was absent, then summarize actionable changes on reconnect.
2. **Portable workspace checkpoints** — save and later restore an exact app/file/browser working set from a pendant gesture, with conflict-safe previews.
3. **Cross-source draft reconciliation** — compare project drafts across Mail, Notes, local files, and authenticated browser tabs, then prepare cited conflict reports and synchronized edits for review.

They require pendant presence events, Mac activity/workspace journaling, browser state fingerprints, bounded cross-source search, provenance-aware diffs, and reviewable patch/restore protocols.

result.board: Adafruit HUZZAH32 (ESP32 classic), 240 MHz dual core, 320 kB DRAM
result.role: Receives I2S from the pendant, resamples 31250 -> 44100 with a polyphase FIR, and is an A2DP SOURCE to Bluetooth headphones
result.limit: A2DP source is SBC-only and hard-locked to 44.1 kHz stereo in the precompiled bluedroid. RAM is tight: a 44 kB buffer once starved the Bluetooth stack into silence.

result.button: ONE user button, devicetree alias sw0. Press starts a conversation; second press ends it. It is also pokable over J-Link for testing.
result.led: ONE LED, alias led0. Currently signals recording, stays solid while agent audio is buffered, and flashes error codes.
result.buses: GPIO, I2C, SPI and I2S all enabled (prj.conf). I2C and SPI are FREE — nothing is attached to them today.

transcript.text:
This round produced three new cross-surface capabilities and three implementation changes:

1. **Tethered pendant command loop** — button and microphone → Mac planner/browser → verified desktop action → spoken confirmation through the ESP32 bridge, even without LTE.
2. **Physical whole-system health check** — plugging in the pendant triggers checks of USB, audio, relay, browser, permissions, and receipt verification, with a concise spoken diagnosis.
3. **Tap-bounded meeting capsule** — first tap starts a private context capture from Calendar, Mail, and selected Safari tabs; second tap produces a sourced spoken debrief without sending anything.

The highest-value implementation change is a **USB pendant session daemon**. The boards are physically connected now, but no service currently discovers the serial devices, frames button/audio packets, reconnects safely, or correlates them with `/plan`, `/execute`, and job receipts.

I also proposed:

- A cross-surface **truth receipt** that distinguishes planned, executed, verified, and failed actions. This matters because Accessibility is currently false and UI actions may report success while doing nothing.
- A firmware **button/LED protocol** for listening, queued, verified, failed, disconnected, and cancel states.

What I still need:

- A documented serial framing and handshake protocol for the nRF9160 and ESP32.
- A local serial daemon/launchd service.
- A reliable audio return path from Mac/relay through the ESP32.
- Stable correlation IDs across serial, relay, planner, executor, and browser bridge.
- Read-only post-action verification probes.
- Actual implementations for the newly granted `mac_readonly_inspect` schema; it currently returns “granted a schema but has no implementation.”
- The owner’s manual Accessibility and Screen Recording grants remain unavailable; I will not re-request them.

This would let the owner keep maximum automation for ordinary work while reserving a physical, unmistakable gesture for purchases, messages, account changes, and other identity-bearing actions.

args.security_concerns: The private key must remain on-device and never be sent to the relay. Prevent replay with nonce, expiry, job binding, and cancellation on unplug. Never treat a spoken 'yes' alone as authorization for an identity-bearing action.

args.subject: Cross-device action gap
args.body: I see a gap: a USB-attached pendant should provide a local voice/button control plane when LTE is absent, with relay session continuity and Mac/browser execution. Also physical button-triggered post-action undo/receipt. Are these already covered in your action plans?

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

args.user_asks: When my pendant is plugged into my Mac, make it a local voice console automatically: carry my live conversation over USB despite no LTE registration, use the Mac's network for the relay, and resume on LTE later without losing context.
args.why_useful: The pendant is physically wearable and testable now but currently becomes useless when its modem is unregistered or LTE is weak. This makes voice control reliable at a desk and turns the Mac-attached prototype into a real daily fallback, with no microphone opened on the Mac.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the live turn; a cheap background worker maintains session/checkpoint reconciliation.
args.latency_budget: Under 250 ms added one-way over USB; reconnect and session reconciliation under 2 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost beyond the existing live turn; engineering is a USB serial audio/WebSocket tunnel and reconnect state machine.
args.security_concerns: USB audio and control frames must be authenticated and bound to the local pendant identity; never expose the serial bridge beyond localhost. Persist only opaque session checkpoints, not raw audio.
missing: Pendant USB serial audio/control framing and host-side serial daemon
Relay transport mode that accepts a Mac-local pendant tunnel and migrates the same session between USB and LTE
A small Mac launch agent to discover /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* and bridge frames

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.
result.builtFrom: All 5 pieces you named already exist: /pipeline/events, /pipeline/audio, /pipeline/:pipelineid/audio/:direction, /plan, /execute. So this is connective work rather than a new capability — say what is missing BETWEEN them, or whether it is already reachable today and nobody has wired it up.

args.user_asks: I’m starting a meeting—press the pendant button once to put my Mac in a quiet mode, remember what I was doing, and press it again afterward to restore everything and tell me what I missed.
args.why_useful: A physical, glance-free gesture is faster and safer than hunting through macOS controls while joining a meeting. The Mac can suppress distractions, the browser can preserve the active work context, and the pendant can announce the restoration and a short missed-item digest afterward.
args.model_tier: Realtime handles the two short spoken confirmations; background model summarizes accumulated notifications and calendar/mail changes after the meeting.
args.latency_budget: Quiet mode within 1 second of the button event; restoration within 2 seconds; digest within 30 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: One cheap background summarization call per meeting; no model call for the deterministic mode toggle.
args.security_concerns: Do not read notification contents aloud in public by default; store a bounded, encrypted meeting capsule locally and expire it after 24 hours. The second press must restore only state this routine changed.
missing: Pendant firmware button event exposed over the active USB/LTE control channel
Mac state snapshot/restore for focus mode, volume, foreground app, and browser tab set
A notification/calendar delta collector and meeting-capsule store
Relay routine that correlates start/end presses and sends a compact spoken result

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.
result.builtFrom: All 7 pieces you named already exist: /pipeline/events, /execute, /browser/status, /browser/sessions, /machine-context, /machine-context/refresh. So this is connective work rather than a new capability — say what is missing BETWEEN them, or whether it is already reachable today and nobody has wired it up.

args.user_asks: If I tap the pendant twice within 10 seconds after you change something on my Mac, undo the last reversible change and tell me exactly what was restored.
args.why_useful: The owner can recover from an accidental open, move, volume change, or reversible edit without finding the Mac window or remembering a command. It gives the wearable a concrete safety affordance for the system’s otherwise maximum-control automation.
args.model_tier: No expensive reasoning for the gesture; deterministic receipt lookup and undo, with realtime only for the brief spoken confirmation.
args.latency_budget: Recognize the double tap in 300 ms and complete a supported undo within 2 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: No per-use model cost; one small persistent action receipt per mutation and a bounded undo record.
args.security_concerns: Only undo actions explicitly marked reversible by the executor; never undo sends, deletes, purchases, or browser submissions. Require a fresh receipt ID and expire the gesture window to prevent replay.
missing: Pendant double-tap event and debounce firmware
Action receipts need a reversible flag plus inverse payload, not just human-readable logs
